followUp.works: Right, and lesson 11 is where that came from. If it went the other way just now, that is the round to watch for.
followUp.breaks: That is the one this band works hardest to replace, and it comes back the moment you stop thinking about it.

beats.heading: This is what a round finds
beats.body: Not whether you know the word. Whether the English shape came back while you were busy answering.

wrong.en: the shape English gave you

beats.coach: One question, from one lesson, and it names the lesson. Twenty-nine rounds of that is what this is.

beats.text: One round per lesson, five questions each. The round says which lesson it came from, on purpose, because the point is to find the gap rather than to hide it.

sections.title: What This Is
sections.say: Three things, and the third one is a separate sitting.

goals.s: Five questions each, in the order the band taught them. A round is named for its lesson, so a low score points somewhere specific.

goals.t: A drill when a round goes badly
goals.s: Score under sixty on a round and a short drill runs before the next one starts, while the mistake is still live rather than at the very end.
Sixty mixed questions in a second sitting, with nothing naming a lesson and no explanations until you finish. A wrong answer names the half hour to sit again.

sections.title: Before You Start
sections.say: A hundred and forty-five questions. Stop wherever you like.
sections.body: Nothing here is new. Every question quotes a lesson you have already sat. A wrong answer names the half hour to sit again.

sections.title: Lesson By Lesson
sections.say: Twenty-nine rounds. Each one says which lesson it is testing.

rounds.label: Lesson 1 · Greetings
rounds.say: Greetings. Five questions, and the register matters as much as the word.

questions.q: You walk into a bakery at ten in the morning. What comes out of your mouth first?
questions.why: Bonjour is the price of entry. Salut is for people you tutoie, bonne journée is said leaving, and allô exists only on the phone. Lesson 1.

questions.q: Write the French a man says for: Pleased to meet you
questions.why: Enchanté, with a second e as enchantée if you are a woman. Lesson 1.

questions.q: A learner leaves a dinner party at eleven at night and says « Bonne nuit ». Fix it.
questions.why: Bonne nuit is for sleep, and it tells the room you are going to bed. Leaving after dark takes bonne soirée. Lesson 1.

questions.q: Listen. Which form did you hear?
questions.why: Te against vous is one syllable and it is the whole difference between them. Lesson 1.

questions.q: Which is the everyday answer to merci?
questions.why: De rien is the everyday one. Je vous en prie is its formal twin, bienvenue is welcome to a place, and pardon is an apology. Lesson 1.

rounds.label: Lesson 2 · Numbers 1 to 20
rounds.say: One to twenty. The endings move, and that is the lesson.

questions.q: Write the French for: sixteen
questions.why: seize. There is nothing of six in it, which is exactly why it gets heard as six. Lesson 2.

questions.q: Listen. Which number is it?
questions.why: quinze ends on a z and cinq ends on a k. They share a vowel, so the ending is the only thing separating five from fifteen. Lesson 2.

questions.q: A learner asks for « un baguette » at the counter. Fix it.
questions.why: un is the only number with a gender, and baguette is feminine. Lesson 2.

questions.q: How is « dix » said in « dix minutes »?
opts: DEE, with no s at all
questions.why: Alone it is DEES, before a consonant the s vanishes, before a vowel it is a z. minutes starts with a consonant. Lesson 2.

questions.q: Say it: three
questions.why: trois. Saying a number is a different test from recognising one, and it is the half most learners skip. Lesson 2.

rounds.label: Lesson 3 · Numbers 21 to 100
rounds.say: Twenty-one to a hundred. Learn the shape, not the sum.

questions.q: Write the French for: 71
questions.why: soixante et onze. The et rule covers 21, 31, 41, 51, 61 and 71 only, and those six take no hyphens. Lesson 3.

questions.q: Which is 92?
questions.why: quatre-vingt-douze. The s comes off quatre-vingts the moment anything follows it, and nonante is Belgian and Swiss rather than France French. Lesson 3.

questions.q: A learner writes eighty-one as « quatre-vingts-un ». Fix it.
questions.why: quatre-vingt-un. quatre-vingts keeps its s only when nothing follows. Lesson 3.

questions.q: Listen. Which number is it?
questions.why: soixante-seize is 76, sixty and sixteen. The trap is hearing the seize as six. Lesson 3.

questions.q: Which of these takes NO et and NO s?
questions.why: quatre-vingt-onze. 91 never takes et, and the s is gone because onze follows. 71 takes et, 80 alone keeps its s, and 21 takes et. Lesson 3.

rounds.label: Lesson 4 · Large numbers
rounds.say: cent and mille are adjectives. million is a noun.

questions.q: Write the French for: 200
questions.why: deux cents. cent is multiplied and nothing follows it, so it takes the s. Lesson 4.

questions.q: Which is 330?
questions.why: trois cent trente. cent is multiplied, but trente follows it, so the s comes straight off. Lesson 4.

questions.q: A learner writes two thousand as « deux milles ». Fix it.
questions.why: deux mille. mille never takes an s in any position. The s was carried over from cents, where it is real. Lesson 4.

questions.q: A learner says « huit millions visiteurs ». What is missing?
questions.why: huit millions de visiteurs. million is a noun, so it reaches its noun through de, and the s on millions is unconditional. Lesson 4.

questions.q: A French price tag reads 124,80 €. How much is it?
questions.why: The comma is the decimal point in French and the space is the thousands separator, so 124,80 € is a hundred and twenty-four euros eighty. Lesson 4.

rounds.label: Lesson 5 · Noun gender
rounds.say: Gender. Learn the article, not the noun.

questions.q: A noun ends in -tion. Which article does it almost certainly take?
questions.why: une. Thirty-six -tion nouns in the corpus and every one of them is feminine: la direction, la natation, la destination. Lesson 5.

questions.q: Write the article that goes with: bureau
questions.why: le bureau. The -eau ending is masculine ninety-two percent of the time, and l'eau and la peau are the two that break it. Lesson 5.

questions.q: A learner reasons: « livre ends in e, so it is feminine ». What is wrong?
opts: A final e is a lean, not a rule, and le livre is masculine
livre is feminine, the learner is right
Only nouns ending in -e take une
questions.why: A final e is worth a lean and nothing more. le livre is the book and la livre is the pound in weight, so the same spelling runs both ways. Lesson 5.

questions.q: A learner learns the word « armoire » from a card, with no article. Fix the habit.
questions.why: une armoire. Storing the bare noun stores half the word, and the half you dropped is the half you need to speak. Lesson 5.

questions.q: Which of these endings takes une?
questions.why: -ure is feminine: la confiture, la peinture, la ceinture. The other three are masculine endings. Lesson 5.

rounds.label: Lesson 6 · The definite articles
rounds.say: le, la, l and les. When English says nothing, French says le.

questions.q: Complete: « J'aime ___ café. » (I like coffee, as a thing in general)
questions.why: J'aime le café. English drops the article on a whole category and French never does. Lesson 6.

questions.q: Write the definite article for: eau
questions.why: l'eau. Both le and la elide to l' before a vowel sound, which is why the apostrophe hides the gender. Lesson 6.

questions.q: Which of these takes le rather than l'?
questions.why: le hibou. Its h is aspirated so it behaves like a consonant, along with le hamster, le homard and le héros. The other three have an h muet. Lesson 6.

questions.q: A learner writes « les ami ». Fix it.
questions.why: les amis. les is the plural article, so the noun has to be plural too. Lesson 6.

questions.q: Listen. Which did you hear?
questions.why: les enfants, with a z linking into the vowel. The singular would be l'enfant with no z at all. Lesson 6.

rounds.label: Lesson 7 · The indefinite articles
rounds.say: un, une, des. Un introduces it. Le assumes you already know it.

questions.q: Write the French for: I am a teacher
questions.why: Je suis professeur. Nothing at all after être in front of a job. The un is the single most common thing added here. Lesson 7.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.why: C'est un professeur. After c'est the article comes back, and it is the one place it does. After être it never appears. Lesson 7.

questions.q: A learner says « J'achète pommes ». Fix it.
questions.why: J'achète des pommes. French has no bare plural noun, so the slot des fills is never left empty. Lesson 7.

questions.q: Turn « J'ai une voiture » negative.
questions.why: Je n'ai pas de voiture. Under a negative un, une and des all collapse to de. Lesson 7.

questions.q: Why does « Je n'aime pas le café » keep its le?
opts: Because le, la and les do not move under a negative
It is wrong, it should be de
questions.why: The definite articles do not move under a negative. Only un, une, des and the partitives collapse to de. Lesson 7.

rounds.label: Lesson 8 · The partitive articles
rounds.say: du, de la, de l. Un is one of them. Du is some of it.

questions.q: Write the French for: I eat bread
questions.why: Je mange du pain. Some of it, not one of them and not the whole category. French does not leave that slot empty. Lesson 8.

questions.q: You want coffee, not one cup of coffee. Which do you order?
questions.why: du café. Both un café and du café are correct French and they order different things: one is a cup, the other is coffee. Lesson 8.

questions.q: A learner says « beaucoup du café ». Fix it.
questions.why: beaucoup de café. After a quantity word the partitive flattens to plain de, every time. Lesson 8.

questions.q: Which is right for a bottle of water?
questions.why: une bouteille d'eau. A container behaves like a quantity, so it takes plain de, elided before the vowel. Lesson 8.

questions.q: Turn « Je mange du pain » negative.
accept: Je ne mange pas de pain
questions.answer: Je ne mange pas de pain.
questions.why: Je ne mange pas de pain. du, de la, de l' and des all become de under a negative. Lesson 8.

rounds.label: Lesson 9 · Subject pronouns
rounds.say: Nine pronouns. Six verb forms.

questions.q: Which verb form goes with « on »?
questions.why: On est. on means we and takes the il form, which is the mismatch that catches everyone. Lesson 9.

questions.q: A learner writes « On sommes d'accord ». Fix it.
questions.why: On est d'accord. on takes est however many people it means. Lesson 9.

questions.q: You are writing the closing line of a job application. Which do you use for we?
questions.why: nous. on is the spoken we and it is out of place in careful writing. Both are correct French, and only one is correct there. Lesson 9.

questions.q: A group of four women. Which pronoun?
questions.why: elles, for a group that is all women. One man in the room and it becomes ils. Lesson 9.

questions.q: In « Il pleut », who is il?
questions.why: Nobody. il is the empty subject French puts in front of weather, the clock and il y a, and looking for a person in it is what makes the sentence stall. Lesson 9.

rounds.label: Lesson 10 · The verb être
rounds.say: No pattern. Six forms. Every conversation.

questions.q: Write être for vous
questions.why: vous êtes, said [voo ZET] with a z linking in. It is the one form that looks nothing like the others. Lesson 10.

questions.q: Pointing at a man across the room, you say what?
questions.why: C'est Marc. A name takes c'est, never il est. Pointing is always c'est. Lesson 10.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je suis Français » about their nationality. Fix it.
questions.why: Je suis français, with a small f. As a nationality it is an adjective, and French does not capitalise those. The capital belongs to the noun, un Français. Lesson 10.

questions.q: Which is correct for « They are my parents »?
questions.why: Ce sont mes parents. More than one person turns c'est into ce sont. Lesson 10.

questions.q: Say it: « Je suis architecte. »
questions.why: No article in front of the job, ever, after être. Adding un is the most common error in this lesson. Lesson 10.

rounds.label: Lesson 11 · The verb avoir
rounds.say: French has it. English is it.

questions.q: Write the French for: I am twenty
questions.why: J'ai vingt ans. French HAS its age, and ans is never left off. Je suis vingt ans is the reflex to unlearn. Lesson 11.

questions.q: The room is warm and you want to say so about yourself. Which?
questions.why: J'ai chaud. Je suis chaud is real French about something else entirely, which is why nobody corrects it and everybody notices. Lesson 11.

questions.q: Which of these takes de after it?
questions.why: avoir besoin de. With avoir envie de and avoir mal à, it is one of only three that carry anything. The other eleven states take nothing at all. Lesson 11.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je n'ai pas de faim ». Fix it.
questions.why: Je n'ai pas faim. Nothing collapsed to de, because there was no article there to collapse. Lesson 11.

questions.q: Listen. Which did you hear?
questions.why: Ils ont, said [eel ZOHⁿ] with a z. Ils sont has an s sound and means they are. One consonant separates having from being. Lesson 11.

rounds.label: Lesson 12 · Days of the week
rounds.say: Le makes it every week.

questions.q: You are free every Saturday. Which do you say?
questions.why: Je suis libre le samedi. The le makes it every week. Without it you have offered exactly one Saturday. Lesson 12.

questions.q: Write the French for: Wednesday
questions.why: mercredi, [mehr-kruh-DEE], named after Mercury. Lowercase, like every day of the week. Lesson 12.

questions.q: A learner writes « On se voit sur samedi ». Fix it.
questions.why: On se voit samedi. A day name takes no preposition at all, and sur is the English on arriving where it is not wanted. Lesson 12.

questions.q: Which day of the week does a French calendar start on?
questions.why: lundi. The week runs lundi to dimanche, and le week-end sits at the end of the row rather than straddling it. Lesson 12.

questions.q: Which plural IS correct?
opts: tous les samedis, for every Saturday
questions.why: tous les samedis. That is the one place the plural is right. For every Monday as a habit it is le lundi, singular. Lesson 12.

rounds.label: Lesson 13 · Months of the year
rounds.say: En for a month, le for a date.

questions.q: Write the French for: in July
questions.why: en juillet, lowercase. A bare month takes en and never an article. Lesson 13.

questions.q: A learner says « Mon vol est en douze juin ». Fix it.
accept: Mon vol est le douze juin
questions.answer: Mon vol est le douze juin.
questions.why: le douze juin. Put a day in it and the frame changes: en names a month, le names a date. Lesson 13.

questions.q: Which is the first of January?
questions.why: le premier janvier. The first is the only ordinal in the whole system. Every other day is a plain counting number. Lesson 13.

questions.q: Listen. Which month is it?
questions.why: juillet, [zhwee-YEH], with a silent t. juin is [ZHWEHⁿ] and nasal. They are the pair that costs people flights. Lesson 13.

questions.q: Which of these is wrong?
questions.why: le douze de mars. Nothing goes between the number and the month. It still parses, which is why nobody corrects it. Lesson 13.

rounds.label: Lesson 14 · Seasons and weather
rounds.say: Weather makes, people have, things are.

questions.q: The sky is hot. Which shape?
questions.why: Il fait chaud. The weather MAKES. A person HAS, and a thing IS. Three shapes, one adjective. Lesson 14.

questions.q: Write the French for: in spring
questions.why: au printemps. It is the only season that takes au. The other three take en, and there is no reason behind it. Lesson 14.

questions.q: A learner says « Il fait pleut depuis ce matin ». Fix it.
questions.why: Il pleut. pleut is already the whole thing, so welding it to il fait produces two verbs and no sentence. Lesson 14.

questions.q: Which shape does « vent » take?
questions.why: il fait du vent, or il y a du vent. A weather THING takes du after il fait; a weather adjective takes nothing. Lesson 14.

questions.q: How is « automne » said?
questions.why: [oh-TONN]. Written with an m and said with none, and the n at the end is a real n you do pronounce. Lesson 14.

rounds.label: Lesson 15 · Telling the time
rounds.say: Il est says the time. À books it.

questions.q: Someone asks the time and it is eight. What do you answer?
questions.why: Il est huit heures. heures is never dropped, and à books an appointment rather than reporting the clock. Lesson 15.

questions.q: Write the French for: quarter to eight
questions.why: moins LE quart, with the article. It is one short unstressed word in the middle, which is why it goes missing. Lesson 15.

questions.q: A station board reads 20:30. A learner says « vingt heures et demie ». Fix it.
questions.why: vingt heures trente. The twenty-four hour clock takes plain minutes. Mixing it with et demie is the one that marks a beginner in a station. Lesson 15.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Il est midi. midi and minuit are the hour and the noun at once, so they take no heures and no article. And it is midi et demi, without the e. Lesson 15.

questions.q: Listen. What time is it?
opts: Il est douze heures et demie.
questions.why: deux heures, [deu-ZUHR]. douze heures is [doo-ZUHR]. Both grow a z, so the vowel in front of it is the only difference. Lesson 15.

rounds.label: Lesson 16 · Colours
rounds.say: Colours agree. Things that became colours do not.

questions.q: Write: a green skirt (une jupe)
questions.why: une jupe verte. The e is audible: [VEHR] becomes [VEHRT] and the t wakes up. Lesson 16.

questions.q: Which is correct for brown shoes?
questions.why: des chaussures marron. marron was a chestnut before it was a colour, so it never changes. Des marrons is a bag of chestnuts. Lesson 16.

questions.q: A learner writes « une porte blance ». Fix it.
questions.why: blanche. blanc changes more than its ending: the c turns into a ch, and you can hear it. Lesson 16.

questions.q: How do you write dark green eyes?
questions.why: des yeux vert foncé. Neither half moves: a two-word colour has stopped being a plain colour. Lesson 16.

questions.q: Which colour sounds identical in the masculine and the feminine?
questions.why: bleu and bleue are [BLUH] both ways, as are noir and noire. vert, gris and blanc all wake a consonant up. Lesson 16.

rounds.label: Lesson 17 · Basic adjectives
rounds.say: Colours follow the noun. These six come first.

questions.q: Write: a big house
questions.why: une grande maison. grand is one of the six that go in FRONT, which is the opposite of where a colour goes. Lesson 17.

questions.q: A learner writes « un beau homme ». Fix it.
questions.why: un bel homme. beau becomes bel in front of a vowel sound, because two vowels would collide. It is not the feminine. Lesson 17.

questions.q: What is the feminine of vieux?
questions.why: vieille. beau and vieux replace the word outright rather than adding to it. vieil is the masculine used before a vowel. Lesson 17.

questions.q: Which is the plural of « un vieux vélo »?
questions.why: des vieux vélos. vieux and mauvais already end in the letter the plural would add, so the masculine never changes. Lesson 17.

questions.q: Listen. Which did you hear?
questions.why: bonne, [BON], with a plain n. The masculine bon is [BOHⁿ] and nasal, so the doubling is audible. Lesson 17.

rounds.label: Lesson 18 · Adjective placement
rounds.say: When in doubt, put it after.

questions.q: Where does an adjective go if you have never met it before?
opts: At the end of the sentence
questions.why: After. The group in front is ten words and closed; the group behind is every other describing word in the language. Lesson 18.

questions.q: A learner writes « une rouge voiture ». Fix it.
questions.why: une voiture rouge. English puts the colour first and French puts it second, on every phrase. Lesson 18.

questions.q: Write the French for: beautiful paintings (using beaux)
questions.why: de beaux tableaux. des becomes de once one of the ten sits in front of a plural noun, and the adjective keeps its own plural ending. Lesson 18.

questions.q: The building itself is old. Which?
questions.why: C'est un hôtel ancien. In front, ancien means former: a place that used to be a hotel. Behind, it means old. Same word, two meanings, decided by position. Lesson 18.

questions.q: Which is correct for a small red dress?
questions.why: une petite robe rouge. One from each group with the noun in between. No new rule, just the two you already have. Lesson 18.

rounds.label: Lesson 19 · The family
rounds.say: French has no apostrophe. Turn it around.

questions.q: Write the French for: Paul's mother
questions.why: la mère de Paul. French has no apostrophe s, so the phrase turns around: the mother OF Paul. Lesson 19.

questions.q: How is « le fils » said?
questions.why: [LUH FEES]. Silent l and a sounded s, which is the reverse of what the spelling suggests. The thread, fil, is [FEEL] and behaves normally. Lesson 19.

questions.q: A learner writes « les grand-parents ». Fix it.
questions.why: les grands-parents. The grand takes the plural s here, though la grand-mère never changes shape. Lesson 19.

questions.q: Which article does « bébé » take?
opts: la for a girl, le for a boy
questions.why: le bébé, for any baby at all. The word has one gender and the child has another, and they do not have to agree. Lesson 19.

questions.q: Listen. Which did you hear?
questions.why: la cousine, [koo-ZEEN], with a real n because a vowel follows. The masculine is [koo-ZAⁿ], nasal, with no n sound at all. Lesson 19.

rounds.label: Lesson 20 · Possessive adjectives
rounds.say: Ask what is owned, not who owns it.

questions.q: Her father. Which?
questions.why: son père. son agrees with père, not with her. Ask what is owned, never who owns it. Lesson 20.

questions.q: Write the French for: my friend (a woman, using amie)
questions.why: mon amie. amie is feminine, and it still takes mon: ma would put two vowels together. Lesson 20.

questions.q: A learner writes « leurs enfants » about one child. Fix it.
questions.why: leur enfant. leur takes its s from the thing owned, not from the number of owners. Lesson 20.

questions.q: Which is wrong?
questions.why: le mon livre. A possessive replaces the article, so the two never appear together. Lesson 20.

questions.q: His mother. Which?
questions.why: sa mère. mère is feminine so it takes sa, whoever the owner is. This is the mirror of son père and the pair is the whole lesson. Lesson 20.

rounds.label: Lesson 21 · Negation
rounds.say: Wrap the verb, then ask what the verb was.

questions.q: Turn « Il est là » negative.
questions.why: Il n'est pas là. ne and pas wrap the verb, and ne elides to n' in front of a vowel. Lesson 21.

questions.q: Turn « J'ai un frère » negative.
questions.why: Je n'ai pas de frère. After avoir, un, une and des collapse to de. Lesson 21.

questions.q: Turn « C'est un livre » negative.
questions.why: Ce n'est pas un livre. After être nothing collapses. The de rule belongs to avoir, and applying it here is the over-correction. Lesson 21.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je ne ai pas de temps ». Fix it.
questions.why: Je n'ai pas de temps. ne cannot sit unelided in front of a vowel. Lesson 21.

questions.q: Why does « Je n'aime pas le café » keep le?
opts: Because it is a fixed phrase
Because the definite articles never collapse
It does not, it should be de café
questions.why: le, la and les do not move. Only un, une, des and the partitives become de. Lesson 21.

rounds.label: Lesson 22 · Yes and no questions
rounds.say: Est-ce que always works. The other two are choices.

questions.q: Which way of asking is never wrong, spoken or written?
opts: Swapping the verb and the pronoun
questions.why: Est-ce que. Your voice alone is spoken only, and inversion is for careful writing or formal speech. Lesson 22.

questions.q: Write the inversion form of « Il a faim ? »
questions.why: A-t-il faim ? The t is inserted purely so two vowels do not collide, and it is joined by hyphens on both sides. Lesson 22.

questions.q: A learner writes « Est-ce que il est prêt ? ». Fix it.
questions.why: Est-ce qu'il est prêt ? The que elides in front of a vowel, exactly like ne and le. Lesson 22.

questions.q: Which uses two methods at once and so is wrong?
questions.why: Est-ce que es-tu prêt ? Pick one method. Stacking est-ce que on top of an inversion asks the question twice. Lesson 22.

questions.q: How do you ask « Am I hungry? »
questions.why: Est-ce que j'ai faim ? Inversion with je is avoided in speech, and reaching for Ai-je to complete the table is the trap. Lesson 22.

rounds.label: Lesson 23 · Question words
rounds.say: Your word, then est-ce que. That always works.

questions.q: You want to know WHEN the train leaves. Which word?
questions.why: quand gets you a time. où gets you a place, and asking the wrong one gets you a confident answer to a question you did not ask. Lesson 23.

questions.q: Write the French for: How many children do you have? (vous)
questions.why: Combien d'enfants. combien always carries de, and it elides in front of a vowel. Lesson 23.

questions.q: A learner writes « Quel heure est-il ? ». Fix it.
questions.why: Quelle heure. heure is feminine so quel agrees with it. All four forms sound identical, so only writing exposes this. Lesson 23.

questions.q: A learner writes « Ou est le train ? ». What is missing?
questions.why: où, with the accent. Without it, ou means or, and the accent is the only thing separating two very common words. Lesson 23.

questions.q: Which is right at the end of a spoken question?
questions.why: Tu fais quoi ? que cannot sit at the end. It becomes quoi there, and that is where you will hear it most. Lesson 23.

rounds.label: Lesson 24 · Prepositions of place
rounds.say: One word goes straight onto the noun. A phrase needs de first.

questions.q: Write the French for: The keys are on the desk
accept: Les clés sont sur le bureau
les cles sont sur le bureau
questions.answer: Les clés sont sur le bureau.
questions.why: sur le bureau. sur is one word and it goes straight onto the noun, with no de. Lesson 24.

questions.q: A learner writes « Le café est à côté la banque ». Fix it.
accept: Le café est à côté de la banque
le cafe est a cote de la banque
questions.answer: Le café est à côté de la banque.
questions.why: à côté DE la banque. A multi-word preposition needs de before the noun. près de and loin de work the same way. Lesson 24.

questions.q: What does « de + le » become?
questions.why: du. And de + les is des, à + le is au, à + les is aux. Only la and l' are left alone. Lesson 24.

questions.q: Which is wrong?
questions.why: sur de la boîte. sur is a one-word preposition, so the de is an over-correction borrowed from à côté de. Lesson 24.

questions.q: You are going to a friend's place. Which word?
questions.why: chez. It means at somebody's place and English has no single word for it. Lesson 24.

rounds.label: Lesson 25 · Countries and nationalities
rounds.say: Learn the country with its article. Everything else follows.

questions.q: Write the French for: I am going to Canada
questions.why: au Canada. le Canada is masculine, so à + le gives au. Store the article with the country and this falls out. Lesson 25.

questions.q: A learner says « Je viens du France ». Fix it.
questions.why: de France. A feminine country takes plain de coming from, and en going to. Lesson 25.

questions.q: Going to the United States. Which?
questions.why: aux États-Unis. les États-Unis is plural, so à + les gives aux. Lesson 25.

questions.q: Going to Iran. Which?
questions.why: en Iran. l'Iran is masculine, but it opens on a vowel, and a vowel takes en whatever the gender. Lesson 25.

questions.q: Which is right for a French woman describing herself?
questions.why: Je suis française. Lowercase, because it is an adjective here, and no article after être. Lesson 25.

rounds.label: Lesson 26 · Food
rounds.say: Aimer takes the whole thing. Manger takes a part of it.

questions.q: Write the French for: I like bread
questions.why: J'aime le pain. aimer points at the whole category, so it takes le, la or les. Lesson 26.

questions.q: Which verb takes du, de la or des?
questions.why: boire, with manger and prendre. Those three take an amount. aimer, adorer, détester and préférer take the whole category. Lesson 26.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je mange le pain ». Fix it.
questions.why: Je mange du pain. manger takes a part of it. Je mange le pain says you ate the whole loaf that was on the table. Lesson 26.

questions.q: Listen. Which food is it?
questions.why: le poisson, [luh pwah-SOHⁿ]. It is also the one -son noun that breaks the -tion feminine pattern. Lesson 26.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: des pâtes. les pâtes is plural only. Une pâte is a dough or a paste, which is a different thing on a different shelf. Lesson 26.

rounds.label: Lesson 27 · The body
rounds.say: The person goes in the verb. The body part takes le, la or les.

questions.q: Write the French for: I have a headache
questions.why: J'ai mal à la tête. The person is already in j'ai, so the body part takes a plain article rather than a possessive. Lesson 27.

questions.q: A learner writes « Mon dos fait mal ». Fix it.
questions.why: J'ai mal au dos. French does not make the body part the subject. à + le gives au. Lesson 27.

questions.q: My teeth hurt. Which?
questions.why: J'ai mal aux dents. à + les gives aux, exactly as it did with countries. Lesson 27.

questions.q: Which is correct for brown eyes?
questions.why: les yeux marron. marron never agrees, here as everywhere. les yeux bleus and les yeux verts do take the silent s. Lesson 27.

questions.q: How do you say you have blue eyes?
questions.why: J'ai les yeux bleus. French HAS the eyes, with a plain article. Mes yeux sont bleus is understandable and it is not what anybody says. Lesson 27.

rounds.label: Lesson 28 · Daily routine
rounds.say: The parts of the day take le. Midi and minuit take nothing.

questions.q: Write the French for: I get up at seven
accept: Je me lève à sept heures
je me leve a sept heures
questions.answer: Je me lève à sept heures.
questions.why: Je me lève. se lever carries its me, and dropping it leaves a verb with nobody doing anything. Lesson 28.

questions.q: At noon. Which?
questions.why: à midi. Noon is a point on the clock, so there is nothing to mark as a habit. A stretch of hours takes le: le matin, le soir. Lesson 28.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je déjeuner le midi ». Fix it.
questions.why: Je déjeune à midi. Two things went wrong: the infinitive was left unconjugated, and midi took an article it never takes. Lesson 28.

questions.q: Which article does « après-midi » take here?
questions.why: l'après-midi. It is a stretch of hours so it takes an article, and the article elides before the vowel. Lesson 28.

questions.q: You mean THIS evening, not evenings in general. Which?
questions.why: Ce soir. le soir makes it a habit, every evening. It is the same le that made le samedi every week. Lesson 28.

rounds.label: Lesson 29 · The house
rounds.say: Never say room. Say which room.

questions.q: You need the toilet in a French home. What do you ask for?
questions.why: les toilettes, always plural. The salle de bain is where the bath is, and in most French homes that is a different room. Lesson 29.

questions.q: Write the French for: the kitchen
questions.why: la cuisine. The -ine ending is feminine ninety-six percent of the time, which is a lean you can use. Lesson 29.

questions.q: An advert says « trois pièces ». What are you being offered?
opts: Three rooms in total, kitchen and bathroom not counted
questions.why: Three rooms in total, and the kitchen and bathroom are not among them. Hearing it as three bedrooms is how people rent the wrong flat. Lesson 29.

questions.q: A learner uses « chambre » for the room they are sitting in. Fix it.
questions.why: le salon for the living room, or la pièce for a room in general. A chambre has a bed in it. Lesson 29.

questions.q: Which takes le because it is a verb plus a noun?
questions.why: le lave-vaisselle, like le sèche-linge and le micro-ondes. A verb plus a noun is masculine, so those three need no storing. Lesson 29.

sections.title: Where You Are
sections.say: Read the round scores, not the total.
sections.body: The percentage at the top is the least useful number on that screen. What is worth reading is the list underneath it, because a round is a lesson and a low round is an afternoon of work rather than a verdict on your French. Two or three weak rounds after twenty-nine lessons is an ordinary result and the fix is specific: go back to those units, sit them again, and come back here. When the rounds are level, the exam is the next thing, and it is deliberately harder in one way only, which is that it will not tell you what it is asking about.
points: A wrong answer names the half hour to sit again.
Read the round scores rather than the total. The total hides which lesson went.
A drill that fired is worth more than a round you passed. It caught something live.
The exam is a separate sitting, and it is the one that answers whether you have A1.

lessons.title: L'examen A1
lessons.intro: Sixty questions across twelve situations, mixed so that nothing tells you which lesson it came from. No explanations until the end, and no drills. Seventy percent is a pass.
grammarAssumed: The whole A1 band, a1.01 to a1.29, and the lesson-by-lesson review in a1.30.l1

overview.introFr: Soixante questions, douze situations, aucune indication de leçon.

acts.title: The brief
acts.milestone: You know the rules of the sitting.

acts.title: Sixty questions
acts.milestone: A1 complete.

lessons.reframe: Nothing here tells you which lesson it came from.

sections.title: The Exam
sections.say: Sixty questions, and it will not help you while you answer.

goals.s: Each part is a situation rather than a lesson, and every one of them crosses three or four units. Nothing here tells you which lesson it came from.
Right or wrong, you get the next question. Everything you missed is collected and explained on the result card, with the lesson to go back to.
The review lesson does both of those. This one measures, which it cannot do while also teaching the thing it is about to ask about.
Sit the review first if you have not. Coming here cold is allowed and it mostly tells you what you already suspected.

sections.title: Before You Start
sections.say: Once you start, it does not stop to explain.
sections.body: Nothing here tells you which lesson it came from. That is the only way this differs from the review, and it is the whole difficulty.

sections.title: L'examen A1
sections.say: Twelve parts. Nothing is explained until you finish.

rounds.label: At the counter
rounds.say: A shop, a queue, and somebody waiting for you to start.

questions.q: It is ten in the morning and you are third in the queue. You reach the front. First word?
questions.why: Bonjour, before anything else. Opening with the order rather than the greeting is the one thing that reads as rude. Lesson 1, greetings.

questions.q: Write the French for: Two coffees, please
questions.why: Deux cafés, s'il vous plaît. A counted thing takes the plain number, and the s on cafés is silent but written. Lessons 2 and 1.

questions.q: You want coffee by weight to take home, not a cup. Which?
questions.why: du café. un café is a cup and le café is the category. The partitive is the one that means some of it. Lesson 8, partitive articles.

questions.q: The total is 12,40 €. How much?
questions.why: Twelve euros forty. The comma is the decimal point in French. Lesson 4, large numbers.

questions.q: They say merci. You answer?
questions.why: De rien. Answering merci with merci leaves the exchange open. Lesson 1, greetings.

rounds.label: Saying who you are
rounds.say: Your name, your job, your age, where you are from.

questions.q: Write the French for: I am a teacher
questions.why: No article after être in front of a job. Je suis un professeur is the reflex carried over from English. Lesson 7, indefinite articles.

questions.q: Write the French for: I am twenty-five
questions.why: French HAS its age and never leaves ans off. Lessons 11 and 3.

questions.q: A woman from Germany says which?
questions.why: Je suis allemande. Lowercase as an adjective, feminine agreement, and no article. Lessons 25 and 10.

questions.q: Pointing at a colleague across the room, you say?
questions.why: C'est. Anything with mon, un or a name in front of it takes c'est, never il est. Lesson 10, être.

questions.q: Say it: « Je viens de Lyon. »
questions.why: A town takes de and nothing else. A country would take de, du or des depending on its article. Lessons 10 and 25.

rounds.label: Your people and your things
rounds.say: Who belongs to whom, and whose is whose.

questions.q: Write the French for: Marie's brother
questions.why: French has no apostrophe s, so the phrase turns around. Lesson 19, the family.

questions.q: Her father. Which?
questions.why: son père. The possessive agrees with the thing owned, not with the owner. Lesson 20, possessives.

questions.q: A learner writes « ma amie ». Fix it.
questions.why: mon amie, though amie is feminine. ma would put two vowels together. Lesson 20, possessives.

questions.q: Which article does bébé take?
opts: le for a boy, la for a girl
questions.why: le bébé, always. The word has a gender and the child has one, and they are unrelated. Lesson 19, the family.

questions.q: One child, belonging to two parents. Which?
questions.why: leur enfant. The s on leur comes from the thing owned, and there is one child. Lesson 20, possessives.

rounds.label: Describing somebody
rounds.say: What they look like, and where the describing word goes.

questions.q: Write: a big red house
questions.why: One from each group with the noun in between: grande in front, rouge behind. Lesson 18, placement.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: un bel homme. beau becomes bel in front of a vowel sound, and it is not the feminine. Lesson 17, basic adjectives.

questions.q: A learner writes « Il a les yeux marrons ». Fix it.
questions.why: marron never agrees, because it was a chestnut before it was a colour. Lessons 27 and 16.

questions.q: Listen. Which did you hear?
questions.why: grande, with the d released. The masculine grand is [GRAHⁿ] and stops on the nasal. Lesson 17, basic adjectives.

questions.q: The man is tall. Which?
questions.why: un homme grand is tall. un grand homme is a great man. Position changes the meaning. Lesson 18, placement.

rounds.label: The clock and the calendar
rounds.say: What time, what day, what month.

questions.q: Somebody asks the time and it is eight. Answer?
questions.why: Il est huit heures. heures is never dropped, and à books rather than reports. Lesson 15, telling the time.

questions.q: Write the French for: on the twelfth of March
questions.why: le douze mars. A date takes le, a plain counting number, and nothing between the number and the month. Lesson 13, months.

questions.q: A learner writes « Il est midi et demie ». Fix it.
questions.why: midi et demi, with no e. midi is masculine, and the error is inaudible so nothing ever corrects it. Lesson 15.

questions.q: A board reads 16:10. Said out loud in the everyday way?
questions.why: quatre heures dix in speech, seize heures dix as printed. The twenty-four hour clock never takes et. Lesson 15.

questions.q: Every Monday, as a habit. Which?
questions.why: le lundi. The le makes it every week, and the English plural is wrong here. Lesson 12, days.

rounds.label: Making a plan
rounds.say: Fixing a time with somebody, out loud.

questions.q: Write the French for: Are you free on Saturday? (tu, using est-ce que)
accept: Est-ce que tu es libre samedi ?
est ce que tu es libre samedi
questions.answer: Est-ce que tu es libre samedi ?
questions.why: Est-ce que in front, and a day name takes no preposition. Lessons 22 and 12.

questions.q: A learner writes « On se voit sur samedi ». Fix it.
questions.why: No preposition on a day. sur is the English on arriving where French wants nothing. Lesson 12, days.

questions.q: Which verb form goes with on?
questions.why: On est. on means we and takes the il form. Lesson 9, subject pronouns.

questions.q: You want to say around eight, without promising the minute. Which?
questions.why: vers huit heures. vers replaces à rather than joining it, and pile and précises mean the opposite. Lesson 15.

questions.q: Listen. Which day?
questions.why: jeudi, [zheu-DEE]. It is the one most often confused with mardi over a phone. Lesson 12, days.

rounds.label: Asking for what you need
rounds.say: Questions, and saying no.

questions.q: You want to know WHERE the station is. Which word?
questions.why: où gets you a place. Lesson 23, question words.

questions.q: Write the French for: How many children do you have? (vous)
questions.why: combien always carries de, elided before a vowel. Lesson 23, question words.

questions.q: Turn « J'ai une voiture » negative.
questions.why: After avoir, une collapses to de. Lesson 21, negation.

questions.q: Which is wrong?
questions.why: The last one stacks two methods and asks the question twice. Lesson 22, yes and no questions.

questions.q: A learner writes « Quel heure est-il ? ». Fix it.
questions.why: heure is feminine, so quelle. All four forms sound the same, so only writing catches it. Lesson 23.

rounds.label: At the market
rounds.say: Food, amounts, and the little word in front of it.

questions.q: Write the French for: a kilo of tomatoes
questions.why: A quantity takes plain de, never du or des. Lesson 8, partitive articles.

questions.q: You like fish in general. Which?
questions.why: aimer points at the whole category, so le. Lesson 26, food.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je mange le pain ». Fix it.
questions.why: manger takes an amount. le pain says you ate the whole loaf. Lesson 26, food.

questions.q: Listen. Which did you hear?
questions.why: les haricots verts, and the h is aspirated so there is no z linking into it. Lesson 26, food.

questions.q: Turn « Je mange du fromage » negative.
opts: Je ne mange pas du fromage.
Je ne mange pas le fromage.
Je ne mange pas de fromage.
questions.why: The partitive collapses to de under a negative. Lesson 8, partitive articles.

rounds.label: Finding your way
rounds.say: Where a thing is, and where you are going.

questions.q: Write the French for: The bag is under the table
accept: Le sac est sous la table
questions.answer: Le sac est sous la table.
questions.why: sous goes straight onto the noun, with no de. Lesson 24, prepositions of place.

questions.q: A learner writes « Nous habitons près la gare ». Fix it.
accept: Nous habitons près de la gare
nous habitons pres de la gare
questions.answer: Nous habitons près de la gare.
questions.why: près DE. A multi-word preposition needs de before the noun. Lesson 24.

questions.q: Going to Japan. Which?
questions.why: au Japon. le Japon is masculine and starts on a consonant, so à + le gives au. Lesson 25, countries.

questions.q: What does « à + les » become?
questions.why: aux, as in aux États-Unis and aux dents. Lesson 24, prepositions of place.

questions.q: You are going to a friend's house. Which word?
questions.why: chez, at somebody's place. English has no single word for it. Lesson 24.

rounds.label: At home
rounds.say: The rooms, and what is in them.

questions.q: You need the toilet. What do you ask for?
questions.why: les toilettes, plural, and usually a different room from the salle de bain. Lesson 29, the house.

questions.q: Write the French for: the bedroom
questions.why: la chambre, the room with a bed in it. For a room in general it is la pièce. Lesson 29, the house.

questions.q: Which article does « armoire » take?
questions.why: une armoire, feminine, written l'armoire with the article hidden under the apostrophe. Lesson 5, noun gender.

questions.q: Write the French for: The cat sleeps on the sofa
accept: Le chat dort sur le canapé
le chat dort sur le canape
questions.answer: Le chat dort sur le canapé.
questions.why: sur le canapé. One-word preposition, straight onto the noun. Lessons 24 and 29.

questions.q: An advert offers « trois pièces ». What is that?
opts: Three rooms, kitchen and bathroom not counted
questions.why: Three rooms in total, and the kitchen and bathroom are not among them. Lesson 29, the house.

rounds.label: The weather and the year
rounds.say: What the sky is doing, and when.

questions.q: It is hot outside. Which?
questions.why: Il fait chaud. The weather makes, a person has, a thing is. Lesson 14, seasons and weather.

questions.q: You are too warm. Which?
questions.why: J'ai chaud. Je suis chaud is real French about something else. Lessons 11 and 14.

questions.q: Write the French for: in spring
questions.why: au printemps, the only season that takes au. Lesson 14, seasons and weather.

questions.q: A learner writes « Il fait pleut ». Fix it.
questions.why: pleut is already the whole thing. Welding it to il fait gives two verbs and no sentence. Lesson 14.

questions.q: Listen. Which season?
questions.why: en automne, [ahⁿ-noh-TONN]. The m is silent and the n at the end is real. Lesson 14.

rounds.label: When it goes wrong
rounds.say: The last five. Mixed, and no warning about which lesson.

questions.q: You understood nothing at all. What do you say?
questions.why: Say you have not understood. The other three answer different problems and get you something you did not need. Lesson 1 and this unit.

questions.q: The repetition came back at exactly the same speed. What do you ask for?
questions.why: Ask for slower rather than for again. Asking for again a second time gets you the same sentence at the same speed. This unit.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je suis vingt ans ». Fix it.
questions.why: French has its age. Lesson 11, avoir.

questions.q: Which of these is correct?
questions.why: Only the third. le does not move under a negative, un after avoir becomes de, un after être does not, and faim had no article to collapse. Lesson 21, negation.

questions.q: Say it: « Excusez-moi, je ne comprends pas. »
questions.why: The sentence that keeps a conversation alive. Nobody minds it and it costs nothing. This unit.

sections.title: That Is A1
sections.say: What the number means, and what comes after it.
sections.body: Seventy percent across sixty mixed questions is a real A1, and it is worth being clear about what that means, because it is easy to undersell. It means you can meet somebody, say who you are and how old you are and where you are from, count and pay and tell the time, ask for what you want and say when you do not want it, describe a person and a room and a plate of food, and ask a question five different ways. Below seventy, the round scores tell you where it went, and the review lesson tells you which half hour to sit again. There is no version of this where the answer is start over.
points: Read the missed questions underneath the score. Each one names its lesson.
A part is a situation, not a unit, so a weak part usually means two units rather than one.
Sit the review lesson for anything that went badly, then come back and sit this again.
Nothing here tells you which lesson it came from. That was the point, and you did it anyway.

items.fr: Mon frère est un grand garçon.
items.en: My brother is a big boy.
items.notes: The masculine 'grand' ends in a silent d.

items.fr: Elle habite dans une grande maison.
items.en: She lives in a big house.
items.ipa: ɛl a.bit dɑ̃z yn ɡʁɑ̃d mɛ.zɔ̃
items.notes: Feminine 'grande' pronounces the d clearly.
'Grande' agrees with the feminine 'ville'.

items.fr: Le grand chat noir dort sur le lit.
items.en: The big black cat is sleeping on the bed.
items.ipa: lə ɡʁɑ̃ ʃa nwaʁ dɔʁ syʁ lə li
items.notes: Short adjectives like 'grand' go before the noun.

items.en: I have a small white dog.
items.notes: The masculine 'petit' ends in a silent t.

items.fr: Elle porte une petite robe rouge.
items.en: She is wearing a small red dress.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁt yn pə.tit ʁɔb ʁuʒ
items.notes: Feminine 'petite' pronounces the final t.
'Petite' agrees with the feminine 'ville'.
'Bon' is a short adjective placed before the noun.

items.fr: Nous avons passé de bonnes vacances.
items.ipa: nu za.vɔ̃ pa.se də bɔn va.kɑ̃s

items.fr: Les enfants ont de bons résultats à l'école.
items.en: The children have good results at school.
items.ipa: le zɑ̃.fɑ̃ ɔ̃ də bɔ̃ ʁe.zyl.ta a le.kɔl

items.notes: Feminine 'mauvaise' adds a z sound before a vowel.
'Beau' precedes the noun 'jardin'.
'Bel' replaces 'beau' before a masculine noun starting with a vowel.

items.fr: Elle porte une belle robe bleue.
items.en: She is wearing a beautiful blue dress.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁt yn bɛl ʁɔb blø
items.notes: 'Beau' becomes 'belle' in the feminine.

items.fr: Ils habitent dans une jolie maison blanche.
items.en: They live in a pretty white house.
items.ipa: il za.bit dɑ̃z yn ʒɔ.li mɛ.zɔ̃ blɑ̃ʃ
items.notes: 'Jolie' agrees with the feminine 'maison'.

items.fr: Elle a une nouvelle voiture rouge.
items.en: She has a new red car.
items.ipa: ɛl a yn nu.vɛl vwa.tyʁ ʁuʒ
items.notes: 'Nouveau' becomes 'nouvelle' in the feminine.
'Vieux' precedes the noun 'château'.

items.fr: Mon grand-père a un vieil ami à Lyon.
items.en: My grandfather has an old friend in Lyon.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ɡʁɑ̃.pɛʁ a œ̃ vjɛj a.mi a ljɔ̃
items.notes: 'Vieil' replaces 'vieux' before a vowel-starting masculine noun.
'Jeune' precedes the noun 'homme'.

items.en: She is wearing a short skirt.
items.notes: 'Courte' agrees with the feminine 'jupe'.
'Gros' precedes the noun 'chat'.
'Gros' doubles the s in the feminine 'grosse'.

items.fr: Les journées sont chaudes en juillet.
items.en: The days are hot in July.
items.ipa: le ʒuʁ.ne sɔ̃ ʃod ɑ̃ ʒɥi.jɛ

items.notes: The feminine 'forte' pronounces the final t.

items.fr: Le musée est ouvert le samedi.
items.en: The museum is open on Saturdays.
items.ipa: lə my.ze ɛ u.vɛʁ lə sam.di
items.notes: 'Ouvert' follows 'être' describing the museum.
'Méchant' follows 'n'est pas' describing the dog.

In front, grand is about importance rather than height. Nothing about the man's size is being said.
Behind, grand is a measurement. Same three words, same order of everything else, and the two sentences describe two different men.
In front, ancien means it used to be one and is not one now. It could be flats today.
Behind, ancien means old. It is still a hotel and you can still book a room in it.
In front, pauvre is sympathy. It says nothing at all about money.

items.en: He is a man with no money.
items.notes: Behind, pauvre is about money and nothing else. English uses the one word poor for both of these, which is why the position has to do the work.
In front, propre means it belongs to me and I do not share it.
Behind, propre means clean. Same room either way, and only one of the two sentences is about tidying.
Every word correct, and it does not mean what the learner in the opening scene meant by it. In front, ancien is always former.

items.fr: Les noms en -al font leur pluriel en -aux.
items.en: Nouns ending in -al form their plural with -aux.
items.notes: Ex : un animal, des animaux · un cheval, des chevaux · un journal, des journaux

items.en: I am going to the pharmacy to buy bandages.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ a la faʁ.ma.si puʁ aʃ.te de pɑ̃s.mɑ̃

items.fr: Tu manges des fruits chaque jour pour ta santé.
items.en: You eat fruit every day for your health.
items.ipa: ty mɑ̃ʒ de fʁɥi ʃak ʒuʁ puʁ ta sɑ̃.te

items.fr: Il a des lunettes de soleil parce qu'il fait très beau.
items.en: He has sunglasses because the weather is very nice.
items.ipa: il a de ly.nɛt də sɔ.lɛj paʁs.kil fɛ tʁɛ bo

items.fr: Ma tante attend son opération à l'hôpital.
items.en: My aunt is waiting for her operation at the hospital.
items.ipa: ma tɑ̃t a.tɑ̃ sɔ̃.n‿ɔ.pe.ʁa.sjɔ̃ a lo.pi.tal

items.fr: Nous nettoyons la blessure avec de l'eau et du savon.
items.en: We clean the wound with water and soap.
items.ipa: nu ne.twa.jɔ̃ la ble.syʁ a.vɛk də lo e dy sa.vɔ̃

items.fr: Le patient explique ses symptômes au médecin.
items.en: The patient explains his symptoms to the doctor.
items.ipa: lə pa.sjɑ̃ ɛks.plik se sɛ̃p.tom o med.sɛ̃

items.fr: Elle va passer un examen médical la semaine prochaine.
items.en: She is going to have a medical exam next week.
items.ipa: ɛl va pa.se œ̃.n‿ɛɡ.za.mɛ̃ me.di.kal la sə.mɛn pʁɔ.ʃɛn

items.fr: J'ai un peu de fièvre alors je reste à la maison.
items.en: I have a bit of a fever so I am staying home.
items.ipa: ʒe œ̃ pø də fjɛvʁ a.lɔʁ ʒə ʁɛst a la mɛ.zɔ̃

items.fr: Le chirurgien travaille dans un grand hôpital.
items.en: The surgeon works at a big hospital.

items.fr: Tu bois du sirop contre la toux avant de dormir.
items.en: You drink cough syrup before sleeping.
items.ipa: ty bwa dy si.ʁo kɔ̃tʁ la tu a.vɑ̃ də dɔʁ.miʁ

items.fr: Nous allons prendre rendez-vous chez l'ophtalmologue.
items.en: We are going to make an appointment with the eye doctor.

items.fr: Le médecin ausculte le patient chaque matin.
items.en: The doctor examines the patient every morning.
items.ipa: lə med.sɛ̃ os.kylt lə pa.sjɑ̃ ʃak ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: "ausculte" s'écrit avec un s même s'il ne s'entend presque pas.

items.fr: J'ai pris rendez-vous chez le généraliste.
items.en: I made an appointment with the general practitioner.
items.ipa: ʒe pʁi ʁɑ̃.de.vu ʃe lə ʒe.ne.ʁa.list
items.notes: "généraliste" ne prend qu'un seul l, facile d'en ajouter un par erreur.

items.fr: Elle souffre d'un mal de gorge depuis trois jours.
items.en: She has had a sore throat for three days.
items.ipa: ɛl sufʁ dœ̃ mal də ɡɔʁʒ də.pɥi tʁwa ʒuʁ
items.notes: "souffre" prend deux f, à ne pas oublier.

items.fr: Nous devons remplir ce formulaire médical avant la consultation.
items.en: We must fill out this medical form before the consultation.
items.ipa: nu də.vɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.pliʁ sə fɔʁ.my.lɛʁ me.di.kal a.vɑ̃ la kɔ̃.syl.ta.sjɔ̃
items.notes: "remplir" se termine en ir, ne pas écrire "remplire".

items.fr: Le pharmacien vérifie l'ordonnance avant de donner les médicaments.
items.en: The pharmacist checks the prescription before giving the medicine.
items.ipa: lə faʁ.ma.sjɛ̃ ve.ʁi.fi lɔʁ.dɔ.nɑ̃s a.vɑ̃ də dɔ.ne le me.di.ka.mɑ̃
items.notes: "ordonnance" prend deux n, une erreur fréquente.

items.fr: Mon estomac me fait mal depuis ce matin.
items.en: My stomach has hurt since this morning.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.n‿ɛs.tɔ.ma mə fɛ mal də.pɥi sə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: le c final de "estomac" ne se prononce pas.

items.en: The nurse takes my blood pressure.
items.notes: "artérielle" prend deux l à cause de l'accord au féminin.

items.fr: Il a une entorse à la cheville après le match.
items.en: He has a sprained ankle after the match.
items.ipa: il a yn ɑ̃.tɔʁs a la ʃə.vij a.pʁɛ lə matʃ
items.notes: attention au s final de "entorse", souvent oublié à l'oral.

items.fr: La salle d'urgence est très occupée ce soir.
items.en: The emergency room is very busy tonight.
items.ipa: la sal dyʁ.ʒɑ̃s ɛ tʁɛ.z‿ɔ.ky.pe sə swaʁ
items.notes: "occupée" prend deux c, et le e final s'accorde au féminin.

items.fr: Vous devez suivre ce traitement pendant dix jours.
items.en: You must follow this treatment for ten days.
items.ipa: vu də.ve sɥivʁ sə tʁɛt.mɑ̃ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ di ʒuʁ
items.notes: le x de "dix" ne se prononce pas devant une consonne.

items.fr: Elle a subi une petite intervention chirurgicale hier.
items.en: She had a small surgery yesterday.
items.ipa: ɛl a sy.bi yn pə.tit ɛ̃.tɛʁ.vɑ̃.sjɔ̃ ʃi.ʁyʁ.ʒi.kal jɛʁ
items.notes: "chirurgicale" garde le g doux grâce au i qui suit.

items.fr: Le vaccin contre la grippe est gratuit cette année.
items.en: The flu vaccine is free this year.
items.ipa: lə vak.sɛ̃ kɔ̃tʁ la ɡʁip ɛ ɡʁa.tɥi sɛt a.ne
items.notes: "vaccin" prend deux c, le premier dur et le second doux.

items.fr: Mon cousin a une cicatrice sur le front.
items.en: My cousin has a scar on his forehead.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ku.zɛ̃ a yn si.ka.tʁis syʁ lə fʁɔ̃
items.notes: "cicatrice" commence par deux c qui se prononcent différemment.

items.fr: Le médecin diagnostique une bronchite chez l'enfant.
items.en: The doctor diagnoses the child with bronchitis.
items.ipa: lə med.sɛ̃ djaɡ.nɔs.tik yn bʁɔ̃.ʃit ʃe lɑ̃.fɑ̃
items.notes: le g de "diagnostique" ne se prononce pas.

items.fr: Nous attendons les résultats de l'analyse sanguine.
items.en: We are waiting for the blood test results.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.tɑ̃.dɔ̃ le ʁe.zyl.ta də la.na.liz sɑ̃.ɡin
items.notes: "sanguine" garde le u pour que le g reste dur.

items.fr: Cette maladie se soigne facilement avec des antibiotiques.
items.en: This illness is easily treated with antibiotics.
items.ipa: sɛt ma.la.di sə swaɲ fa.sil.mɑ̃ a.vɛk de.z‿ɑ̃.ti.bjɔ.tik
items.notes: "antibiotiques" prend un s au pluriel, facile à oublier.

items.fr: Elle éternue sans arrêt à cause du rhume des foins.
items.en: She sneezes nonstop because of hay fever.
items.ipa: ɛl e.tɛʁ.ny sɑ̃.z‿a.ʁɛ a koz dy ʁym de fwɛ̃
items.notes: "arrêt" prend un accent circonflexe sur le e.

items.fr: Le kinésithérapeute masse les muscles endoloris.
items.en: The physiotherapist massages the sore muscles.
items.ipa: lə ki.ne.zi.te.ʁa.pøt mas le myskl ɑ̃.dɔ.lɔ.ʁi
items.notes: "kinésithérapeute" est long, attention à ne pas oublier le h.

items.fr: J'ai avalé un comprimé avec un grand verre d'eau.
items.en: I swallowed a pill with a big glass of water.
items.ipa: ʒe a.va.le œ̃ kɔ̃.pʁi.me a.vɛk œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ vɛʁ do
items.notes: "comprimé" ne prend qu'un seul m.

items.fr: Le chirurgien-dentiste examine mes dents une fois par an.
items.en: The dental surgeon examines my teeth once a year.
items.ipa: lə ʃi.ʁyʁ.ʒjɛ̃ dɑ̃.tist ɛɡ.za.min me dɑ̃ yn fwa paʁ ɑ̃
items.notes: le trait d'union entre "chirurgien" et "dentiste" ne s'oublie pas.

items.fr: Elle a des vertiges quand elle se lève trop vite.
items.en: She gets dizzy when she stands up too quickly.
items.ipa: ɛl a de vɛʁ.tiʒ kɑ̃.t‿ɛl sə lɛv tʁo vit
items.notes: "vertiges" prend un g doux grâce au e final.

items.fr: Le nouveau-né pèse trois kilos et deux cents grammes.
items.en: The newborn weighs three kilos two hundred grams.
items.ipa: lə nu.vo ne pɛz tʁwa ki.lo e dø sɑ̃ ɡʁam
items.notes: "nouveau-né" garde son trait d'union, comme un seul mot composé.

items.fr: Mon oncle a subi une greffe du rein l'année dernière.
items.en: My uncle had a kidney transplant last year.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.n‿ɔ̃kl a sy.bi yn ɡʁɛf dy ʁɛ̃ la.ne dɛʁ.njɛʁ
items.notes: "greffe" prend deux f, une erreur courante.

items.fr: Cette pommade soulage les démangeaisons rapidement.
items.ipa: sɛt pɔ.mad su.laʒ le de.mɑ̃.ʒɛ.zɔ̃ ʁa.pid.mɑ̃
items.notes: "pommade" prend deux m.

items.fr: Le patient signe le formulaire de consentement.
items.en: The patient signs the consent form.
items.ipa: lə pa.sjɑ̃ siɲ lə fɔʁ.my.lɛʁ də kɔ̃.sɑ̃t.mɑ̃
items.notes: le gn de "signe" se prononce comme un seul son mouillé.

items.fr: Elle respire difficilement à cause de son asthme.
items.en: She breathes with difficulty because of her asthma.
items.ipa: ɛl ʁɛs.piʁ di.fi.sil.mɑ̃ a koz də sɔ.n‿asm
items.notes: le th de "asthme" ne se prononce pas, mais ne s'oublie pas à l'écrit.

items.fr: Le médecin prescrit un sirop contre la toux sèche.
items.en: The doctor prescribes syrup for the dry cough.
items.ipa: lə med.sɛ̃ pʁɛs.kʁi œ̃ si.ʁo kɔ̃tʁ la tu sɛʃ
items.notes: "prescrit" ne prend pas de e entre le p et le r.

items.fr: J'ai remarqué une éruption cutanée sur mon bras.
items.en: I noticed a skin rash on my arm.
items.ipa: ʒe ʁə.maʁ.ke yn e.ʁyp.sjɔ̃ ky.ta.ne syʁ mɔ̃ bʁa
items.notes: "cutanée" prend un e final muet pour l'accord au féminin.

items.fr: Nous consultons un spécialiste pour ce problème de dos.
items.en: We are consulting a specialist for this back problem.
items.ipa: nu kɔ̃.syl.tɔ̃.z‿œ̃ spe.sja.list puʁ sə pʁɔ.blɛm də do
items.notes: "spécialiste" s'écrit avec un c et non un s après l'é.

items.en: The ambulance arrives quickly after the accident.
items.notes: "accident" prend deux c, le premier dur et le second doux.

items.fr: Elle a perdu connaissance pendant quelques secondes.
items.en: She lost consciousness for a few seconds.
items.ipa: ɛl a pɛʁ.dy kɔ.nɛ.sɑ̃s pɑ̃.dɑ̃ kɛl.kə sə.ɡɔ̃d
items.notes: "connaissance" prend deux n et deux s.

items.fr: Le dossier médical reste confidentiel entre le patient et le médecin.
items.en: The medical file stays confidential between the patient and the doctor.
items.ipa: lə dɔ.sje me.di.kal ʁɛst kɔ̃.fi.dɑ̃.sjɛl ɑ̃tʁ lə pa.sjɑ̃ e lə med.sɛ̃
items.notes: "confidentiel" se termine par tiel, comme "essentiel".

items.fr: Mon grand-père souffre d'hypertension depuis longtemps.
items.en: My grandfather has suffered from high blood pressure for a long time.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ɡʁɑ̃.pɛʁ sufʁ di.pɛʁ.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃ də.pɥi lɔ̃.tɑ̃
items.notes: "hypertension" commence par un h muet suivi d'un y.

items.fr: Cette blessure a laissé une cicatrice profonde.
items.en: This wound left a deep scar.
items.ipa: sɛt ble.syʁ a lɛ.se yn si.ka.tʁis pʁɔ.fɔ̃d
items.notes: "laissé" prend deux s pour garder le son sifflant.

items.fr: Le radiologue examine attentivement la radiographie.
items.en: The radiologist carefully examines the X-ray.
items.ipa: lə ʁa.djɔ.lɔɡ ɛɡ.za.min a.tɑ̃.tiv.mɑ̃ la ʁa.djɔ.ɡʁa.fi
items.notes: "radiologue" se termine par gue, pas par g seul.

items.fr: Elle porte des béquilles depuis son opération au genou.
items.en: She has used crutches since her knee surgery.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁt de be.kij də.pɥi sɔ̃.n‿ɔ.pe.ʁa.sjɔ̃ o ʒə.nu
items.notes: "béquilles" prend un accent aigu sur le premier e.

items.fr: Nous suivons les conseils du médecin traitant.
items.en: We follow the advice of our family doctor.
items.ipa: nu sɥi.vɔ̃ le kɔ̃.sɛj dy med.sɛ̃ tʁɛ.tɑ̃
items.notes: "conseils" prend un e après le s, souvent oublié.

items.fr: L'enfant a une otite qui le fait beaucoup souffrir.
items.en: The child has an ear infection that hurts a lot.
items.ipa: lɑ̃.fɑ̃ a yn ɔ.tit ki lə fɛ bo.ku sufʁiʁ
items.notes: "otite" ne prend qu'un seul t.

items.fr: Le sparadrap ne tient pas bien sur la peau mouillée.
items.en: The adhesive bandage does not stick well to wet skin.
items.ipa: lə spa.ʁa.dʁa nə tjɛ̃ pa bjɛ̃ syʁ la po mu.je
items.notes: le p final de "sparadrap" ne se prononce pas.

items.fr: Elle a rendez-vous à l'hôpital pour une échographie.
items.en: She has an appointment at the hospital for an ultrasound.
items.ipa: ɛl a ʁɑ̃.de.vu a lo.pi.tal puʁ yn e.kɔ.ɡʁa.fi
items.notes: "hôpital" prend un accent circonflexe qui remplace un ancien s.

items.fr: Le patient tousse et se mouche toute la journée.
items.en: The patient coughs and blows his nose all day.
items.ipa: lə pa.sjɑ̃ tus e sə muʃ tut la ʒuʁ.ne
items.notes: "tousse" prend deux s pour garder le son sifflant.

items.fr: Ce médicament peut provoquer des étourdissements.
items.notes: "étourdissements" prend deux s au milieu du mot.

items.fr: L'infirmier change le pansement tous les deux jours.
items.en: The nurse changes the bandage every two days.
items.ipa: lɛ̃.fiʁ.mje ʃɑ̃ʒ lə pɑ̃s.mɑ̃ tu le dø ʒuʁ
items.notes: "infirmier" se termine en ier, sans e final au masculin.

items.fr: Elle a une intolérance au lactose depuis son enfance.
items.en: She has had a lactose intolerance since childhood.
items.ipa: ɛl a yn ɛ̃.tɔ.le.ʁɑ̃s o lak.toz də.pɥi sɔ̃.n‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃s
items.notes: "intolérance" prend un accent aigu sur le deuxième e.

items.fr: Le médecin recommande du repos et beaucoup de sommeil.
items.en: The doctor recommends rest and plenty of sleep.
items.ipa: lə med.sɛ̃ ʁə.kɔ.mɑ̃d dy ʁə.po e bo.ku də sɔ.mɛj
items.notes: "recommande" prend deux m, une erreur fréquente.

items.fr: Nous devons renouveler l'ordonnance avant la fin du mois.
items.en: We must renew the prescription before the end of the month.
items.ipa: nu də.vɔ̃ ʁə.nu.vle lɔʁ.dɔ.nɑ̃s a.vɑ̃ la fɛ̃ dy mwa
items.notes: "renouveler" perd son e muet à certaines formes conjuguées, mais pas à l'infinitif.

items.ipa: lə ba.lɔ̃ de zɑ̃.fɑ̃ ɛ vjɔ.lɛ

items.notes: "Rouge" adds an s to agree with the plural "chaussures".

items.fr: Les fleurs des champs sont violettes.
items.ipa: le flœʁ de ʃɑ̃ sɔ̃ vjɔ.lɛt

"Orange" does not take an s in the plural.

The plain form, and the t at the end is silent.
The noun is feminine, so the colour adds an e. Here you HEAR it: the sleeping t wakes up.

Feminine and plural, so both endings are there. It sounds exactly like the singular verte.
The plain form.
The e is there in writing and changes nothing in the sound. This is the spelling learners refuse to believe.
Still the same sound. Nothing in this sentence tells your ear it is plural except the words around it.
Two endings written, neither of them said. All four bleu sentences sound identical on the colour.
The plain form, and the only form there is.
No e. Marron is a chestnut being used as a colour, and a noun borrowed this way keeps its own shape.
No s either. Writing marrons here would be the one error a French reader always notices.
Feminine and plural and still unchanged. All four marron sentences are spelled the same way.

items.en: Use partitive articles for unspecified quantities: du (masculine), de la (feminine), des (plural).

Any hotel. The listener does not yet know which one, and does not need to.

items.en: I am looking for a hotel.
items.notes: First mention. Un opens the question rather than pointing at an answer.
Second mention. Both people now know which hotel, so le takes over.
The room was introduced one line ago, so it is the room now.
The final “d” in “grand” stays silent when nothing follows it.
The plural “grands” still sounds like singular “grand”, the s stays silent.
The feminine of “beau” is the irregular form “belle”.
“grand” takes a feminine e to agree with “table”.

items.fr: Il a mangé ses croissants avec sa sœur.

items.fr: La cloche sonne à huit heures.
items.en: The bell rings at eight o'clock.
items.notes: liaison obligatoire entre "huit" et "heures", on entend un t.
"queue" s'écrit avec q, u, e, u, e, une orthographe piège.

items.fr: Mon ami répond à la question.
items.notes: "répond" se termine par un d muet, comme le nom "réponse".

items.fr: Le professeur pose une question facile.
items.en: The teacher asks an easy question.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ poz yn kɛs.tjɔ̃ fa.sil
items.notes: "question" contient qu suivi de e, pas de son u audible.

items.fr: La maîtresse montre l'image aux élèves.
items.en: The teacher shows the picture to the students.
items.notes: "aux" est la contraction de "à les", le x final est muet.

items.fr: Les élèves trouvent la bonne réponse.
items.en: The students find the right answer.
items.notes: "réponse" prend un accent aigu sur le premier e.
"perd" se termine par un d muet, comme "attend".
"dictionnaire" prend deux n, une erreur fréquente à l'écrit.

items.fr: Vous copiez la phrase au tableau.
items.en: You copy the sentence on the board.
items.ipa: vu kɔ.pje la fʁaz o ta.blo
items.notes: le verbe "copier" garde le i devant le e du -ez.
"poésie" prend un accent aigu, pas de tréma sur le e.
le verbe "épeler" double le l devant un e muet.
"colorie" ne prend pas d'accent, attention à ne pas ajouter de e.
"découpe" prend un accent aigu sur le premier e.

items.fr: Nous collons les images dans le cahier.
items.en: We glue the pictures in the notebook.
items.ipa: nu kɔ.lɔ̃ le.zi.maʒ dɑ̃ lə ka.je
items.notes: "collons" prend deux l, comme le verbe "coller".
"effacez" prend deux f, une erreur fréquente à l'écrit.

items.fr: Le professeur souligne le mot important.
items.en: The teacher underlines the important word.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ su.liɲ lə mo ɛ̃.pɔʁ.tɑ̃
items.notes: le gn de "souligne" fait un seul son, comme dans "montagne".

items.fr: La maîtresse entoure la bonne réponse.
items.en: The teacher circles the right answer.
items.ipa: la mɛ.tʁɛs ɑ̃.tuʁ la bɔn ʁe.pɔ̃s
items.notes: "entoure" commence par en, pas par an, malgré le même son.

items.en: The students wait for the bell.
items.notes: "attendent" prend deux t, comme le mot "attente".

items.en: We go up to the classroom.
items.notes: "montons" se termine par -ons, ne pas écrire -ont.

items.en: You go down to the yard.
items.notes: "descendez" prend un c avant le s, verbe descendre.
"sortent" se termine par -ent muet au pluriel.
ne pas confondre "entrent" (verbe) et "entre" (préposition).
"couloir" ne prend pas de e après le u.
ne pas confondre "cours" (verbe courir) et "cour" (le lieu).
"récréation" contient deux fois la lettre r, facile d'en oublier une.
"dort" se termine par un t muet, verbe dormir.

items.en: We have a snack at ten o'clock.
items.notes: "goûtons" prend un accent circonflexe sur le u.

items.fr: Vous buvez de l'eau à la fontaine.
items.en: You drink water at the fountain.
items.ipa: vu by.ve də lo a la fɔ̃.tɛn
items.notes: ne pas confondre "eau" (trois lettres pour un seul son) et "au".

items.en: The children eat a piece of fruit.
items.notes: "mangent" garde le e après le g pour conserver le son doux.
"dessine" prend deux s pour garder le son [s].

items.en: The teacher writes her first name.
items.notes: "écrit" se termine par un t muet.
"apprennent" prend deux n devant le e muet.

items.fr: Nous comptons les jours de la semaine.
items.en: We count the days of the week.
items.ipa: nu kɔ̃.tɔ̃ le ʒuʁ də la sə.mɛn
items.notes: "comptons" garde le p muet avant le t, comme dans "compte".

items.fr: Vous cherchez un mot dans le dictionnaire.
items.en: You look for a word in the dictionary.
items.ipa: vu ʃɛʁ.ʃe œ̃ mo dɑ̃ lə dik.sjɔ.nɛʁ
items.notes: "cherchez" prend ch au début et au milieu du mot.

items.fr: J'allume la lumière de la classe.
items.en: I turn on the classroom light.
items.ipa: ʒa.lym la ly.mjɛʁ də la klas
items.notes: "allume" prend deux l, verbe allumer.

items.fr: Tu éteins la lumière du couloir.
items.en: You turn off the hallway light.
items.ipa: ty e.tɛ̃ la ly.mjɛʁ dy ku.lwaʁ
items.notes: "éteins" se termine par un s muet.

items.fr: Il porte son sac sur le dos.
items.en: He carries his bag on his back.
items.ipa: il pɔʁt sɔ̃ sak syʁ lə do
items.notes: "sac à dos" s'écrit en trois mots avec un accent sur le à.

items.fr: Elle met son manteau avant de sortir.
items.en: She puts on her coat before going out.
items.ipa: ɛl mɛ sɔ̃ mɑ̃.to a.vɑ̃ də sɔʁ.tiʁ
items.notes: "met" se termine par un t muet, verbe mettre.

items.fr: Nous enlevons nos chaussures dans la classe.
items.en: We take off our shoes in the classroom.
items.ipa: nu.z‿ɑ̃.lə.vɔ̃ no ʃo.syʁ dɑ̃ la klas
items.notes: "chaussures" prend deux s au milieu du mot.

items.fr: Vous nettoyez le tableau après le cours.
items.en: You clean the board after class.
items.ipa: vu nɛ.twa.je lə ta.blo a.pʁɛ lə kuʁ
items.notes: "nettoyez" prend deux t, verbe nettoyer.

items.fr: Les élèves essuient le tableau blanc.
items.notes: "essuient" prend deux s pour garder le son [s].

items.fr: Le directeur salue les élèves le matin.
items.en: The principal greets the students in the morning.
items.ipa: lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ sa.ly le.ze.lɛv lə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: "salue" ne prend pas de e à la fin.

items.fr: La maîtresse sourit à la classe.
items.en: The teacher smiles at the class.
items.ipa: la mɛ.tʁɛs su.ʁi a la klas
items.notes: "sourit" se termine par un t muet, verbe sourire.
"applaudissent" prend deux p, verbe applaudir.

items.fr: Nous nous lavons les mains avant le repas.
items.en: We wash our hands before the meal.
items.ipa: nu nu la.vɔ̃ le mɛ̃ a.vɑ̃ lə ʁə.pa
items.notes: "mains" prend un s au pluriel qui ne se prononce pas.

items.fr: Vous demandez la permission de sortir.
items.en: You ask for permission to go out.
items.ipa: vu də.mɑ̃.de la pɛʁ.mi.sjɔ̃ də sɔʁ.tiʁ
items.notes: "permission" prend deux s, une erreur fréquente.
"difficile" prend deux f et un seul c.
"corriges" prend deux r, verbe corriger.

items.fr: Il dicte une phrase à la classe.
items.en: He dictates a sentence to the class.
items.ipa: il dikt yn fʁaz a la klas
items.notes: "dicte" ne prend pas de e après le t.

items.en: The students copy the lesson again.
items.notes: "leçon" prend une cédille sous le c devant le o.
"nouveaux" prend un x au pluriel, pas un s.

items.fr: Vous soulignez le verbe dans la phrase.
items.en: You underline the verb in the sentence.
items.ipa: vu su.li.ɲe lə vɛʁb dɑ̃ la fʁaz
items.notes: "soulignez" contient le son gn comme dans "montagne".
"appelle" prend deux p et deux l.
"présents" prend un accent aigu sur le premier e.

items.fr: Les élèves lèvent le doigt pour répondre.
items.en: The students raise their finger to answer.
items.ipa: le.ze.lɛv lɛv lə dwa puʁ ʁe.pɔ̃dʁ
items.notes: ne pas oublier le t muet à la fin de "doigt".

items.fr: Nous rangeons nos affaires dans le sac.
items.en: We put our things away in the bag.
items.ipa: nu ʁɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ no.za.fɛʁ dɑ̃ lə sak
items.notes: "rangeons" garde le e après le g pour le son doux.

items.fr: Vous partagez votre livre avec un ami.
items.en: You share your book with a friend.
items.notes: "partagez" garde le a avant le g, verbe partager.

items.fr: Les enfants retrouvent leurs parents à la sortie de l'école.
items.en: The children meet their parents at the school exit.
items.ipa: le.zɑ̃.fɑ̃ ʁə.tʁuv lœʁ pa.ʁɑ̃ a la sɔʁ.ti də le.kɔl
items.notes: "retrouvent" se termine par -ent muet au pluriel.
"classeur" prend deux s comme le mot "classe".

items.fr: La maîtresse range ses craies dans la boîte.
items.en: The teacher puts her chalk away in the box.
items.ipa: la mɛ.tʁɛs ʁɑ̃ʒ se kʁɛ dɑ̃ la bwat
items.notes: "boîte" prend un accent circonflexe sur le i.
"posent" se termine par -ent muet au pluriel.

items.fr: Nous fermons nos cahiers avant de partir.
items.en: We close our notebooks before leaving.
items.ipa: nu fɛʁ.mɔ̃ no ka.je a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ
items.notes: "cahiers" contient un h muet, facile à oublier.

items.fr: Vous ouvrez vos livres à la page dix.
items.en: You open your books to page ten.
items.ipa: vu.z‿u.vʁe vo livʁ a la paʒ dis
items.notes: "ouvrez" ne prend pas d'accent malgré le son entendu.

items.fr: Les élèves vont réciter leur poésie demain.
items.en: The students are going to recite their poem tomorrow.
items.ipa: le.ze.lɛv vɔ̃ ʁe.si.te lœʁ pɔ.e.zi də.mɛ̃
items.notes: "poésie" prend un accent aigu, pas de tréma sur le e.

items.fr: Je vais chercher un livre à la bibliothèque.
items.en: I am going to look for a book at the library.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ ʃɛʁ.ʃe œ̃ livʁ a la bi.bli.jɔ.tɛk
items.notes: "bibliothèque" prend un h après le t, souvent oublié.

items.fr: Tu vas montrer ton dessin à la classe.
items.en: You are going to show your drawing to the class.
items.ipa: ty va mɔ̃.tʁe tɔ̃ de.sɛ̃ a la klas
items.notes: "montrer" à l'infinitif se termine par -er, sans t final.

items.fr: Il va corriger son exercice ce soir.
items.en: He is going to correct his exercise tonight.
items.ipa: il va kɔ.ʁi.ʒe sɔ̃.n‿ɛg.zɛʁ.sis sə swaʁ
items.notes: "exercice" prend un x, pas cs, et un seul c au milieu.

items.fr: Elle va lever la main pendant le cours.
items.en: She is going to raise her hand during class.
items.ipa: ɛl va lə.ve la mɛ̃ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ lə kuʁ
items.notes: "pendant" se termine par -ant, à ne pas confondre avec -ent.

items.fr: Nous allons ranger la salle de classe.
items.en: We are going to tidy up the classroom.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.ʒe la sal də klas
items.notes: "salle" prend deux l, ne pas confondre avec "sale".

items.fr: Vous allez apprendre une nouvelle leçon.
items.en: You are going to learn a new lesson.
items.notes: "nouvelle" prend deux l au féminin.

items.fr: Ils vont recopier la phrase au tableau.
items.en: They are going to copy the sentence on the board again.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ ʁə.kɔ.pje la fʁaz o ta.blo
items.notes: "recopier" commence par re, comme "refaire".

items.fr: Elles vont écouter la maîtresse attentivement.
items.en: They are going to listen to the teacher carefully.
items.notes: "attentivement" prend deux t et un seul m à la fin.

items.fr: Le professeur va donner les résultats demain.
items.en: The teacher is going to give the results tomorrow.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ va dɔ.ne le ʁe.zyl.ta də.mɛ̃
items.notes: "résultats" prend un t final muet et un s au pluriel.

items.fr: La maîtresse va coller les images au mur.
items.en: The teacher is going to stick the pictures on the wall.
items.ipa: la mɛ.tʁɛs va kɔ.le le.zi.maʒ o myʁ
items.notes: "coller" prend deux l comme "collons".

items.fr: Les élèves vont ranger leurs affaires ensemble.
items.en: The students are going to put their things away together.
items.notes: "ensemble" se termine par -mble, attention à l'ordre des lettres.

items.fr: Nous allons chanter une nouvelle chanson demain.
items.en: We are going to sing a new song tomorrow.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ ʃɑ̃.te yn nu.vɛl ʃɑ̃.sɔ̃ də.mɛ̃
items.notes: "chanson" et "chanter" partagent la même racine mais des terminaisons différentes.

items.fr: Vous allez ouvrir vos cahiers de français.
items.en: You are going to open your French notebooks.
items.ipa: vu.z‿a.le u.vʁiʁ vo ka.je də fʁɑ̃.sɛ
items.notes: "ouvrir" est un infinitif en -ir, sans terminaison -ez.

items.fr: Le directeur va parler aux parents ce soir.
items.en: The principal is going to speak to the parents tonight.
items.ipa: lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ va paʁ.le o paʁ.ɑ̃ sə swaʁ
items.notes: "aux" remplace "à les", le x final est muet.

items.fr: Les enfants vont goûter à dix heures.
items.en: The children are going to have a snack at ten o'clock.
items.notes: "goûter" prend un accent circonflexe sur le u, comme "goûtons".

items.fr: La classe va commencer dans cinq minutes.
items.en: Class is going to start in five minutes.
items.ipa: la klas va kɔ.mɑ̃.se dɑ̃ sɛ̃k mi.nyt
items.notes: "commencer" prend deux m mais un seul c au début.

items.fr: Nous n'avons pas de fruits frais.
items.en: We do not have any fresh fruit.
items.ipa: nu na.vɔ̃ pa də fʁɥi fʁɛ
items.notes: "frais" ends in a silent s, homophone trap with "frai".

« à + le » devient toujours « au » : au collège.

items.en: She has a red pencil case.

Très courant à l'oral, entre élèves.
Elision: l' before a vowel.
The group of pupils or the lesson itself.
The room where lessons happen.
Often shortened to le prof.
Same form for boys and girls: l'élève.
Feminine: l'étudiante.
Head of the school.
Feminine of le directeur.
Also: le camarade de classe.
Where pupils eat lunch.
Short for la cour de récréation.
Place for borrowing books.
Hallway between classrooms.
Everyday writing pen.

Rubber for erasing pencil.
Do not confuse with la livre, the pound.
Also means the rule.
Literally: bag for the back.
Whiteboard or blackboard at the front of class.
Used on a blackboard.
Also means the leaf.
The material; a single sheet is la feuille.
Pupil's table in class.
Everyday chair.
Also means the office.
Always plural in French.

Handy cognate.
Often shortened to l'ordi.
Note the cedilla: ç.
Usually plural: faire ses devoirs.
A practice task in class.

Je lis, tu lis, il lit.
J'écris, tu écris, il écrit.
Regular -er verb; no preposition needed: écouter le professeur.
J'apprends le français.
Regular -er verb.
A student's weekly class schedule.
The school bell that marks the start and end of class.
Where students store their books at school.
A first draft before the final copy.
The sheet a student hands in to be graded.
A mark out of 20 in French schools.
Often shortened to l'exam in casual speech.
The school report with grades and comments.
