items.notes: Back to school in September, a big moment in France.
Always plural in French.
False friend: not a university. French pupils attend le collège from about 11 to 15.
The school before university, from about 15 to 18.
School for children from about 3 to 6, before primary school.
School from about 6 to 11, between la maternelle and le collège.
Used in primary school. In secondary school the word is le professeur.
Feminine of le maître. Children say maîtresse when they call their teacher.
Watches over pupils outside class. Feminine: la surveillante.
Where pupils go when they feel sick at school.
The indoor sports hall for physical education classes.
The classroom with computers.
A marker pen, often used for drawing or writing on a whiteboard.
From surligner, to highlight text.
From tailler, to sharpen, plus crayon.
The math tool for drawing circles, not the one for finding north.
The triangle-shaped ruler used in geometry.
Allowed in some math classes, forbidden in others.
Le manuel scolaire is the schoolbook for a subject.
A small board pupils write on with chalk or a marker, then wipe clean.
A class test: on a un contrôle de maths demain.

items.en: to revise, to study for a test
items.notes: Je révise mes leçons avant le contrôle.

Looks like the English word, but the ending sounds like graf.
Used for any written passage you read in class.
Ch sounds like sh in French.
The g is soft, like the s in measure.
In school this means a summary of a text, not a CV.
Also the name of the school subject where you study poems.
French pupils often learn a poem by heart each month.
The fables of La Fontaine are classics in French schools.
Un conte de fées is a fairy tale.
The globe of the Earth used in geography class.
Used in art class, le cours de dessin.
Always plural on school supply lists.
A one day class trip, to a museum for example.
A longer trip with overnight stays, unlike la sortie scolaire.
Literally green class, a week of school in the countryside.
Staying with a family abroad while their child visits yours.
A woman is la remplaçante.
Parents must explain une absence with a written note.
For a girl or woman, être absente.
What you answer at roll call in the morning.
What you do before speaking in class.
Uses prendre, to take, just like in English.
Ses changes with the person: je fais mes devoirs.
Same image as English, learning with the heart.

items.en: to go up to the board
items.notes: Teachers call a pupil to the front to solve an exercise.
French grades usually go from 0 to 20.
Below 10 out of 20 counts as a bad grade in France.
To do the same school year again after failing it.
Réussir means to succeed, not to pass by walking.
English is the first foreign language in most French schools.
The teacher reads a text aloud and pupils write it down.
The final s is silent, singular and plural sound the same.
The French school year has three terms.
Avoir la moyenne means scoring at least 10 out of 20.
The little book where pupils write down their homework.
Rare in France, most public schools have no uniform.
A week of school in the mountains with ski lessons.
A classic punition is copying lines after class.
Le carnet de correspondance links teachers and parents.

items.fr: Les élèves écoutent attentivement la maîtresse.
items.en: The students listen attentively to the teacher.
items.notes: “maîtresse” keeps the circumflex from “maître”, even with the feminine ending.

items.fr: Il y a vingt élèves dans notre classe.
items.en: There are twenty students in our class.
items.ipa: il i a vɛ̃.t‿e.lɛv dɑ̃ nɔtʁ klas
items.notes: “vingt” keeps its silent g and t together when nothing follows it.

items.fr: Les cahiers rouges sont sur l'étagère du fond.
items.en: The red notebooks are on the back shelf.
items.ipa: le ka.je ʁuʒ sɔ̃ syʁ le.ta.ʒɛʁ dy fɔ̃
items.notes: “rouges” takes a plural s to agree with “cahiers”, though the sound doesn't change.

items.fr: Est-ce que la récréation commence bientôt ?
items.ipa: ɛs kə la ʁe.kʁe.a.sjɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃s bjɛ̃.to

example.en: In class, we study math every morning.
example.fr: En classe, nous étudions les mathématiques tous les matins.

example.en: French is my favorite subject.
example.fr: Le français est ma matière préférée.

example.en: History class starts at ten o'clock.
example.fr: L'histoire commence à dix heures.

example.en: We are learning the geography of Europe.
example.fr: Nous apprenons la géographie de l'Europe.

example.en: Science is interesting this year.
example.fr: Les sciences sont intéressantes cette année.

example.en: Physics requires a lot of concentration.
example.fr: La physique demande beaucoup de concentration.

example.en: The chemistry teacher wears a white coat.
example.fr: Le professeur de chimie porte une blouse blanche.

example.en: In biology, we study plants.
example.fr: En biologie, nous étudions les plantes.

example.en: I have an English class on Monday.
example.fr: J'ai un cours d'anglais le lundi.

example.en: She has been learning Spanish for two years.
example.fr: Elle apprend l'espagnol depuis deux ans.

example.en: Music class is on Friday.
example.fr: Le cours de musique est le vendredi.

example.en: Art class lets you draw and paint.
example.fr: Les arts plastiques permettent de dessiner et de peindre.

example.en: Physical education takes place at the gym.
example.fr: L'éducation physique a lieu au gymnase.

example.fr: Nous apprenons l'informatique une fois par semaine.

example.en: French grammar is sometimes difficult.
example.fr: La grammaire française est parfois difficile.

example.en: He makes a lot of spelling mistakes.
example.fr: Il fait beaucoup de fautes d'orthographe.

example.en: Conjugating irregular verbs is complicated.
example.fr: La conjugaison des verbes irréguliers est compliquée.

example.en: I learn ten vocabulary words every day.
example.fr: J'apprends dix mots de vocabulaire chaque jour.

example.fr: La rédaction doit faire deux pages.

example.en: In geometry, we draw triangles.
example.fr: En géométrie, on dessine des triangles.

example.en: The principal meets parents in his office.
example.fr: Le proviseur reçoit les parents dans son bureau.

example.en: The principal speaks to the students in the yard.
example.fr: La proviseure parle aux élèves dans la cour.

example.en: The caretaker opens the doors in the morning.
example.fr: Le concierge ouvre les portes le matin.

example.en: My tutor helps me with math.
example.fr: Mon tuteur m'aide en mathématiques.

example.en: My tutor comes twice a week.
example.fr: Ma tutrice vient deux fois par semaine.

example.en: The class representative speaks on behalf of the students.
example.fr: Le délégué de classe parle au nom des élèves.

example.en: The class representative organizes the meeting.
example.fr: La déléguée de classe organise la réunion.

example.en: Put your papers in the blue binder.
example.fr: Mets tes feuilles dans le classeur bleu.

example.en: The folder holds all my documents.
example.fr: La pochette contient tous mes documents.

example.en: He always writes with a fountain pen.
example.fr: Il écrit toujours avec un stylo-plume.

example.en: The red marker doesn't work anymore.
example.fr: Le marqueur rouge ne fonctionne plus.

example.en: Attach the sheets with a paperclip.
example.fr: Attache les feuilles avec un trombone.

example.en: The stapler is on the teacher's desk.
example.fr: L'agrafeuse est sur le bureau du professeur.

example.en: We are looking at a cell under the microscope.
example.fr: Nous observons une cellule au microscope.

example.en: The wall map shows the countries of the world.
example.fr: La carte murale montre les pays du monde.

example.en: The classroom clock is slow.
example.fr: L'horloge de la classe est en retard.

example.en: The teacher turns on the projector.
example.fr: Le professeur allume le vidéoprojecteur.

example.en: Students wait under the covered area when it rains.
example.fr: Les élèves attendent sous le préau quand il pleut.

example.en: The sports field is behind the school.
example.fr: Le terrain de sport est derrière l'école.

example.en: Swimming class takes place at the pool.
example.fr: Le cours de natation a lieu à la piscine.

example.en: Teachers gather in the staff room.
example.fr: Les enseignants se réunissent dans la salle des professeurs.

example.en: Go to the office for your certificate.
example.fr: Va au secrétariat pour ton certificat.

example.en: Students change shoes in the locker room.
example.fr: Les élèves changent de chaussures dans le vestiaire.

example.en: The restrooms are at the end of the hallway.
example.fr: Les toilettes sont au fond du couloir.

example.en: The experiment is done in the laboratory.
example.fr: L'expérience se fait dans le laboratoire.

example.en: Students without class go to study hall.
example.fr: Les élèves sans cours vont en permanence.

example.en: I do my homework in the study room.
example.fr: Je fais mes devoirs à la salle d'étude.

example.en: Education is free in this country.
example.fr: L'éducation est gratuite dans ce pays.

example.en: Language teaching starts early.
example.fr: L'enseignement des langues commence tôt.

example.en: Learning to read takes time.
example.fr: L'apprentissage de la lecture prend du temps.

example.en: This training lasts six months.
example.fr: Cette formation dure six mois.

example.en: He has been studying at university since September.
example.fr: Il étudie à l'université depuis septembre.

example.en: The faculty of medicine is very large.
example.fr: La faculté de médecine est très grande.

example.en: The campus is near downtown.
example.fr: Le campus se trouve près du centre-ville.

example.en: Registration is done online this year.
example.fr: L'inscription se fait en ligne cette année.

example.en: Schooling is mandatory until age sixteen.
example.fr: La scolarité est obligatoire jusqu'à seize ans.

example.en: She received a scholarship for her studies.
example.fr: Elle a reçu une bourse pour ses études.

example.en: He displays his diploma in his office.
example.fr: Il affiche son diplôme dans son bureau.

example.en: The certificate proves you finished the course.
example.fr: Le certificat prouve que tu as terminé le cours.

example.en: The guidance counselor sees students this week.
example.fr: La conseillère d'orientation reçoit les élèves cette semaine.

example.en: We study every evening after dinner.
example.fr: Nous étudions chaque soir après le dîner.

example.en: She has been teaching French for ten years.
example.fr: Elle enseigne le français depuis dix ans.

example.en: Can you explain the rule again?
example.fr: Peux-tu expliquer la règle encore une fois ?

example.en: I don't understand this sentence.
example.fr: Je ne comprends pas cette phrase.

example.en: The teacher grades the papers in the evening.
example.fr: Le professeur corrige les copies le soir.

example.en: He writes down each answer in his notebook.
example.fr: Il note chaque réponse sur son cahier.

example.en: The teacher is going to quiz three students today.
example.fr: Le professeur va interroger trois élèves aujourd'hui.

example.en: Don't copy off your neighbor.
example.fr: Ne copie pas sur ton voisin.

example.en: Underline the important words in red.
example.fr: Souligne les mots importants en rouge.

example.en: The young students like to color pictures.
example.fr: Les petits élèves aiment colorier des dessins.

example.en: She draws animals very well.
example.fr: Elle dessine très bien les animaux.

example.en: We calculate the result without a calculator.
example.fr: Nous calculons le résultat sans calculatrice.

example.en: Add these two numbers.
example.fr: Additionne ces deux nombres.

example.en: You have to subtract ten from twenty.
example.fr: Il faut soustraire dix de vingt.

example.en: Multiply six by seven.
example.fr: Multiplie six par sept.

example.en: Divide the class into small groups.
example.fr: Divise la classe en petits groupes.

example.en: I'm trying to memorize the poem for tomorrow.
example.fr: J'essaie de mémoriser le poème pour demain.

example.en: Each student must recite their text in front of the class.
example.fr: Chaque élève doit réciter son texte devant la classe.

example.en: Can you translate this sentence into English?
example.fr: Peux-tu traduire cette phrase en anglais ?

example.en: Spell your name, please.
example.fr: Épelle ton nom, s'il te plaît.

example.en: She pronounces difficult words well.
example.fr: Elle prononce bien les mots difficiles.

example.en: We discuss the topic in small groups.
example.fr: Nous discutons du sujet en petits groupes.

example.en: Stop chatting during class.
example.fr: Arrêtez de bavarder pendant le cours.

example.en: The students go quiet when the teacher comes in.
example.fr: Les élèves se taisent quand le professeur entre.

items.fr: Mon fils va à l'école demain.
items.en: My son is going to school tomorrow.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fis va a l‿e.kɔl də.mɛ̃

items.fr: Nous arrivons à l'école à neuf heures.
items.en: We arrive at school at nine o'clock.
items.ipa: nu a.ʁi.vɔ̃ a l‿e.kɔl a nœ.v‿œʁ

items.fr: Tu as un nouveau sac ce matin.
items.en: You have a new bag this morning.
items.ipa: ty a œ̃ nu.vo sak sə ma.tɛ̃

items.en: He is wearing his blue uniform.

items.fr: Elle range ses crayons dans la trousse.
items.en: She puts her pencils away in the pencil case.
items.ipa: ɛl ʁɑ̃ʒ se kʁɛ.jɔ̃ dɑ̃ la tʁus

items.fr: Le matin, je prends mon petit-déjeuner avant l'école.
items.en: In the morning, I have breakfast before school.
items.ipa: lə ma.tɛ̃ ʒə pʁɑ̃ mɔ̃ pə.ti de.ʒœ.ne a.vɑ̃ l‿e.kɔl

items.fr: Les enfants jouent dans la cour pendant la pause.
items.en: The children play in the yard during the break.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ʒu dɑ̃ la kuʁ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la poz

items.fr: Vous avez combien de cours aujourd'hui ?
items.en: How many classes do you have today?

items.fr: Mon fils apprend les chiffres en classe.
items.en: My son is learning numbers in class.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fis a.pʁɑ̃ le ʃi.fʁə ɑ̃ klas

items.fr: La maîtresse explique la leçon lentement.
items.en: The teacher explains the lesson slowly.
items.ipa: la mɛ.tʁɛs ɛk.spli.k la lə.sɔ̃ lɑ̃t.mɑ̃

items.fr: Le vendredi, nous avons un cours de musique.
items.en: On Fridays, we have a music class.
items.ipa: lə vɑ̃.dʁə.di nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿œ̃ kuʁ də my.zik

items.fr: Elle dessine un chat sur sa feuille.
items.en: She draws a cat on her sheet of paper.
items.ipa: ɛl de.sin œ̃ ʃa syʁ sa fœj

items.fr: Nous mangeons à la cantine à midi.
items.en: We eat at the cafeteria at noon.
items.ipa: nu mɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ a la kɑ̃.tin a mi.di

items.fr: Le professeur pose une question facile.
items.en: The teacher asks an easy question.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fe.sœʁ poz yn kɛs.tjɔ̃ fa.sil

items.fr: Je lève la main pour répondre.
items.en: I raise my hand to answer.
items.ipa: ʒə lɛv la mɛ̃ puʁ ʁe.pɔ̃.dʁ

items.fr: Mon fils oublie souvent son cahier.
items.en: My son often forgets his notebook.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fis u.bli su.vɑ̃ sɔ̃ ka.je

items.fr: Elle porte son sac à dos tous les jours.
items.en: She wears her backpack every day.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁt sɔ̃ sak a do tu le ʒuʁ

items.fr: Les élèves rentrent en classe après la récréation.
items.en: The students go back to class after recess.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ʁɑ̃tʁ ɑ̃ klas a.pʁɛ la ʁe.kʁe.a.sjɔ̃

items.fr: Le bus scolaire arrive à sept heures et demie.
items.en: The school bus arrives at half past seven.
items.ipa: lə bys sko.lɛʁ a.ʁiv a sɛ.t‿œʁ e də.mi

items.en: I wait for my son in front of the school.

items.fr: Nous allons acheter des fournitures scolaires demain.
items.en: We are going to buy school supplies tomorrow.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ a.ʃə.te de fuʁ.ni.tyʁ sko.lɛʁ də.mɛ̃

items.fr: Mon fils commence l'école primaire cette année.
items.en: My son is starting elementary school this year.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fis kɔ.mɑ̃s l‿e.kɔl pʁi.mɛʁ sɛt a.ne

items.fr: La rentrée scolaire est le premier septembre.
items.en: The start of the school year is September first.
items.ipa: la ʁɑ̃.tʁe sko.lɛʁ ɛ lə pʁə.mje sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ

items.fr: Je signe le carnet de mon fils chaque soir.
items.en: I sign my son's notebook every evening.
items.ipa: ʒə siɲ lə kaʁ.nɛ də mɔ̃ fis ʃak swaʁ

items.fr: Elle finit ses devoirs avant le dîner.
items.en: She finishes her homework before dinner.
items.ipa: ɛl fi.ni se də.vwaʁ a.vɑ̃ lə di.ne

items.fr: Le directeur accueille les nouveaux élèves.
items.en: The principal welcomes the new students.

items.fr: Nous choisissons une nouvelle école pour notre fille.
items.en: We are choosing a new school for our daughter.
items.ipa: nu ʃwa.zi.sɔ̃.z‿yn nu.vɛl e.kɔl puʁ nɔtʁ fij

items.fr: Le professeur écrit la date au tableau.
items.en: The teacher writes the date on the board.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fe.sœʁ e.kʁi la dat o ta.blo

items.fr: Les élèves rangent leurs affaires avant de partir.
items.en: The students put their things away before leaving.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ʁɑ̃ʒ lœʁ.z‿a.fɛʁ a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ

items.fr: Ma fille adore lire des histoires.
Il faut arriver à l'école avant huit heures.
items.en: You have to arrive at school before eight o'clock.
items.ipa: il fo a.ʁi.ve a l‿e.kɔl a.vɑ̃ ɥi.t‿œʁ

items.fr: Nous préparons le sac d'école ce soir.
items.en: We are getting the school bag ready tonight.
items.ipa: nu pʁe.pa.ʁɔ̃ lə sak de.kɔl sə swaʁ

items.fr: Elle demande la permission de sortir.
items.en: She asks for permission to go out.
items.ipa: ɛl də.mɑ̃d la pɛʁ.mi.sjɔ̃ də sɔʁ.tiʁ

items.fr: Mon fils participe à un club de sport.
items.en: My son takes part in a sports club.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fis paʁ.ti.sip a œ̃ klœb də spɔʁ

items.fr: Le cours d'anglais commence à dix heures.
items.en: English class starts at ten o'clock.
items.ipa: lə kuʁ dɑ̃.glɛ kɔ.mɑ̃s a di.z‿œʁ

items.fr: Je vérifie l'emploi du temps de ma fille.
items.ipa: ʒə ve.ʁi.fi l‿ɑ̃.plwa dy tɑ̃ də ma fij

items.fr: Les parents rencontrent le professeur ce jeudi.
items.en: The parents are meeting the teacher this Thursday.
items.ipa: le pa.ʁɑ̃ ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃tʁ lə pʁɔ.fe.sœʁ sə ʒø.di

items.fr: Elle aime dessiner pendant les pauses.
items.en: She likes to draw during breaks.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛm de.si.ne pɑ̃.dɑ̃ le poz

items.fr: Nous inscrivons notre fils à l'école du quartier.
items.en: We are enrolling our son at the neighborhood school.
items.ipa: nu.z‿ɛ̃.skʁi.vɔ̃ nɔtʁ fis a l‿e.kɔl dy kaʁ.tje

items.fr: Elle a une gomme rose dans sa trousse.
items.en: She has a pink eraser in her pencil case.
items.ipa: ɛl a yn gɔm ʁoz dɑ̃ sa tʁus
items.notes: Homophone trap: "a" (verb avoir) has no accent, unlike "à" (preposition).
Liaison on "deux stylos"; plural s on "stylos" and "bleus" is silent.

items.fr: Ses crayons sont dans le tiroir.
items.en: Her pencils are in the drawer.
items.ipa: se kʁɛ.jɔ̃ sɔ̃ dɑ̃ lə ti.ʁwaʁ
items.notes: "Ses" (possessive) sounds like "ces" and "c'est", easy to mix up when writing from dictation.

items.fr: Il fait ses devoirs après l'école.
items.en: He does his homework after school.
items.ipa: il fɛ se də.vwaʁ a.pʁɛ l‿e.kɔl
items.notes: "Fait" ends in a silent t, do not write "fais".
"C'est" versus "s'est", a classic homophone trap.

items.fr: Ils vont à la cantine ensemble.
items.en: They go to the cafeteria together.
items.notes: Liaison between "vont" and "à"; the final t of "vont" is normally silent.

items.fr: On apprend les couleurs en classe.
items.en: We learn the colors in class.
items.notes: "On" versus "ont", sound identical but spelled differently.

items.fr: Elle a six ans et demi.
items.en: She is six and a half years old.
items.notes: "Six" liaises to /siz/ before a vowel; do not forget the z sound in writing the liaison mentally, only the letters stay the same.

items.fr: Les enfants ont beaucoup de devoirs.
items.en: The children have a lot of homework.
items.notes: "Beaucoup" has a silent final p.

items.fr: Il est cinq heures et demie.
items.notes: "Cinq" keeps its q sound in liaison before "heures", unlike before some other consonants.
Silent final letters in "tableau" and "blanc".

items.fr: Nous écrivons dans nos cahiers neufs.
items.en: We write in our new notebooks.
items.notes: Liaison on "nos cahiers"; "neufs" keeps its f sound but the plural s is silent.

items.fr: Elle prend son sac et son manteau.
items.en: She takes her bag and her coat.
items.ipa: ɛl pʁɑ̃ sɔ̃ sak e sɔ̃ mɑ̃.to
items.notes: "Et" versus "est", same sound, different spelling and meaning.
"Aujourd'hui" has an unusual spelling with a silent d and an apostrophe.

items.fr: Il y a vingt-cinq enfants dans la classe.
items.en: There are twenty-five children in the class.
items.ipa: i.l‿i a vɛ̃t.sɛ̃.k‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ dɑ̃ la klas
items.notes: Compound number "vingt-cinq" needs a hyphen.

items.fr: Nous allons à la bibliothèque cet après-midi.
items.en: We are going to the library this afternoon.
items.notes: "Cet" (not "ce") is used before a word starting with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Elle met son cahier dans son sac.
items.en: She puts her notebook in her bag.
items.ipa: ɛl mɛ sɔ̃ ka.je dɑ̃ sɔ̃ sak
items.notes: "Met" ends in a silent t.
"Doucement" ends in -ment but is pronounced /mɑ̃/, not spelled like it sounds.

items.fr: Mon crayon est sous la table.
items.en: My pencil is under the table.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ kʁɛ.jɔ̃ ɛ su la tablə
items.notes: "Est" versus "et", a very common homophone mistake.

items.fr: Les enfants vont chanter une chanson demain.
items.en: The children are going to sing a song tomorrow.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ vɔ̃ ʃɑ̃.te yn ʃɑ̃.sɔ̃ də.mɛ̃
items.notes: "Chanson" and "chanter" share the nasal "an" sound but different endings.

items.fr: Elle va apprendre un nouveau mot chaque jour.
items.en: She is going to learn a new word every day.
items.ipa: ɛl va.z‿a.pʁɑ̃dʁ œ̃ nu.vo mo ʃak ʒuʁ
items.notes: Liaison between "va" and "apprendre".

items.fr: Le tableau blanc est propre ce matin.
items.en: The whiteboard is clean this morning.
items.ipa: lə ta.blo blɑ̃ ɛ pʁɔpʁ sə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: Silent final consonants in "blanc" and "propre".

items.fr: Nous allons ranger la salle de classe.
items.en: We are going to tidy the classroom.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.ʒe la sal də klas
items.notes: "Allons" ends in a silent s, unlike the liaison sound before a vowel.

items.fr: Il porte un pull vert aujourd'hui.
items.en: He is wearing a green sweater today.
items.ipa: il pɔʁt œ̃ pyl vɛʁ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi
items.notes: "Pull" is a borrowed English word pronounced /pyl/, not like the English word.

items.fr: Les stylos rouges sont dans la boîte.
items.en: The red pens are in the box.
items.ipa: le sti.lo ʁuʒ sɔ̃ dɑ̃ la bwat
items.notes: Circumflex accent on "boîte", easy to forget.

items.fr: Elle va lire un livre pendant la pause.
items.en: She is going to read a book during the break.
items.ipa: ɛl va liʁ œ̃ livʁ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la poz
items.notes: Nasal sound in "un livre", do not add an extra n.

items.fr: On va faire un exercice de calcul.
items.en: We are going to do a math exercise.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ va fɛʁ œ̃.n‿ɛg.zɛʁ.sis də kal.kyl
items.notes: "Exercice" has an x pronounced /gz/ and a double c pronounced /s/.

items.fr: Le sac de mon fils est très lourd.
items.en: My son's bag is very heavy.
items.ipa: lə sak də mɔ̃ fis ɛ tʁɛ luʁ
items.notes: Silent final d in "lourd".

items.fr: Nous allons visiter une autre école.
items.en: We are going to visit another school.
items.notes: Liaison on "une autre" and "autre école".

items.fr: Elle écrit son prénom sur la feuille.
items.en: She writes her first name on the sheet of paper.
items.ipa: ɛl e.kʁi sɔ̃ pʁe.nɔ̃ syʁ la fœj
items.notes: "Écrit" ends in a silent t; "feuille" has the tricky -euille spelling.

items.fr: Le vendredi, on a cours de dessin.
items.en: On Fridays, we have art class.
items.ipa: lə vɑ̃.dʁə.di ɔ̃.n‿a kuʁ də de.sɛ̃
items.notes: "Vendredi" is often mispronounced with an extra vowel that shouldn't be written.

items.fr: Ils ont un exercice à faire ce soir.
items.en: They have an exercise to do tonight.
items.notes: "Ont" versus "on", homophone trap again with a different subject.

items.fr: Le maître explique le nouveau mot.
items.en: The teacher explains the new word.
items.ipa: lə mɛtʁ ɛk.splik lə nu.vo mo
items.notes: Circumflex accent on "maître", replacing an old silent s.

items.fr: La classe est calme pendant l'examen.
items.en: The class is quiet during the exam.
items.ipa: la klas ɛ kalm pɑ̃.dɑ̃ l‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃
items.notes: "Examen" ends in -men, not -min, even though it sounds nasal.

items.fr: Elle va poser une question au professeur.
items.en: She is going to ask the teacher a question.
items.ipa: ɛl va po.ze yn kɛs.tjɔ̃ o pʁɔ.fe.sœʁ
items.notes: "Question" has "qu" pronounced /k/, not /kw/.

items.en: We are going to count to one hundred.
items.notes: "Cent" sounds like "sans" and "sent"; the final t is silent.
Here "neuf" means "new", not the number nine, though spelled the same.

items.fr: Le stylo noir n'écrit plus bien.
items.en: The black pen doesn't write well anymore.
items.ipa: lə sti.lo nwaʁ ne.kʁi ply bjɛ̃
items.notes: The negation "n'" elides before the vowel of "écrit", easy to forget the apostrophe.

items.fr: Elle va chercher son sac à l'entrée.
items.en: She is going to get her bag at the entrance.
items.ipa: ɛl va ʃɛʁ.ʃe sɔ̃ sak a lɑ̃.tʁe
items.notes: "À l'entrée" needs the elided article "l'" before a vowel.

items.fr: On va apprendre les jours de la semaine.
items.en: We are going to learn the days of the week.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ va.z‿a.pʁɑ̃dʁ le ʒuʁ də la sə.mɛn
items.notes: Silent final s in "jours", only heard in liaison.
"Contents" agrees in the plural with a silent final s and t.

items.fr: Le professeur ferme la porte doucement.
items.en: The teacher closes the door quietly.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fe.sœʁ fɛʁm la pɔʁt dus.mɑ̃
items.notes: Several silent final e's in a row: "ferme", "porte".
Literally: to have hunger. J'ai faim = I am hungry.
Literally: to have thirst. J'ai soif = I am thirsty.
Avoir phrase: J'ai sommeil, I am sleepy.
Avoir phrase: J'ai froid, I am cold.
Avoir phrase: J'ai chaud, I am hot.
Avoir phrase: Tu as raison, you are right.
Avoir phrase: J'ai tort, I am wrong.
J'ai honte means I am ashamed. Uses avoir, not être.
“a” (from avoir) sounds like “à” but takes no accent here because it's the verb.

items.en: to feel like, to want to

items.fr: Nous avons faim après le travail.
Elle a chaud dans la salle d'attente.
items.en: She is hot in the waiting room.
items.ipa: ɛl a ʃo dɑ̃ la sal da.tɑ̃t

items.fr: Il a froid dans le bureau.
items.en: He is cold in the office.
items.ipa: il a fʁwa dɑ̃ lə by.ʁo
items.notes: "froid" se termine par un d muet, on ne l'entend pas

items.fr: Elle a soif pendant la marche.

items.fr: Mon beau-père tond la pelouse le matin.
items.en: My father-in-law mows the lawn in the morning.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ bo pɛʁ tɔ̃ la pə.luz lə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: « tond » vient de tondre, le d final est muet.

items.fr: Ma belle-mère range la cuisine après le repas.
items.en: My mother-in-law tidies the kitchen after the meal.
items.ipa: ma bɛl mɛʁ ʁɑ̃ʒ la kɥi.zin a.pʁɛ lə ʁə.pa
items.notes: Le s final de « repas » est muet.

items.fr: Mon beau-frère achète une nouvelle maison.
items.en: My brother-in-law is buying a new house.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ bo fʁɛʁ a.ʃɛt yn nu.vɛl mɛ.zɔ̃
items.notes: « achète » prend un accent grave, pas aigu.

items.fr: Ma belle-sœur attend un appel important.
items.en: My sister-in-law is waiting for an important call.
items.notes: « attend » prend deux t, comme la plupart des verbes en -attendre.
« filleul » se prononce fi-yeul, le double l fait le son y.

items.fr: Ma marraine envoie une carte pour Noël.
items.en: My godmother sends a card for Christmas.
items.ipa: ma ma.ʁɛn ɑ̃.vwa yn kaʁt puʁ nɔ.ɛl
items.notes: « Noël » prend un tréma sur le e pour séparer les deux sons.

items.fr: Mon parrain travaille dans une banque.
items.en: My godfather works at a bank.
items.notes: « parrain » prend deux r, contrairement à « parent ».

items.fr: Mes petits-enfants dessinent avec des crayons.
items.ipa: me pə.ti.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ de.sin a.vɛk de kʁɛ.jɔ̃
items.notes: « dessinent » garde deux s pour le son s dur, pas z.

items.fr: Mon arrière-grand-père fête ses quatre-vingt-dix ans.
items.en: My great-grandfather is celebrating his ninetieth birthday.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.n‿a.ʁjɛʁ gʁɑ̃ pɛʁ fɛt se ka.tʁə vɛ̃ dis ɑ̃
items.notes: « quatre-vingt-dix » s'écrit avec des traits d'union entre chaque mot.

items.fr: Nous préparons le repas pour toute la famille.
items.en: We are preparing the meal for the whole family.
items.ipa: nu pʁe.pa.ʁɔ̃ lə ʁə.pa puʁ tut la fa.mij
items.notes: « toute » s'accorde au féminin devant « famille ».

items.fr: Ma demi-sœur habite dans un petit village.
items.en: My half-sister lives in a small village.
items.ipa: ma də.mi sœʁ a.bit dɑ̃.z‿œ̃ pə.ti vi.laʒ
items.notes: « demi-sœur » garde un trait d'union, comme tous les mots composés avec demi-.

items.en: I have a present for Léa.
items.notes: ai. Said more often than the other five together, because most of what a beginner says is about themselves.

items.fr: Tu as un cadeau pour Léa ?
items.en: Do you have a present for Léa?
items.respell: tü ah uhⁿ ka-DOH poor lay-A
items.notes: as. Two letters, and the s is silent, so it sounds exactly like the a of il a.

items.fr: Il a un cadeau pour Léa.
items.en: He has a present for Léa.
items.respell: ee LA uhⁿ ka-DOH poor lay-A
items.notes: a. One letter, no accent on it, and the l of il runs straight into it.

items.fr: Nous avons un cadeau pour Léa.
items.en: We have a present for Léa.
items.respell: noo za-VOHⁿ uhⁿ ka-DOH poor lay-A
items.notes: avons, and the silent s of nous wakes up as a z in front of the vowel.

items.fr: Vous avez un cadeau pour Léa ?
items.en: Do you have a present for Léa?
items.respell: voo za-VAY uhⁿ ka-DOH poor lay-A
items.notes: avez, with the same join you already learned on vous êtes. One word out loud.

items.fr: Ils ont un cadeau pour Léa.
items.en: They have a present for Léa.
items.respell: eel ZOHⁿ uhⁿ ka-DOH poor lay-A
items.notes: ont, and the join makes a z. Ils sont opens on an s instead, and that is the whole difference.
Hunger, had. The English is "I am hungry" and there is no word for am anywhere in this sentence.
About the person. Il fait chaud is about the room, and the two are not interchangeable.
The rarest of the fourteen in this corpus: one row existed before this lesson, and it was the headword.
The question a French speaker asks before they open a window. The s of as is silent.
Avoir l'air is how French says somebody looks or seems. The corpus held no example of it at any level.
A real possession: one noun after the form, and no second verb behind it.

items.en: I do not have a car.
items.notes: Une became de. The same collapse you met on un, une and des one lesson ago.
Nothing collapsed, because faim never had a word in front of it. Never pas de faim.
English puts the owner first and adds an apostrophe. French puts the relationship first and joins it with de. The two names come out in the opposite order.
The relationship first, then de, then the owner.
Pairs with .235: same owner, different relationship, so only the first word moves.
Pairs with .236: same owner, different relationship.
Daughter, not girl. With de and a name behind it, la fille is a relationship.
The l in fils is silent and the s is said: FEES, not FEELS.

items.fr: Marie est la sœur de Paul.
items.notes: Half of the pair. Only the name after de changes between this and .242, and the meaning changes with it.

items.fr: Paul est le frère de Marie.
items.notes: The other half. The same two people, and de now points at Marie.
Voici puts somebody in front of the person you are talking to. a1.01 already used it at fr.a1.salutations.073.
The same frame with a longer relationship word in it. Nothing about the order changes.

items.fr: J'ai un frère et deux sœurs.
items.en: I have one brother and two sisters.
items.notes: avoir plus a number. a1.07 owns the verb and a1.02 owns the numbers, so this sentence needs nothing new.

items.en: I do not have a brother.
items.notes: After a negative, un and une flatten to de. The same frame as fr.a1.famille.233, « Je n'ai pas de voiture. »

items.fr: Tu as des frères et sœurs ?
items.en: Do you have any brothers and sisters?
items.notes: The question you will be asked. Rising intonation, no inversion, which is how it is really said.
Learn it as one word. Mon goes with the words that take le.
Ma goes with the words that take la.
Mes goes with anything plural, whichever kind of word it is.
Masculine plural, whatever mix of boys and girls it covers. The theme holds the singular l'enfant and has never held the plural.
La fille is girl or daughter. With de and a name behind it, only one reading is available, and that is what de buys you.

The plural of notre, and it is the same word whatever the things are. Nos parents, nos filles. Nothing about who is doing the owning changes it and nothing about the kind of thing changes it either. Only how many.
The plural of votre. Vos parents, vos livres. This is the one form of the fifteen that was absent from the corpus in every article form before this lesson, and a grid looks complete without it.

The plural of leur, and the s counts the THINGS rather than the owners. The owners were already several before the s arrived. Leur fille is one daughter belonging to several people; leurs filles is more than one daughter belonging to the same several people.
A man friend. The n of mon arrives on the front of ami and is fully pronounced, which is why this sounds like moh-na-mee rather than mon, ami.

A woman friend, and the word for her is the une kind: une amie. It still takes mon rather than ma, because ma amie would put two vowel sounds against each other. Said out loud this is the same as mon ami, sound for sound, and only the page can tell you which one was meant.
A brother is the un kind, so the word for my is mon.
A sister is the une kind, so the same my becomes ma. Nothing about the speaker changed between this sentence and the one before it.
More than one thing, so the question about the kind is never asked and mes covers both.
The owner changed and the ending on the possessive did not. Compare the row above.
Same speaker as the sentence before, and the word changed because the thing did.
The plural, and it looks exactly like mes with a different first letter.
This also means her brother. French does not say whose it is, only what it is.
This also means her sister, word for word. The sentence carries no information about the owner at all, and the English has to pick one.
And her parents. Same sentence, and only what is around it decides.
From here the kind of thing stops mattering.
The same word as the sentence above it, in front of a une word. This row asks nothing.
The only change this row ever makes, and it is about how many.
The polite or plural your, and it behaves exactly like notre.
Unchanged again.
vos. This is the form most courses leave out of the table without anybody noticing.
Several people own him, and leur carries no s because he is one brother.
Still leur. The kind of thing has not mattered for three rows now.
The s arrives because there are two parents, not because there are several owners. The owners were already several in all three of these sentences.

items.en: He is talking with his sister.
items.notes: The owner is a man and the possessive is sa, because a sister is the une kind.

items.en: She is talking with her sister.
items.notes: The owner is a woman and the possessive is still sa. One word changed between these two sentences and it was not the possessive. The English had to change twice as much.
A woman friend, and the word for her is the une kind. It takes mon anyway, because ma amie would put two vowel sounds against each other and French will not have it.

items.fr: Ma sœur et mon amie sont ici.
items.en: My sister and my friend are here.
items.notes: Both of these are the une kind and one takes ma while the other takes mon. The only difference between them is the letter the second one starts with.
The s of mes wakes up as a z in front of the vowel. Say it beside the next sentence.
And her friends. The only thing separating this from the sentence above is the vowel in the first syllable, which is the one place in this lesson where listening carries real work.
Several people, one daughter, and no s on leur.
The same several people and more than one daughter. The s counts the daughters. Out loud these two sentences are identical, so this is a difference you read rather than hear.
There is no le in this sentence and there cannot be one. The possessive is standing where the article would have stood, so the two never appear together.

items.fr: Le village est très joli au printemps.
items.en: The village is very pretty in spring.
items.ipa: lə vi.laʒ ɛ tʁɛ ʒɔ.li o pʁɛ̃.tɑ̃
items.notes: Same trap: "joli" means pretty, not jolly.

items.fr: Quelle heure est-il, s'il vous plaît ?

items.en: Excuse me, what time is it?

items.fr: Vous avez l'heure, s'il vous plaît ?
items.en: Do you have the time, please?

items.fr: Il est huit heures et demie.

items.notes: « demie » agrees with the feminine « heure », but « demi » stays masculine after « midi » and « minuit ».

items.fr: Le musée ouvre à dix heures.

items.notes: Liaison links "une" and "heure" so you hear one linked syllable; don't write an extra word between them.
The x in "deux" is silent alone but liaises as a z sound before "heures".

items.fr: Il est cinq heures moins dix.
items.notes: "Cinq" holds a nasal vowel sound, not a separate n consonant like in English.

items.fr: Il est sept heures du matin.
items.notes: The p in "sept" is always silent, and the final t liaises into the next word.

items.fr: Il est huit heures du soir.
items.notes: The t of "huit" is silent alone but is pronounced here through liaison.
"Neuf" is an exception where the final f sound changes to v before heures.

items.fr: Nous avons rendez-vous à dix heures.
items.en: We have an appointment at ten o'clock.
items.notes: The x of "dix" liaises to a z sound right before "heures".
"Une" and "heure" link into one sound, don't write "une" as if it stood alone.

items.fr: Le magasin ouvre à huit heures et demie.
items.en: The store opens at half past eight.
items.ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ u.vʁ a ɥi.tœʁ e də.mi
items.notes: The t of "huit" is silent alone but liaises before "heures".
"Est" (is) sounds close to "et" (and) but they are never interchangeable in writing.

items.fr: Le rendez-vous est à quatorze heures.
items.en: The appointment is at two PM.
items.notes: The final t of "est" is silent alone but is pronounced here before the vowel of "à".

items.fr: La réunion commence à seize heures trente.
items.ipa: la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃s a sɛ.zœʁ tʁɑ̃t
items.notes: "Réunion" and "trente" both contain nasal vowels that are easy to under-spell.

items.fr: Il travaille de neuf heures à dix-sept heures.
items.en: He works from nine to five.
items.ipa: il tʁa.vaj də nœ.vœʁ a diz.sɛ.tœʁ
items.notes: "Neuf" again shifts its final sound to v before the vowel of "heures".

items.fr: Le cours de français dure deux heures.
items.en: The French class lasts two hours.
items.ipa: lə kuʁ də fʁɑ̃.sɛ dyʁ dø.zœʁ
items.notes: The x of "deux" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

items.fr: La bibliothèque ouvre à neuf heures et demie.
items.en: The library opens at half past nine.
items.ipa: la bi.bli.jɔ.tɛk u.vʁ a nœ.vœʁ e də.mi
items.notes: "Neuf" shifts to a v sound before the vowel of "heures" once again.
"Cinq" holds a nasal vowel that liaises smoothly into "heures".
The only singular hour. Une and heure run together into one sound, so nothing marks where the number ends.
The x of deux is silent on its own and says z here. This and douze heures are the pair the ear actually fails on.
The silent s of trois says z before the vowel, exactly as the x of deux does.
No new consonant appears. The r of quatre simply carries straight on into the vowel.
The q of cinq is sounded here. The vowel before it stays nasal and never becomes a separate n.
The x says z, the same join as deux and trois. Six alone ends in an s sound and here it does not.
The p of sept is silent always. The t is silent alone and sounded here.
The t of huit is silent alone and sounded here. Huit opens on a sound English has no letter for.
The one genuine exception. The f of neuf becomes a v, and it does that before heures and before ans and nowhere else in the language.
The x says z. Dix alone ends in an s sound, so the consonant both appears and changes.
The z is already there in the spelling and simply carries over. The o stays nasal.
Said for a length of time and not for a time of day: the twelfth hour on a clock is midi or minuit.

items.fr: Le film commence à huit heures et demie.
items.en: The film starts at half past eight.
items.ipa: /lə film kɔ.mɑ̃s a ɥi.tœʁ e də.mi/
items.notes: The same showing as the listing that reads vingt heures trente. One clock is what you say and the other is what is printed.

items.fr: Le train part à quatre heures dix.
items.en: The train leaves at four ten.
items.notes: The same train as the board that reads seize heures dix. Past twelve the two clocks stop agreeing on the number.

items.fr: Le magasin ferme à six heures du soir.
items.en: The shop closes at six in the evening.
items.ipa: /lə ma.ɡa.zɛ̃ fɛʁm a si.zœʁ dy swaʁ/
items.notes: The spoken clock has only twelve hours, so it says which half of the day it means. The printed one says dix-huit heures and does not need to.

items.fr: Le rendez-vous est à deux heures de l'après-midi.
items.en: The appointment is at two in the afternoon.
items.notes: The one of the four built on être, so it is the pair a learner can be asked to produce. The card it faces reads quatorze heures.

items.fr: Lundi, je commence un nouveau travail.
items.en: On Monday, I'm starting a new job.
items.ipa: lœ̃.di ʒə kɔ.mɑ̃s œ̃ nu.vo tʁa.vaj
items.notes: 'Lundi' is capitalized here only because it opens the sentence; day names are otherwise always lowercase.

items.fr: Le lundi, je vais à la bibliothèque après les cours.
items.en: On Mondays, I go to the library after class.
items.ipa: lə lœ̃.di ʒə vɛ a la bi.bli.jɔ.tɛk a.pʁɛ le kuʁ
items.notes: 'Le lundi' (with the article) means every Monday, a repeated habit, not a single Monday.

items.en: We have an appointment on Tuesday morning.

items.fr: Le mardi, ma sœur fait du yoga.
items.en: On Tuesdays, my sister does yoga.
items.ipa: lə maʁ.di ma sœʁ fɛ dy jɔ.ga
items.notes: 'Le mardi' means every Tuesday; without the article, 'mardi' alone would mean just one Tuesday.

items.fr: Le mercredi après-midi, les enfants n'ont pas école.
items.en: On Wednesday afternoons, children don't have school.
items.ipa: lə mɛʁ.kʁə.di a.pʁɛ mi.di le zɑ̃.fɑ̃ nɔ̃ pa ze.kɔl
items.notes: 'Le mercredi' signals a repeated Wednesday habit, unlike a single 'mercredi'.

items.fr: Mercredi, je dois aller chez le dentiste.
items.en: This Wednesday, I have to go to the dentist.
items.ipa: mɛʁ.kʁə.di ʒə dwa a.le ʃe lə dɑ̃.tist

items.fr: Jeudi prochain, nous partons en voyage.
items.en: Next Thursday, we're leaving on a trip.
items.ipa: ʒø.di pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃ nu paʁ.tɔ̃ ɑ̃ vwa.jaʒ
items.notes: Day names like 'jeudi' stay lowercase even when followed by 'prochain'.

items.fr: Le jeudi, il joue au foot avec ses amis.
items.en: On Thursdays, he plays soccer with his friends.
items.ipa: lə ʒø.di il ʒu o fut a.vɛk se za.mi
items.notes: 'Le jeudi' describes a weekly habit; drop the article and 'jeudi' means just one specific Thursday.

items.fr: Le vendredi, la boulangerie ferme plus tôt.
items.en: On Fridays, the bakery closes earlier.
items.ipa: lə vɑ̃.dʁə.di la bu.lɑ̃.ʒʁi fɛʁm ply to
items.notes: 'Le vendredi' here means every Friday, a recurring closing time, not one Friday.

items.fr: Samedi, je fais les courses au marché.
items.en: This Saturday, I'm doing the shopping at the market.
items.ipa: sam.di ʒə fɛ le kuʁs o maʁ.ʃe

items.fr: Le samedi matin, mes parents dorment tard.
items.en: On Saturday mornings, my parents sleep in.
items.ipa: lə sam.di ma.tɛ̃ me pa.ʁɑ̃ dɔʁm taʁ
items.notes: 'Le samedi matin' means every Saturday morning, a routine, not a single occasion.

items.fr: Dimanche, toute la famille se retrouve chez grand-mère.
items.en: On Sunday, the whole family gets together at grandma's.
items.ipa: di.mɑ̃ʃ tut la fa.mij sə ʁə.tʁuv ʃe gʁɑ̃.mɛʁ
items.notes: 'Dimanche' stays lowercase mid-sentence; only a capital D at the very start of a sentence is correct.

items.fr: Le dimanche, nous ne travaillons jamais.
items.ipa: lə di.mɑ̃ʃ nu nə tʁa.va.jɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ
items.notes: 'Le dimanche' with the article means every Sunday, contrasted with a single 'dimanche'.
After 'nous sommes', the day name 'lundi' stays lowercase.

items.fr: La réunion est reportée à jeudi.
items.en: The meeting is postponed to Thursday.
items.ipa: la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ ɛ ʁə.pɔʁ.te a ʒø.di

items.notes: 'Vendredi dernier' needs no article and no capital letter.

items.fr: Le professeur donne un contrôle le lundi et le jeudi.
items.en: The teacher gives a quiz on Mondays and Thursdays.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ dɔn œ̃ kɔ̃.tʁol lə lœ̃.di e lə ʒø.di
items.notes: Using 'le' before both days shows this happens every Monday and every Thursday, not just once.

items.fr: Ce n'est pas lundi, c'est mardi.
items.ipa: sə nɛ pa lœ̃.di sɛ maʁ.di

items.fr: Mon cours de piano est le mercredi à seize heures.
items.en: My piano lesson is on Wednesdays at four o'clock.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ kuʁ də pja.no ɛ lə mɛʁ.kʁə.di a sɛ.zœʁ
items.notes: 'Le mercredi' here marks a fixed weekly time slot, repeated every week.

items.fr: Nous fermons le dimanche et le lundi.
items.en: We are closed on Sundays and Mondays.
items.ipa: nu fɛʁ.mɔ̃ lə di.mɑ̃ʃ e lə lœ̃.di
items.notes: 'Le dimanche et le lundi' means every Sunday and every Monday, a permanent weekly closure.

items.fr: Le facteur passe le mardi et le vendredi.
items.en: The mailman comes on Tuesdays and Fridays.
items.ipa: lə fak.tœʁ pas lə maʁ.di e lə vɑ̃.dʁə.di
items.notes: 'Le mardi et le vendredi' describes the mail carrier's regular weekly route.

items.en: Are you free on Wednesday evening?

items.fr: Le marché a lieu tous les samedis.
items.en: The market takes place every Saturday.
items.ipa: lə maʁ.ʃe a ljø tu le sam.di
items.notes: 'Tous les samedis' reinforces that the market happens every single Saturday.

items.fr: J'ai piscine le mardi et le jeudi.
items.en: I have swimming on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
items.ipa: ʒe pi.sin lə maʁ.di e lə ʒø.di
items.notes: 'Le mardi et le jeudi' marks a fixed weekly schedule for swimming lessons.
'Samedi prochain' needs no article, unlike the habitual 'le samedi'.

items.fr: Le lundi est souvent difficile après le week-end.
items.en: Monday is often hard after the weekend.
items.ipa: lə lœ̃.di ɛ su.vɑ̃ di.fi.sil a.pʁɛ lə wik.ɛnd

items.fr: Mardi, il y a une grève des trains.
items.en: On Tuesday, there's a train strike.
items.ipa: maʁ.di il i a yn gʁɛv de tʁɛ̃

items.fr: Le jeudi soir, mes cousins viennent dîner.
items.en: On Thursday evenings, my cousins come for dinner.
items.ipa: lə ʒø.di swaʁ me ku.zɛ̃ vjɛn di.ne
items.notes: 'Le jeudi soir' is a recurring weekly visit, not a one-time event.

items.fr: Nous partons jeudi et nous revenons dimanche.
items.en: We're leaving on Thursday and coming back on Sunday.
items.ipa: nu paʁ.tɔ̃ ʒø.di e nu ʁə.və.nɔ̃ di.mɑ̃ʃ
items.notes: Both 'jeudi' and 'dimanche' stay lowercase mid-sentence here.

items.fr: La pharmacie est fermée le dimanche.
items.en: The pharmacy is closed on Sundays.
items.ipa: la faʁ.ma.si ɛ fɛʁ.me lə di.mɑ̃ʃ
items.notes: 'Le dimanche' here means every Sunday, the pharmacy's regular closing day.

items.fr: Le samedi, je fais du sport avec mon frère.
items.en: On Saturdays, I do sports with my brother.
items.ipa: lə sam.di ʒə fɛ dy spɔʁ a.vɛk mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ
items.notes: 'Le samedi' indicates a weekly habit of exercising with his brother.

items.fr: Mercredi, nous allons au cinéma en famille.
items.en: On Wednesday, we're going to the movies as a family.
items.ipa: mɛʁ.kʁə.di nu za.lɔ̃ o si.ne.ma ɑ̃ fa.mij

items.fr: Le mardi matin, j'ai un cours de français.
items.en: On Tuesday mornings, I have a French class.
items.ipa: lə maʁ.di ma.tɛ̃ ʒe œ̃ kuʁ də fʁɑ̃.sɛ
items.notes: 'Le mardi matin' marks a fixed recurring class slot every week.

items.fr: Dimanche prochain, c'est la fête des mères.
items.ipa: di.mɑ̃ʃ pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃ sɛ la fɛt de mɛʁ
items.notes: 'Dimanche prochain' stays lowercase and needs no article.

items.en: Monday or Tuesday, does that work for you?

items.fr: Le premier avril, on fait des blagues.
items.en: On the first of April, people play pranks.
items.ipa: lə pʁə.mje a.vʁil ɔ̃ fɛ de blag

items.fr: La rentrée scolaire est en septembre.
items.en: The start of the school year is in September.
items.ipa: la ʁɑ̃.tʁe skɔ.lɛʁ ɛ ɑ̃ sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: 'Septembre' is lowercase here, only sentence-initial month names take a capital letter.

items.fr: En décembre, les vitrines sont magnifiques.
items.en: In December, the shop windows are beautiful.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ de.sɑ̃bʁ le vi.tʁin sɔ̃ ma.ɲi.fik
items.notes: 'Décembre' needs its accent aigu on the é, and no capital letter mid-sentence.

items.fr: L'anniversaire de mon père est en octobre.
items.en: My father's birthday is in October.
items.ipa: la.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ də mɔ̃ pɛʁ ɛ ɑ̃ nɔk.tɔbʁ

items.fr: Le concours a lieu tous les ans en novembre.
items.en: The competition takes place every year in November.
items.ipa: lə kɔ̃.kuʁ a ljø tu le zɑ̃ ɑ̃ nɔ.vɑ̃bʁ

items.fr: Cette année, mon anniversaire tombe un mardi.
items.en: This year, my birthday falls on a Tuesday.
items.ipa: sɛ.ta.ne mɔ̃ na.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ tɔ̃b œ̃ maʁ.di
items.notes: 'Mardi' stays lowercase here since it is not the first word of the sentence.

items.fr: Elle a soufflé ses bougies un lundi soir.
items.en: She blew out her candles on a Monday evening.
items.ipa: ɛ.la su.fle se bu.ʒi œ̃ lœ̃.di swaʁ

items.fr: Je dois acheter un cadeau avant jeudi.
items.en: I need to buy a gift before Thursday.
items.ipa: ʒə dwa aʃ.te œ̃ ka.do a.vɑ̃ ʒø.di

items.fr: La Saint-Valentin est célébrée le quatorze février.
items.en: Valentine's Day is celebrated on February fourteenth.
items.ipa: la sɛ̃.va.lɑ̃.tɛ̃ ɛ se.le.bʁe lə ka.tɔʁz fe.vʁi.e

items.fr: La fête du Travail est le premier mai.
items.en: Labor Day is on May first.
items.notes: Even inside a fixed holiday name, 'mai' is never capitalized in French.
items.ipa: la fɛt dy tʁa.vaj ɛ lə pʁə.mje mɛ

items.fr: En France, le onze novembre commémore la fin de la Première Guerre mondiale.
items.en: In France, November eleventh commemorates the end of World War One.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ fʁɑ̃s lə ɔ̃z nɔ.vɑ̃bʁ kɔ.me.mɔʁ la fɛ̃ də la pʁə.mjɛʁ gɛʁ mɔ̃.djal
items.notes: 'Novembre' stays lowercase even though 'onze novembre' names a famous historical date.

items.fr: Le carnaval de Nice se déroule en février.
items.en: The Nice carnival takes place in February.
items.ipa: lə kaʁ.na.val də nis sə de.ʁul ɑ̃ fe.vʁi.e
items.notes: 'Février' needs its accent aigu even in a place name context like 'le carnaval de Nice'.

items.fr: Chaque année, le feu d'artifice a lieu le quatorze juillet.
items.en: Every year, the fireworks display takes place on July fourteenth.
items.ipa: ʃak a.ne lə fø daʁ.ti.fis a ljø lə ka.tɔʁz ʒɥi.jɛ

items.fr: J'ai cours de yoga le lundi et le mercredi soir.
items.en: I have yoga class on Monday and Wednesday evenings.
items.ipa: ʒe kuʁ də jɔ.ga lə lœ̃.di e lə mɛʁ.kʁə.di swaʁ
items.notes: Naming both days with 'le' shows a fixed weekly schedule, every Monday and every Wednesday.

items.fr: Le docteur me reçoit uniquement le mardi.
items.en: The doctor only sees me on Tuesdays.
items.ipa: lə dɔk.tœʁ mə ʁə.swa y.nik.mɑ̃ lə maʁ.di
items.notes: 'Le mardi' here means every Tuesday is reserved for these appointments.

items.fr: Nous avons une réunion d'équipe tous les vendredis.
items.en: We have a team meeting every Friday.
items.ipa: nu za.vɔ̃ yn ʁe.y.njɔ̃ de.kip tu le vɑ̃.dʁə.di
items.notes: 'Tous les vendredis' emphasizes that the meeting repeats every single Friday.

items.fr: Elle prend le train le vendredi soir pour rentrer chez ses parents.
items.en: She takes the train on Friday evenings to go back to her parents' house.
items.ipa: ɛl pʁɑ̃ lə tʁɛ̃ lə vɑ̃.dʁə.di swaʁ puʁ ʁɑ̃.tʁe ʃe se pa.ʁɑ̃
items.notes: 'Le vendredi soir' describes a regular weekly routine, not a single trip.

items.fr: Le cours de cuisine a lieu un mercredi sur deux.
items.en: The cooking class takes place every other Wednesday.
items.ipa: lə kuʁ də kɥi.zin a ljø œ̃ mɛʁ.kʁə.di syʁ dø

items.fr: Elle arrose ses plantes le mercredi et le samedi.
items.en: She waters her plants on Wednesdays and Saturdays.
items.ipa: ɛ.la.ʁoz se plɑ̃t lə mɛʁ.kʁə.di e lə sam.di
items.notes: 'Le mercredi et le samedi' describes a fixed watering routine every week.

items.fr: Tous les jeudis, elle prend son cours de yoga à dix-huit heures.
items.en: Every Thursday, she has her yoga class at six in the evening.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Tous les jeudis,","t":"every thursday,"},{"w":"elle prend","t":"she takes"},{"w":"son cours de yoga","t":"her yoga class"},{"w":"à dix-huit heures.","t":"at six in the evening"}]}

items.fr: Le mois de février est le plus court de l'année.
items.en: The month of February is the shortest of the year.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le mois de février","t":"the month of february"},{"w":"est","t":"is"},{"w":"le plus court","t":"the shortest"},{"w":"de l'année.","t":"of the year"}]}

items.fr: Tous les mardis, je vais à la bibliothèque après le travail.
items.en: Every Tuesday, I go to the library after work.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Tous les mardis,","t":"every tuesday,"},{"w":"je vais","t":"i go"},{"w":"à la bibliothèque","t":"to the library"},{"w":"après le travail.","t":"after work"}]}

items.fr: Le mercredi, mon fils a son cours de musique à seize heures.
items.en: On Wednesday, my son has his music class at four in the afternoon.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le mercredi,","t":"on wednesday,"},{"w":"mon fils","t":"my son"},{"w":"a son cours de musique","t":"has his music class"},{"w":"à seize heures.","t":"at four in the afternoon"}]}

items.fr: Tous les jeudis soir, nous regardons un film en famille.
items.en: Every Thursday evening, we watch a movie as a family.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Tous les jeudis soir,","t":"every thursday evening,"},{"w":"nous regardons","t":"we watch"},{"w":"un film","t":"a movie"},{"w":"en famille.","t":"as a family"}]}
Every Monday, as a rule. The article is the only thing making it habitual.
This coming Monday, once. No article, and no preposition either.

items.fr: Le magasin est fermé le mardi.
items.en: The shop is closed on Tuesdays.
items.notes: Every Tuesday. This is what a sign on a door means.

items.en: The shop is closed on Tuesday.
items.notes: One Tuesday, the next one. A handwritten note taped over the sign.
Every Wednesday. On means we, and takes the same form as il.
This Wednesday only. Nothing in front of the day, and nothing before it.

items.fr: Elle est à Paris le jeudi.
items.en: She is in Paris on Thursdays.
items.notes: Every Thursday, as a standing arrangement.

items.en: She is in Paris on Thursday.
items.notes: One Thursday. Whether it is the next one is decided by the conversation.

items.fr: Nous avons une réunion le vendredi.
items.en: We have a meeting on Fridays.
items.notes: Every Friday. The one in the diary that repeats.

items.en: We have a meeting on Friday.
items.notes: One meeting, this Friday. Drop the article and you have changed the diary.
Every Saturday. This is a fact about your week.
This Saturday. This is an answer to an invitation.

items.fr: Le musée est gratuit le dimanche.
items.en: The museum is free on Sundays.
items.notes: Every Sunday. Worth knowing before you buy a ticket.

items.en: The museum is free on Sunday.
items.notes: This Sunday only, because of something happening that week.
This Saturday. An arrangement for one day, which is what makes it a plan.

items.en: We see each other on Saturdays.
items.notes: Every Saturday. Not a plan at all, a description of how things are.

items.fr: Mon anniversaire est le premier janvier.
items.en: My birthday is on the first of January.
items.notes: A day inside a month, so le plus a number. premier is the only ordinal a date ever takes.
The month on its own, so en and nothing else. The same frame that gives the date takes no number here.

items.fr: La fête du Travail est en mai.
items.ipa: /la fɛt dy tʁa.vaj ɛ ɑ̃ mɛ/
items.notes: Which May day is not said, so the month alone is enough and en carries it.
Somewhere in June. True, and not enough for anybody to meet you at an airport.

items.fr: Mon vol est le douze juin.
items.en: My flight is on the twelfth of June.
items.notes: One day inside June. The number comes first and the le cannot be dropped.
The month alone. Note the le in front of concert is the noun's own, not the date frame.

items.fr: Le concert est le quatorze juillet.
items.en: The concert is on the fourteenth of July.
items.notes: A plain cardinal, quatorze, with no ordinal ending and no de before the month.

items.fr: Le magasin est fermé en août.
items.en: The shop is closed in August.
items.notes: The whole month, which is what a sign on a French shop door usually means in August.

items.fr: Le magasin est fermé le premier août.
items.en: The shop is closed on the first of August.
items.ipa: /lə ma.ɡa.zɛ̃ ɛ fɛʁ.me lə pʁə.mje ut/
items.notes: One day, so a date. Same sentence, same shop, and a week of your shopping between them.

items.fr: L'anniversaire de mon père est le trois octobre.
items.en: My father's birthday is on the third of October.
items.ipa: /la.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ də mɔ̃ pɛʁ ɛ lə tʁwa ɔk.tɔbʁ/
items.notes: trois, not troisième. Every day but the first takes a plain counting number.

items.en: I have an exam in December.
items.notes: Sometime in December. Enough to plan a holiday around and not enough to revise for.

items.fr: J'ai un examen le douze décembre.
items.en: I have an exam on the twelfth of December.
items.notes: One day. The number goes in front of the month, which is the opposite of the English order.
« à la maison » means at home, a fixed everyday expression.

items.fr: Il y a une table dans le salon.
items.en: There is a table in the living room.
items.notes: « salon » is masculine, so it takes « le ».
items.prompt: Il y a une table dans ___ salon.

items.notes: Before a vowel or silent h, « je » becomes « j' » (elision).

items.fr: Le pour le masculin, la pour le féminin, l' devant une voyelle.
items.en: Use le for masculine nouns, la for feminine nouns, and l' before a vowel.
items.notes: Ex : le salon · la chambre · l'entrée
items.prompt: Quand utiliser « le », « la » ou « l' » ?

items.notes: Very informal, use only with friends.
Always plural in French.
A comfortable chair with arms, usually in the living room.
Bedroom furniture with drawers for clothes.
Literally the low table, placed in front of the sofa.
A decorative cushion on the sofa. A pillow for sleeping is l'oreiller.
Masculine in French: un vase de fleurs.
Un cadre photo hangs on the wall.
Literally carries coats. Usually near the front door.
Named after Monsieur Poubelle, the official who introduced it in Paris.
Masculine: un interrupteur. It interrupts the electric current.
Heats the room in winter.
Means both the fireplace inside and the chimney on the roof.
The space under the roof, often used for storage.
The flat area at the top of the stairs, shared with the neighbors in a building.
The key goes in the lock: la clé est dans la serrure.
From sonner, to ring. On sonne à la porte.
Literally the box for letters, at the entrance of the house or building.
Moving out of a home. The verb is déménager.
The opposite of déménager: nous emménageons dans la nouvelle maison.
The grass in the garden: on tond la pelouse.
Surrounds the garden or the yard.
For serving tea at home.
Pronounced pwal, not pwehl.
The lid of a pot or a jar.
Une planche alone is a board or plank.
The kitchen sink; the bathroom sink is le lavabo.
For drying dishes, not for hands.
For washing dishes or wiping the table.
Also called le liquide vaisselle.
Un seau d'eau: a bucket of water.
Passer le balai: to sweep.
A floor cloth used with a bucket.
Le linge is the laundry.
Le fil alone is a wire or thread.
Le panier alone is a basket.
For hanging clothes in the wardrobe.
A one-room apartment.
Often shortened to un appart in speech.
A large detached house, often with a garden.
The large gate at the entrance of a property.
A low fence or barrier around a yard.
A glassed-in room attached to the house.
French homes often close les volets at night.
The glass itself; the window is la fenêtre.
La poignée de porte: the door handle.
Ouvrir le tiroir: to open the drawer.
A built-in cupboard or closet.
Les meubles: the furniture.
A dining room cabinet for dishes.
Couper l'électricité: to cut the power.
The final z is pronounced.
Il n'y a plus d'eau chaude: there is no more hot water.
Mettre le chauffage: to turn on the heating.
The meter for electricity, gas, or water.
Fermer le robinet: to turn off the tap.
Une fuite d'eau: a water leak.
Une panne de courant: a power outage.
The corridor inside a home or building.
Wall-to-wall carpet; a rug is un tapis.
The mat in front of the door.
Changer une ampoule: to change a light bulb.

items.fr: Notre maison a un grand jardin.
items.en: Our house has a big garden.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ mɛ.zɔ̃ a œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ ʒaʁ.dɛ̃
items.notes: “a” (from avoir) has no accent, unlike “à” (to/at).

items.fr: La maison est grande et blanche.
items.en: The house is big and white.
items.ipa: la mɛ.zɔ̃ ɛ ɡʁɑ̃d e blɑ̃ʃ
items.notes: “Grande” and “blanche” take the feminine ending to agree with “maison”.

items.fr: Ma maison a un grand jardin.
items.en: My house has a big garden.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ma maison","t":"my house"},{"w":"a","t":"has"},{"w":"un grand jardin.","t":"a big garden"}]}

items.fr: La cuisine est à côté du salon.
items.en: The kitchen is next to the living room.
items.notes: "à" (preposition, with accent) must not be confused with "a" (verb avoir), even though both sound the same.

items.fr: Il y a un grand lit dans la chambre.
items.en: There is a big bed in the bedroom.
items.ipa: /il i a œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ li dɑ̃ la ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: The final "d" of "grand" and the final "t" of "lit" are both silent.

items.fr: Nous rangeons nos affaires chaque matin.
items.en: We put our things away every morning.
items.notes: Liaison links "nos" and "affaires" with a /z/ sound that has no letter of its own to add.

items.fr: Mon frère dort dans la petite chambre.
items.en: My brother sleeps in the small bedroom.
items.ipa: /mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ dɔʁ dɑ̃ la pə.tit ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: The final "e" of "petite" is silent, but it makes the preceding "t" audible, unlike masculine "petit".

items.fr: Le salon a deux fenêtres et une porte.
items.en: The living room has two windows and one door.
items.ipa: /lə sa.lɔ̃ a dø fə.nɛtʁ e yn pɔʁt/
items.notes: "et" (and) sounds exactly like "est" (is), so context alone tells you which spelling to use.

items.fr: Ma sœur balaie la cuisine tous les soirs.
items.en: My sister sweeps the kitchen every evening.
items.ipa: /ma sœʁ ba.lɛ la kɥi.zin tu le swaʁ/
items.notes: "balaie" keeps the "ai" spelling even though it sounds like a simple "è".

items.fr: Les rideaux sont bleus dans le salon.
items.en: The curtains are blue in the living room.
items.ipa: /le ʁi.do sɔ̃ blø dɑ̃ lə sa.lɔ̃/
items.notes: The final "x" of "rideaux" and the final "s" of "bleus" are both silent plural markers.

items.fr: Il ferme la fenêtre parce qu'il fait froid.
items.en: He closes the window because it is cold.
items.ipa: /il fɛʁm la fə.nɛtʁ paʁs.kil fɛ fʁwa/
items.notes: "que" drops its "e" before the vowel of "il", written as "qu'il".

items.fr: Nous avons un canapé confortable au salon.
items.en: We have a comfortable sofa in the living room.
items.notes: "Nous avons" is joined by a liaison /z/ even though "nous" ends in a silent "s".

items.fr: La salle de bain est au bout du couloir.
items.en: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
items.ipa: /la sal də bɛ̃ ɛ.t‿o bu dy ku.lwaʁ/
items.notes: "bain" is one single nasal sound, not "ba" plus a separate "n".

items.fr: Mes parents rangent le garage le samedi.
items.en: My parents tidy the garage on Saturdays.
items.ipa: /me pa.ʁɑ̃ ʁɑ̃ʒ lə ɡa.ʁaʒ lə sam.di/
items.notes: The "ent" ending of "rangent" is completely silent, just like most third person plural verb endings.

items.fr: On mange dans la cuisine ce soir.
items.en: We are eating in the kitchen tonight.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ mɑ̃ʒ dɑ̃ la kɥi.zin sə swaʁ/
items.notes: "on" (we, one) sounds identical to "ont" (they have), so only sentence sense tells you which to write.

items.fr: Le chat dort sur le grand lit blanc.
items.en: The cat sleeps on the big white bed.
items.ipa: /lə ʃa dɔʁ syʁ lə ɡʁɑ̃ li blɑ̃/
items.notes: The final consonants of "grand" and "blanc" are silent unless a liaison occurs.

items.fr: J'ouvre la porte de la cave doucement.
items.en: I open the cellar door slowly.
items.ipa: /ʒuvʁ la pɔʁt də la kav dus.mɑ̃/
items.notes: "je" loses its "e" before a vowel and becomes "j'" attached to "ouvre".

items.fr: Il y a beaucoup de bruit chez les voisins.
items.en: There is a lot of noise at the neighbors' place.
items.ipa: /il i a bo.ku də bʁɥi ʃe le vwa.zɛ̃/
items.notes: "beaucoup" combines the tricky spelling "eau" for /o/ with "ou" for /u/, easy to mix up when writing fast.

items.fr: Le marché est ouvert le samedi matin.
items.en: The market is open on Saturday morning.
items.notes: Liaison between est and ouvert adds a t sound that is not heard when est stands alone.
Je elides to j' before the vowel-initial verb achète.

items.fr: Elle choisit des tomates bien mûres.
items.notes: The final t in choisit is silent, easy to forget when writing.
Pèse needs a grave accent to mark the open e sound, a detail invisible in casual speech.

items.en: How much does this cheese cost?
items.notes: Combien contains two nasal vowels that are easy to under-articulate when writing quickly.
Sont sounds like son; only the verb context tells you to add the final t.
The final d of vend is silent, a common trap for this regular verb ending.

items.en: We are looking for yellow flowers.
items.notes: Jaunes agrees in gender and number with fleurs, adding a silent final s.

items.fr: Vous voulez un kilo de carottes ?
items.en: Do you want a kilo of carrots?
items.notes: The unstressed e in de is a schwa that can fade in speech but must stay in writing.

items.fr: Ils achètent du pain à la boulangerie.
items.en: They buy bread at the bakery.
items.notes: Liaison between ils and achètent produces a z sound signaling the plural, not audible in il achète.

items.en: They look at the exotic fruits.
items.notes: The verb ending -ent in regardent is silent, so elle regarde and elles regardent sound almost identical.

items.fr: Je prends deux kilos de pommes de terre.

Feminine form: la couvreuse. From couvrir, to cover.
Feminine form: la carreleuse. Lays tiles on floors and walls.
Feminine form: la déménageuse. From déménager, to move house.
Feminine form: la livreuse. From livrer, to deliver.
Same form for both genders: la garagiste for a woman.
Same form for both genders: la pompiste for a woman. From la pompe, the pump.
Same form for both genders: la guide touristique for a woman.
Same form for both genders: la réceptionniste for a woman.

Feminine form: la fromagère. From le fromage, cheese.

Feminine form: la masseuse.
Feminine form: la gardienne. Also used for a goalkeeper, le gardien de but.
Feminine: la députée, same pronunciation.
Sells cold cuts and cooked meats. Feminine: la charcutière.
Often used for both men and women.
Feminine: la cordonnière.

From blanchir, to whiten. Feminine: la blanchisseuse.
Feminine: l'ambulancière.
From le brancard, the stretcher. Feminine: la brancardière.
Literally wise woman. The same word is used for men in the job.
Feminine: l'aide-soignante.

Same form for women: la pédiatre.
Short for le médecin généraliste. Same form for women: la généraliste.
Feminine: la marchande.
Sells in bulk to shops. Same form for women: la grossiste.
Sells to the public. Feminine: la détaillante.
Feminine: l'apprentie, same pronunciation.
Feminine: la gérante.
From veiller, to stay awake. Feminine: la veilleuse de nuit.
Feminine: l'agente de sécurité.
L'entretien means upkeep. Feminine: l'agente d'entretien.
Le ménage means housework. A man is un homme de ménage.
Informal, from nourrice. The official term is assistante maternelle.
Borrowed from English. Loads and unloads ships.

Works metal in a forge. Feminine: la forgeronne.
Makes pottery from clay. Feminine: la potière.

Engraves designs into metal, wood, or stone. Feminine: la graveuse.

English needs a. French forbids it after être. The gap is the grammar.
The one place the article comes back. C'est points at a person; il est describes one.

items.notes: suis. Said far more often than any other form, because most of what you say is about yourself.

items.respell: tü eh ee-see poor la kohⁿ-fay-RAHⁿS

items.notes: sommes. The doubled m really does sound, which is why it is not a nasal vowel.

items.fr: Vous êtes ici pour la conférence ?
items.en: Are you here for the conference?
items.respell: voo zet ee-see poor la kohⁿ-fay-RAHⁿS
items.notes: êtes, and the only form in the six that binds to its pronoun out loud: voo-ZET, never voo ETT.

items.fr: Ils sont ici pour la conférence.
items.en: They are here for the conference.
items.respell: eel sohⁿ ee-see poor la kohⁿ-fay-RAHⁿS
items.notes: sont. A nasal vowel and no T sound. Compare ils ont, which is the next lesson.
A name takes nothing in front of it. It is already as specified as a word can be.
Introducing somebody else. c est points at a person; il est would describe one.
ma is a little word in front of the noun, so the sentence takes c est.
The plural of c est. Nobody says ce est, and almost nobody remembers ce sont.
No un. English needs one and French forbids it, so the error is audible every time.
Being a student counts as a job here. The gap after es is the grammar.
The liaison and the missing article in one short question.

items.en: I am French. (said by a man)
items.notes: Lowercase f. The adjective is not capitalised in French the way the English is.

items.en: I am French. (said by a woman)
items.notes: The e wakes the s, and the two are audibly different. This is the agreement a1.01 taught on enchanté.
Plural group, plural adjective. The s is silent and the agreement is only on the page.
de plus a town. Nothing agrees with anything, whoever is saying it.
A woman, and de still does not move. Compare elle est espagnole, where the adjective did.
The question that gets you both origin answers. de plus où, elided.

items.en: I am tired. (said by a man)
I am tired. (said by a woman)
items.notes: Identical out loud to the masculine. The agreement is real and it is silent, exactly like désolé and désolée in a1.01.
Here the agreement IS audible: the e wakes the d. Compare fatiguée, where it stays silent.
un is the little word in front, so the sentence takes c est.
Same doctor, no little word, so il est. Il est un médecin is the sentence to unlearn.
le counts too. The test is any little word, not the indefinite one specifically.
Not a person at all. c est also points at a thing, a situation or an idea, which il est never does.
Two joins in four words, and the first one is the one nobody hears themselves miss.
The half of the ils sont / ils ont pair that belongs to this lesson. The other half is a1.07.

The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 044.
Two words arrived and nothing else in the sentence moved. Ne went in front of suis and pas went behind it.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 046.
The same wrap, and ne has lost its e because est starts on a vowel. That is the elision rule from sons.07, not a new one.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 048.
The wrap goes around the conjugated verb whatever person it is in. Sommes is one word, so ne and pas sit either side of it.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 050.
Soif never had a word in front of it, so the negative had nothing to take away. It is pas soif and never pas de soif.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 052.

items.en: I do not have a brother.
items.notes: Two things changed. The wrap went round ai, and then the un became de. A learner who does only the first says Je n ai pas un frère.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 054.

items.en: I do not have a car.
items.notes: De agrees with nothing. Une became de, exactly as un did, and there is no de feminine to remember.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 056.
Des became de like the other two, and then de lost its e in front of the vowel. The same elision, arriving on the other side of the sentence.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 058.

items.en: I do not have a book.
items.notes: Un became de. This is the rule you already have, on the noun the next two cards use as well.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 060.

items.en: I do not have the book.
items.notes: Same verb, same noun, and le did not move. Only un, une, des, du and de la ever collapse. Le, la and les stay exactly where they were.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 062.
The un survived, and the only thing different from the first card is the verb. After être nothing collapses at all.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 064.
Une survived as well. If this had been avoir it would have been de, and the only thing telling you otherwise is the verb.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 066.

items.notes: Des survived too, and ne kept its e because sont starts on a consonant. The exception reaches every person of être, not just ce n est pas.
The sentence before the negative arrives. Its negative is 068.

items.notes: The written form, with both halves of the wrap in place. This is what you write and what you will be marked on.

items.en: I do not have a dog. (spoken French, with the ne dropped)
items.notes: The same sentence as Je n ai pas de chien, said the way it is actually said. Dropping the ne is not slang and not careless: it is what ordinary spoken French does with a negative, and a learner who has only met the written form will hear this and register agreement rather than refusal. Recognise it. Do not write it, and do not say it while you are still learning which half you would be dropping.

en France (in or to France).
Feminine: française. Nationality adjectives are lowercase in French.
au Canada (in or to Canada).
Feminine: canadienne.
en Belgique (in or to Belgium).
Same form for masculine and feminine: belge.
aux États-Unis (in or to the United States). Always plural.
Feminine: américaine.
au Sénégal (in or to Senegal).
Feminine: sénégalaise.
en Allemagne (in or to Germany).
Feminine: allemande.
en Espagne (in or to Spain).
Feminine: espagnole.
en Italie (in or to Italy).
Feminine: italienne.
au Portugal (in or to Portugal).
Feminine: portugaise.
au Japon (in or to Japan).
Feminine: japonaise.
au Mexique (in or to Mexico). Masculine even though it ends in e.
Feminine: mexicaine.

items.en: She is Canadian, but she lives in France.

items.notes: Nationality adjectives like “canadienne” take a lowercase letter in French.

items.fr: La France est un pays d'Europe.
items.en: France is a country in Europe.
items.notes: La liaison 'est_un' sonne comme 'ɛtɛ̃', facile d'oublier le t de liaison à l'écrit.

items.fr: Le Canada est un grand pays.
items.notes: 'Grand' se termine par un d muet, ne pas ajouter de lettre en trop.
'États-Unis' prend un trait d'union et deux majuscules.
'Sont' et 'son' sont homophones ; le t ici sert seulement à la liaison d'inversion.
France is the la kind, so the word for to is en. Nothing else in this sentence changes when the country does.

items.en: I am going to the United States.
items.notes: The country is plural, so the word for to is aux, and the x wakes up as a z in front of the vowel. Said out loud this is one long word rather than two.

items.en: I come from the United States.
items.notes: The same plural country, coming the other way, and des does exactly what aux did. The s wakes up as a z for the same reason.
Iran is the le kind and still takes en, because au Iran would put two vowel sounds against each other. The n of en arrives on the front of Iran and is fully pronounced.
Coming the other way the exception is over: this is the ordinary de of a le country, cut short in front of a vowel exactly as le and la were.
Mexique ends in an e and takes le anyway, so the word for to is au. The ending is a hint rather than a rule, and this is the country most likely to catch you out.
No article in front of the nationality. The last sound is a nasal vowel with no n behind it.
The e on the end wakes the n up. The nasal vowel collapses into a plain one with a real n after it, which is the same thing that happens between brun and brune.
A capital F, because here the word is the name of a person rather than a description of one. Out loud this is identical to the sentence without the capital.
The same en as en France, on a different la country. The choice was made by the article and by nothing else.
And the same de. Belgium and France take the same two words as each other and nothing about either country decided it except which article it carries.

items.ipa: il nɛʒ bo.ku ɑ̃.n‿i.vɛʁ a ke.bɛk

items.notes: “faim” ends in a nasal vowel spelled “aim”, don't confuse it with “fin”.
“prêt” agrees in gender: use “prête” for a feminine subject.
The hyphen links the inverted verb and pronoun: "appelez-vous".
Inversion "es-tu" takes a hyphen, not a space.

items.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu fais dans la vie ?
items.en: What do you do for a living?
items.ipa: kɛs kə ty fɛ dɑ̃ la vi
items.notes: "Que" elides to "qu'" before the vowel in "est-ce".

items.fr: Combien de frères et sœurs as-tu ?
items.en: How many brothers and sisters do you have?
items.ipa: kɔ̃.bjɛ̃ də fʁɛʁ e sœʁ a ty
items.notes: "Sœur" is spelled with the œ ligature.

items.en: How many children do you have?

items.notes: "Quelle" agrees with the feminine noun "heure" even though the subject is "il".

items.fr: Combien de temps dure le film ?
items.en: How long does the movie last?
items.ipa: kɔ̃.bjɛ̃ də tɑ̃ dyʁ lə film
items.notes: "Dure" ends in a silent e, unlike "dur".

items.fr: Est-ce que le train part à midi ?
items.en: Does the train leave at noon?
items.ipa: ɛs kə lə tʁɛ̃ paʁ a mi.di

items.notes: Leave a space before the question mark.
"Est-ce que" stays fixed; only the surrounding words change.

items.fr: Pourquoi est-ce que tu es en retard ?
items.ipa: puʁ.kwa ɛs kə ty ɛ ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ

items.en: Which clothes are you wearing tonight?
items.ipa: kɛl vɛt.mɑ̃ pɔʁt ty sə swaʁ

items.fr: Est-ce que tu préfères le thé ou le café ?
items.en: Do you prefer tea or coffee?
items.ipa: ɛs kə ty pʁe.fɛʁ lə te u lə ka.fe
items.notes: "Ou" (or) has no accent, unlike "où" (where).

items.en: What do you do in the morning?
items.notes: Leave a space before the question mark.

items.en: Do you have a smaller size?
items.ipa: a.ve vu la taj ɑ̃ də.su
items.notes: Inversion "avez-vous" takes a hyphen.

items.en: What is the weather like today?

items.fr: Fait-il beau à Paris en ce moment ?
items.en: Is the weather nice in Paris right now?
items.ipa: fɛ.til bo a pa.ʁi ɑ̃ sə mɔ.mɑ̃
items.notes: Leave a space before the question mark.

items.fr: Est-ce qu'il y a du vent aujourd'hui ?
items.ipa: ɛs kil ja dy vɑ̃ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi
