items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Quelles langues","t":"which languages"},{"w":"parles-tu","t":"do you speak"},{"w":"couramment ?","t":"fluently"}]}

items.fr: Est-ce qu'il y a un supermarché près d'ici ?
items.en: Is there a supermarket near here?
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Est-ce qu'il y a","t":"is there"},{"w":"un supermarché","t":"a supermarket"},{"w":"près d'ici ?","t":"near here"}]}

items.fr: Avons-nous assez de temps pour visiter le musée ?
items.en: Do we have enough time to visit the museum?
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Avons-nous assez","t":"do we have enough"},{"w":"de temps","t":"of time"},{"w":"pour visiter","t":"to visit"},{"w":"le musée ?","t":"the museum"}]}

items.fr: Tu es prêt pour l'examen de demain ?
items.en: Are you ready for tomorrow's exam?
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Tu es prêt","t":"are you ready"},{"w":"pour l'examen","t":"for the exam"},{"w":"de demain ?","t":"tomorrow"}]}
The same question as Tu es prêt ?, with the two words swapped and a hyphen holding them together. The hyphen is not decoration: Es tu prêt ? without it is a typo rather than a question.
No t is added here, because est already ends in one. Compare A-t-il faim ?, where a has no consonant to lend and one is put in.
prête rather than prêt, because the word is describing a woman. The question form did not cause that: it would be prête in the statement too.
The nous form, and it is the longest of the twelve. Nothing special happens to it.
The one of the twelve you will hear most often, because vous is already the careful pronoun and inversion is the careful form. The two travel together.
The t on the end of sont is silent in the statement Ils sont prêts, and inversion wakes it up: this comes out as sohⁿ-TEEL.
The same question as Tu as faim ?, swapped. Said to a friend across a table it sounds oddly stiff, which is the whole subject of this lesson rather than a fault in the sentence.
A ends in a vowel and il starts with one, so a t is put between them. There is no such word as a-il. The t means nothing at all and is there only to keep the two vowels apart.
The same insertion with elle. If you can say A-t-il you can say A-t-elle, and those are the only two places in this lesson it happens.
No t is inserted, because avons already ends in a consonant. The rule only fires when a vowel would meet a vowel.
The avoir form you will meet most, and the corpus agrees: avez-vous turns up in shops, restaurants and waiting rooms far more than any other inversion on this list.
Like sont-ils, the silent t wakes up. Ils ont is said eel-ZOHⁿ and Ont-ils is said ohⁿ-TEEL, so the same two words rearrange their sounds completely.
Est-ce que loses its e in front of il. This is the fourth time you have watched French refuse to let two vowel sounds meet, and the third different way it has got out of it.
The same cut in front of elle. In fast speech ess-KEEL and ess-KEL are close enough to be worth listening for, and they are the only pair in this lesson your ear has real work to do on.
And in front of on. Two things happen at once here: que loses its e, and the n of on carries over onto est, so the middle of this comes out as kohⁿ-NEH.
The safe form of the vous question. Notice that est-ce que did not care that the pronoun changed: you bolt the same three words onto the front of anything.

A statement, and it is the same four words as the question. On the page one full stop separates them. Out loud one is a voice going down and the other is a voice going up, and nothing else differs at all.
Oui on its own is a complete answer. The rest is only there if you want to say more.
Non, then a reason. Nothing here needs a negative: saying why is friendlier than saying not.
The answer to the avoir question, and j'ai rather than je ai for the same reason est-ce qu'il is not est-ce que il.
A negative statement with a rising voice on the end, which makes it a question. The negation is the one the previous lesson taught, doing exactly what it did there; only the contour is new.
Not oui. When somebody asks you a question with a not in it and you want to disagree with the not, French has a separate word for that, and this is the only job it does.
The word for where, and everything after it is a sentence you already had.
One word changed from the sentence above and the answer changed completely.
The only one of the seven whose answer has a grammar of its own: parce que.
The word the unit description leaves out, and one you have been saying since the first lesson.

items.fr: Avec qui est-ce que tu pars ?
items.notes: The word for who, with a small word in front of it.

items.fr: Combien de temps est-ce que tu pars ?
items.en: How long are you going for?
items.ipa: /kɔ̃.bjɛ̃ də tɑ̃ ɛs kə ty paʁ/
items.respell: kohⁿ-byaⁿ duh tahⁿ ehs-kuh tü PAR
items.notes: Combien brings de with it as soon as you name the thing being counted.

items.fr: À quelle heure est-ce que tu pars ?
items.notes: Quel cannot stand alone. It takes the shape of the thing behind it.

items.fr: Où est-ce que le train part ?
items.en: Where does the train leave from?
items.notes: A real question with a real answer. It is answered with a platform number, which is not what was wanted.

items.fr: Quand est-ce que le train part ?
items.notes: One word different from the sentence above it, and it is the only word in either that was ever carrying the question.
Only one of the seven words could have asked this, and it is the word for who.
A place, so the question was where. Nothing else fits.
A time, so the question was when.

items.en: It is because it is raining.
items.notes: A reason, so the question was why. This is the only one of the seven whose answer has its own word.
A number, so the question was how many.
What somebody is like, so the question was how. Comment asks it, and the unit description omits it.
Que joined the frame and the two ran together. This is the one to reach for.
The same question with the word at the end, where it changes shape to quoi. Very common out loud.

items.fr: Qu'est-ce qui est dans le sac ?
items.notes: The thing is doing something, so qui. Nothing is between the frame and the verb.

items.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu as dans le sac ?
items.en: What do you have in the bag?
items.ipa: /kɛs kə ty a dɑ̃ lə sak/
items.respell: kehs-kuh tü a dahⁿ luh SAK
items.notes: Somebody is doing something to it, so que. There is a person between the frame and the verb.
With the accent, it is the word for where.
Without it, the same sound is the word for or. Nothing you can hear separates these two.

items.en: How many suitcases do you have?
items.notes: A consonant follows, so de keeps its vowel.

items.en: How many friends do you have?
items.notes: A vowel follows, so de loses its own. The same repair as l'ami, mon amie and n'ai.
A train is the un kind, so quel with nothing on the end.
A valise is the une kind, so quelle. Out loud this is the same word as the sentence above it.
More than one, so an s arrives, and it is silent. Still the same word out loud.
The une kind and more than one, so both endings. Four spellings and one sound, all the way down.
The frame with nothing in front of it. Put a question word there and it stops being a yes or no.

items.fr: Je me lève à sept heures.
items.en: I get up at seven o'clock.
items.notes: Reflexive verbs need a pronoun: « je » goes with « me ».

items.fr: Elle prend son petit déjeuner le matin.
items.en: She has her breakfast in the morning.
items.notes: French says « le matin » for in the morning, with no preposition.
items.prompt: Elle prend son petit déjeuner ___ matin.

items.fr: Je me réveille à huit heures chaque jour.
items.en: I wake up at eight o'clock every day.
items.notes: « chaque » is always followed by a singular noun: chaque jour.
items.prompt: Je me réveille à huit heures chaque jours.

items.fr: Le verbe est pronominal, le pronom change avec la personne.
items.en: The verb is reflexive, and the pronoun changes with the subject.
items.notes: Ex : je me lève · tu te lèves · il se lève
items.prompt: Quand utiliser « se » dans « se lever » ?

items.notes: Often used for coming back home at the end of the day.
Reflexive verb: je me maquille, elle se maquille.
Reflexive verb: je me peigne. Related noun: le peigne, the comb.
Stronger than dormir: it marks the moment you drift off. Je m'endors vite.
An afternoon rest, common after lunch.
Uses faire: je fais la sieste après le déjeuner.
The snack children eat around four in the afternoon.
Je promène le chien le soir. Note the accent change: promener, je promène.
A small daily chore: j'arrose les plantes le matin.
Literally to take the trash can outside. Je sors la poubelle le lundi.
Before a meal: je mets la table. The opposite is débarrasser la table.
After a meal: je débarrasse la table.
Son changes with the subject: je fais mon lit, tu fais ton lit.
Je repasse mes chemises. The iron itself is le fer à repasser.
Literally to pass the vacuum cleaner. Je passe l'aspirateur le samedi.
Same meaning as se doucher, built with prendre: je prends une douche.
Je prends un bain le dimanche soir. The bathtub is la baignoire.
Reflexive: je me change après le travail. Without se, changer means to change something else.
The midday break at work or school: ma pause déjeuner est à midi.
Everyday alternative to se coucher: je vais au lit à dix heures.
Last step of the day: j'éteins la lumière. The opposite is allumer.
Styling your hair, with or without a comb.
Stretching your body after waking up.
Je bâille: I am yawning.
From le mouchoir, the tissue.
Les enfants vont à l'école: the children go to school.
Many French families go every weekend.
La mosquée: the mosque.
L'église: the church.
Je rentre à la maison à six heures.
On fait une pause? Shall we take a break?
Literally, to do the fat morning.
Je me mets au lit à dix heures.
Je reste à la maison ce soir.
Also used for babysitting.
Literally, to give to eat to the baby.
Qui prépare le dîner ce soir?
Nourrir: to feed, for pets and animals.
Hanging wet laundry on the line to dry.
Folding clean laundry before putting it away.
Balayer la cuisine: to sweep the kitchen.
La poussière: the dust.
Usually done with la serpillière.
Nettoyer: to clean.
Vider: to empty.
All the beds in the house.
Ferme la porte à clé: lock the door.
To open or close the curtains.
Je mets le réveil à sept heures.
Dépêche-toi! Hurry up!
With a towel or un sèche-cheveux.

items.fr: Je me lève à sept heures tous les jours.
items.en: I get up at seven every day.
items.ipa: ʒə mə lɛv a sɛ.t œʁ tu le ʒuʁ
items.notes: “Lève” takes an accent grave because the stem vowel is stressed, unlike in “lever”.

items.fr: Le matin, je bois un jus d'orange.
items.en: In the morning, I drink an orange juice.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le matin,","t":"in the morning,"},{"w":"je bois","t":"I drink"},{"w":"un jus d'orange.","t":"an orange juice"}]}

items.fr: Il se lave les mains avant le repas.
items.en: He washes his hands before the meal.
items.ipa: /il sə lav le mɛ̃ avɑ̃ lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The nasal vowel in 'mains' is spelled with -ains but sounds like a single nasal vowel.

items.fr: Nous prenons le petit déjeuner ensemble.
items.notes: The final t in 'petit' is silent here since no liaison occurs before the consonant sound of 'déjeuner'.

items.fr: Elle se brosse les dents après le petit déjeuner.
items.en: She brushes her teeth after breakfast.
items.ipa: /ɛl sə bʁɔs le dɑ̃ apʁɛ lə pəti deʒøne/
items.notes: 'Dents' sounds identical to 'dans', so listeners must rely on context to spell it correctly.

items.fr: Tu prends ta douche le matin.
items.en: You take your shower in the morning.
items.notes: The final d in 'prends' is silent, which can tempt learners to drop the letter entirely when writing.

items.fr: Nous allons à l'école à huit heures.
items.en: We go to school at eight o'clock.
items.notes: The liaison in 'huit heures' pronounces the t of 'huit' before the vowel of 'heures'.

items.fr: Je bois un café avant de partir.
items.en: I drink a coffee before leaving.
items.ipa: /ʒə bwa œ̃ kafe avɑ̃ də paʁtiʁ/
items.notes: The nasal vowel in 'un' must be written with the silent n, not just the vowel sound alone.

items.fr: Il met son manteau et ses chaussures.
items.en: He puts on his coat and his shoes.
items.ipa: /il mɛ sɔ̃ mɑ̃to e se ʃosyʁ/
items.notes: 'Ses' sounds exactly like 'ces', so spelling depends on recognizing the possessive meaning.

items.fr: Elle prend le bus pour aller au travail.
items.en: She takes the bus to go to work.
items.ipa: /ɛl pʁɑ̃ lə bys puʁ ale o tʁavaj/
items.notes: The final d of 'prend' is never pronounced, a common source of spelling slips in dictation.

items.fr: Nous marchons jusqu'à la gare tous les jours.
items.en: We walk to the station every day.
items.ipa: /nu maʁʃɔ̃ ʒyska la ɡaʁ tu le ʒuʁ/
items.notes: Before a plural noun, 'tous' is pronounced without its final s, unlike when it stands alone as a pronoun.

items.fr: Je déjeune à midi avec mes collègues.
items.en: I have lunch at noon with my colleagues.
items.ipa: /ʒə deʒøn a midi avɛk me kɔlɛɡ/
items.notes: The unstressed e in 'je' is a mute e that learners sometimes drop or add incorrectly in writing.

items.fr: Il travaille dans un bureau au centre-ville.
items.en: He works in an office downtown.
items.ipa: /il tʁavaj dɑ̃ zœ̃ byʁo o sɑ̃tʁəvil/
items.notes: The liaison between 'dans' and 'un' produces a z sound that must not be written as an extra letter.

items.fr: Elle rentre chez elle vers dix-huit heures.
items.en: She goes home around six p.m.
items.notes: The liaison chain in 'dix-huit heures' links three sounds together and can obscure the correct spelling of each number.

items.en: We have dinner together in the evening.
items.notes: 'Ensemble' begins with a nasal vowel spelled en, easily confused with an or in when written from sound alone.

items.fr: Je regarde la télévision avant de dormir.
items.ipa: /ʒə ʁəɡaʁd la televizjɔ̃ avɑ̃ də dɔʁmiʁ/
items.notes: The mute e in 'regarde' is rarely pronounced but must still appear in the spelling.

items.fr: Il se couche tôt pendant la semaine.
items.en: He goes to bed early during the week.
items.ipa: /il sə kuʃ to pɑ̃dɑ̃ la səmɛn/
items.notes: The final t in 'tôt' is completely silent, so learners must remember it exists only in writing.

items.fr: Elle éteint la lumière avant de s'endormir.
items.en: She turns off the light before falling asleep.
items.ipa: /ɛl etɛ̃ la lymjɛʁ avɑ̃ də sɑ̃dɔʁmiʁ/
items.notes: 'Éteint' ends in a nasal vowel sound that is spelled -eint, not with a simple n.

items.fr: Nous nous levons tôt le week-end aussi.
items.en: We get up early on weekends too.
items.ipa: /nu nu ləvɔ̃ to lə wikɛnd osi/
items.notes: The two consecutive 'nous' before a reflexive verb are easy to merge into one when writing quickly.

items.fr: Tu ranges ta chambre chaque matin.
items.en: You tidy your room every morning.
items.notes: Both 'ranges' and 'chambre' contain the nasal vowel spelled an, which can be mistaken for en.

items.fr: Je prépare le déjeuner pour les enfants.
items.en: I prepare lunch for the children.
items.ipa: /ʒə pʁepaʁ lə deʒøne puʁ le zɑ̃fɑ̃/
items.notes: The liaison in 'les enfants' adds a z sound between the words that is not written as a separate letter.

items.fr: Elle part au travail à pied.
items.en: She leaves for work on foot.
items.notes: The final d in 'pied' is silent, a frequent trap since many other words ending in d behave the same way.

items.fr: Nous faisons les courses le samedi matin.
items.en: We do the shopping on Saturday morning.
items.ipa: /nu fəzɔ̃ le kuʁs lə samdi matɛ̃/
items.notes: 'Faisons' is pronounced with a schwa sound even though it is spelled with ai, an irregular pattern to memorize.

items.fr: Je me douche avant de m'habiller.
items.notes: The silent h in 'habiller' still triggers elision, so 'me' becomes m'habiller in writing.

items.fr: Il attend le bus devant chez lui.
items.en: He waits for the bus in front of his house.
items.ipa: /il atɑ̃ lə bys dəvɑ̃ ʃe lɥi/
items.notes: The final d in 'attend' is silent, matching the pattern of other present-tense endre verbs.

items.fr: Elle mange une pomme après le déjeuner.
items.en: She eats an apple after lunch.
items.ipa: /ɛl mɑ̃ʒ yn pɔm apʁɛ lə deʒøne/
items.notes: 'Une' must agree with the feminine noun 'pomme', not the masculine 'un', even though pomme starts with a consonant.

items.fr: Nous rangeons la cuisine après le dîner.
items.en: We tidy the kitchen after dinner.
items.ipa: /nu ʁɑ̃ʒɔ̃ la kɥizin apʁɛ lə dine/
items.notes: 'Rangeons' keeps an extra e before -ons to preserve the soft g sound, an irregular spelling rule for -ger verbs.

items.fr: Je sors du travail à dix-sept heures.
items.en: I leave work at five p.m.
items.ipa: /ʒə sɔʁ dy tʁavaj a diz sɛt‿œʁ/
items.notes: The liaison in 'dix-sept heures' pronounces the final consonants of both number words before the vowel.

items.fr: Elle se repose un peu avant le dîner.
items.en: She rests a little before dinner.
items.ipa: /ɛl sə ʁəpoz œ̃ pø avɑ̃ lə dine/
items.notes: The nasal vowel in 'un' is a single sound but requires writing both the vowel and the silent n.

items.fr: Nous éteignons les lumières en partant.
items.en: We turn off the lights when leaving.
items.notes: 'Éteignons' contains the gn sound spelled with ign, which is easy to misspell as in or ein.

items.en: I wake up at seven o'clock every morning.

items.fr: Je range ma chambre avant de dormir.
items.en: I tidy my room before sleeping.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je range ma chambre","t":"i tidy my room"},{"w":"avant de dormir.","t":"before sleeping"}]}

items.en: We say hello to each other before starting the meeting.

items.en: You introduce yourself with your full name.

items.notes: "aux" contracts à + les, the x is silent but liaises as z.

items.en: They introduce themselves to each other with pleasure.

items.notes: "présentent" ends in a silent ent, easy to drop the final letters.

items.fr: Je présente ma sœur à mes amis.
items.en: I introduce my sister to my friends.
items.ipa: ʒə pʁe.zɑ̃t ma sœʁ a me.z‿a.mi
items.notes: "sœur" has an œ ligature, do not write it as oe or eu.

items.fr: Le médecin se présente avant l'examen.
items.en: The doctor introduces himself before the exam.
items.ipa: lə mɛd.sɛ̃ sə pʁe.zɑ̃t a.vɑ̃ lɛg.za.mɛ̃
items.notes: "examen" starts with ex pronounced eg before a vowel, not eks.

items.en: The immigration officer introduces himself calmly.
items.notes: "calmement" keeps both m's from calme plus ment, a common doubling error.

items.fr: Bonjour, j'ai un rendez-vous à quatorze heures.
items.en: Hello, I have an appointment at two o'clock.
items.notes: "rendez-vous" keeps its hyphen and the z is silent at the end of rendez.

items.fr: Bonjour, voici mon passeport et mes papiers.
items.en: Hello, here is my passport and my papers.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ vwa.si mɔ̃ pas.pɔʁ e me pa.pje
items.notes: "et" and "est" are homophones, only "et" fits here.

items.fr: Bonjour, je cherche le service de l'immigration.
items.en: Hello, I am looking for the immigration service.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ ʒə ʃɛʁʃ lə sɛʁ.vis də li.mi.gʁa.sjɔ̃
items.notes: "cherche" has a silent h right after c, part of the ch digraph.

items.fr: Bonjour, je viens pour la visite médicale annuelle.
items.en: Hello, I am here for the annual medical exam.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ ʒə vjɛ̃ puʁ la vi.zit me.di.kal a.nɥɛl
items.notes: "annuelle" doubles the n and ends in elle, not el.

items.fr: Bonjour, je dépose mon dossier à la mairie.
items.en: Hello, I am dropping off my file at city hall.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ ʒə de.poz mɔ̃ dɔ.sje a la mɛ.ʁi
items.notes: "mairie" is written with ai, pronounced like è, not like the word mer.

items.fr: Bonjour, je viens signer mon contrat de travail.
items.en: Hello, I am here to sign my work contract.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ ʒə vjɛ̃ si.ɲe mɔ̃ kɔ̃.tʁa də tʁa.vaj
items.notes: "contrat" ends in a silent t, only heard in the plural liaison.

items.fr: Bonjour, l'entretien commence dans dix minutes.
items.en: Hello, the interview starts in ten minutes.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ lɑ̃.tʁə.tjɛ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃s dɑ̃ di mi.nyt
items.notes: "dix" loses its x sound before a consonant, pronounced "di" here.

items.fr: Bonjour, la réceptionniste note mon nom.
items.en: Hello, the receptionist writes down my name.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ la ʁe.sɛp.sjɔ.nist nɔt mɔ̃ nɔ̃
items.notes: "réceptionniste" doubles the n before iste, a frequent spelling slip.

items.fr: Bonjour, je viens pour ouvrir un compte bancaire.
items.en: Hello, I am here to open a bank account.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ ʒə vjɛ̃ puʁ u.vʁiʁ œ̃ kɔ̃t bɑ̃.kɛʁ
items.notes: "bancaire" ends in aire, not èr, though it sounds the same.

items.en: Hello, the nurse takes my blood pressure.
items.notes: "prend" ends in a silent d, only heard in liaison.

items.fr: Bonjour, le fonctionnaire demande ma carte d'identité.
items.en: Hello, the civil servant asks for my ID card.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ lə fɔ̃k.sjɔ.nɛʁ də.mɑ̃d ma kaʁt di.dɑ̃.ti.te
items.notes: "fonctionnaire" has a silent c after n, part of the cti sound like si.

items.fr: Bonjour, je viens chercher mon permis de travail.
items.en: Hello, I am here to pick up my work permit.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ ʒə vjɛ̃ ʃɛʁ.ʃe mɔ̃ pɛʁ.mi də tʁa.vaj
items.notes: "permis" ends in a silent s, do not add an extra one.

items.fr: Bonjour, l'employeur me pose quelques questions.
items.en: Hello, the employer asks me a few questions.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ lɑ̃.plwa.jœʁ mə poz kɛlk kɛs.tjɔ̃
items.notes: "quelques" keeps the qu spelling even though it sounds like k.

items.fr: Bonjour, je viens pour mon cours de français aujourd'hui.
items.en: Hello, I am here for my French class today.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ ʒə vjɛ̃ puʁ mɔ̃ kuʁ də fʁɑ̃.sɛ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi
items.notes: "aujourd'hui" is one word with a silent h, a very common misspelling.

items.fr: Bonjour, le douanier vérifie mes bagages.
items.en: Hello, the customs officer checks my bags.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ lə dwa.nje ve.ʁi.fi me ba.ɡaʒ
items.notes: "douanier" is pronounced dwa not doo-a, the ou glides into a semivowel.

items.fr: Bonjour, l'avocate me reçoit dans son bureau.
items.en: Hello, the lawyer receives me in her office.
items.ipa: bɔ̃.ʒuʁ la.vɔ.kat mə ʁə.swa dɑ̃ sɔ̃ by.ʁo
items.notes: "reçoit" needs a cedilla under the c to keep the soft s sound before o.

items.en: How are you doing since your move?
items.ipa: kɔ.mɑ̃ va ty də.pɥi tɔ̃ de.me.naʒ.mɑ̃
items.notes: "déménagement" has three e's in a row with different accents, easy to drop one.

items.fr: Je vais bien aussi, merci beaucoup à vous.
items.en: I am also doing well, thank you very much.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ bjɛ̃.n‿o.si mɛʁ.si bo.ku a vu
items.notes: "aussi" doubles the s, a single s would change the sound.

items.fr: Je vais mieux, merci de demander.
items.en: I am feeling better, thanks for asking.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ mjø mɛʁ.si də də.mɑ̃.de
items.notes: "mieux" ends in eux, not ieu, a common vowel-cluster trap.

items.fr: Il demande si tout va bien à la maison.
items.en: He asks if everything is fine at home.
items.ipa: il də.mɑ̃d si tu va bjɛ̃ a la mɛ.zɔ̃
items.notes: "si" and "s'y" are homophones, only "si" fits this sentence.

items.fr: Elle répond qu'elle va très bien aujourd'hui.
items.en: She answers that she is doing very well today.
items.ipa: ɛl ʁe.pɔ̃ kɛl va tʁɛ bjɛ̃ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi
items.notes: "qu'elle" elides que and elle, easy to forget the apostrophe.

items.en: We are well, thank you very much.
items.notes: Liaison "nous allons": the s sounds like z, silent on its own.

items.en: Do you feel better than yesterday?
items.notes: "hier" starts with a silent h, and elides with que to kjɛʁ.

items.fr: Tout se passe bien depuis votre arrivée ?
items.en: Is everything going well since your arrival?
items.ipa: tu sə pas bjɛ̃ də.pɥi vɔ.tʁa.ʁi.ve
items.notes: "arrivée" doubles the r and ends in ée for the feminine.

items.fr: Je me sens bien mieux maintenant.
items.ipa: ʒə mə sɑ̃ bjɛ̃ mjø mɛ̃t.nɑ̃
items.notes: "maintenant" has a silent e in the middle syllable when spoken quickly.

items.fr: Comment se porte votre famille ces jours-ci ?
items.en: How is your family doing these days?
items.ipa: kɔ.mɑ̃ sə pɔʁt vɔtʁ fa.mij se ʒuʁ.si
items.notes: "ces" and "ses" are homophones, context alone tells them apart.

items.fr: Au revoir, on se voit la semaine prochaine.
items.en: Goodbye, we will see each other next week.
items.ipa: o ʁə.vwaʁ ɔ̃ sə vwa la sə.mɛn pʁɔ.ʃɛn
items.notes: "prochaine" doubles the n before e for the feminine form.

items.fr: À bientôt, prenez soin de vous.
items.en: See you soon, take care of yourself.
items.ipa: a bjɛ̃.to pʁə.ne swɛ̃ də vu
items.notes: "bientôt" carries a circumflex accent on the o, easy to forget.

items.fr: Elle salue tout le monde avant de partir.
items.ipa: ɛl sa.ly tu lə mɔ̃d a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ
items.notes: "tout" here means "all" and stays invariable before "le monde".

items.fr: Ils disent au revoir avant de sortir du bureau.
items.en: They say goodbye before leaving the office.
items.ipa: il diz o ʁə.vwaʁ a.vɑ̃ də sɔʁ.tiʁ dy by.ʁo
items.notes: "disent" ends in a silent ent, do not write disent as disant.

items.fr: Nous saluons nos collègues avant de partir.
items.en: We greet our colleagues before leaving.
items.ipa: nu sa.ly.ɔ̃ no kɔ.lɛg a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ
items.notes: "nos" and "nous" are easy to mix up when writing quickly.

items.fr: Tu pars sans dire au revoir à personne.
items.en: You leave without saying goodbye to anyone.
items.ipa: ty paʁ sɑ̃ diʁ o ʁə.vwaʁ a pɛʁ.sɔn
items.notes: "sans" and "s'en" are homophones, only "sans" fits here.

items.fr: Vous quittez la salle en silence.
items.en: You leave the room in silence.
items.ipa: vu ki.te la sal ɑ̃ si.lɑ̃s
items.notes: "quittez" doubles the t, unlike quitter's single t root sound.

items.fr: Il fait un signe de la main avant de partir.
items.ipa: il fɛ.t‿œ̃ siɲ də la mɛ̃ a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ
items.notes: "signe" has a silent g that softens into the gn sound.

items.fr: Je dis au revoir à mon collègue de travail.
items.en: I say goodbye to my work colleague.
items.ipa: ʒə di o ʁə.vwaʁ a mɔ̃ kɔ.lɛg də tʁa.vaj
items.notes: "collègue" has an accent grave on the first e, easy to miss.

items.fr: On se dit à demain avant de se quitter.
items.en: We say see you tomorrow before parting.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ sə di a də.mɛ̃ a.vɑ̃ də sə ki.te
items.notes: "quitter" doubles the t, unlike its cousin "quiet" in English.

items.fr: Merci beaucoup pour ce rendez-vous rapide.
items.en: Thank you very much for this quick appointment.
items.ipa: mɛʁ.si bo.ku puʁ sə ʁɑ̃.de.vu ʁa.pid
items.notes: "rapide" ends in a silent e that still changes the preceding sound slightly.

items.fr: Je vous remercie pour votre accueil chaleureux.
items.en: I thank you for your warm welcome.
items.ipa: ʒə vu ʁə.mɛʁ.si puʁ vɔ.tʁa.kœj ʃa.lø.ʁø
items.notes: "accueil" has a tricky ue after c to keep the k sound before eil.

items.en: Thank you for listening to me carefully.
items.notes: "attentivement" doubles the t at the start, a frequent slip.

items.fr: Nous vous remercions pour votre patience.
items.en: We thank you for your patience.
items.ipa: nu vu ʁə.mɛʁ.sjɔ̃ puʁ vɔtʁ pa.sjɑ̃s
items.notes: "patience" is spelled with a t but pronounced like an s before ience.

items.fr: S'il vous plaît, montrez-moi vos papiers.
items.ipa: sil vu plɛ mɔ̃.tʁe mwa vo pa.pje
items.notes: "S'il" elides si and il, always written with an apostrophe.

items.fr: S'il te plaît, attends un petit instant.
items.notes: "attends" doubles the t and ends in a silent ds.

items.fr: De rien, ça me fait plaisir de vous aider.
items.en: You're welcome, it is my pleasure to help you.
items.ipa: də ʁjɛ̃ sa mə fɛ plɛ.ziʁ də vu.z‿e.de
items.notes: "ça" carries a cedilla to keep the soft s sound before a.

items.fr: Merci mille fois pour votre gentillesse.
items.en: Thank you a thousand times for your kindness.
items.ipa: mɛʁ.si mil fwa puʁ vɔtʁ ʒɑ̃.ti.jɛs
items.notes: "mille" ends in a silent e, and the double l stays single sound.

items.en: Excuse me, I am looking for the exit.
items.ipa: ɛk.sky.ze mwa ʒə ʃɛʁʃ la sɔʁ.ti
items.notes: "Excusez-moi" keeps the hyphen, and the x sounds like ks here.

items.en: Sorry, can you repeat the question?
items.ipa: paʁ.dɔ̃ pu.ve vu ʁe.pe.te la kɛs.tjɔ̃
items.notes: "répéter" has two accented e's in a row, easy to drop one.

items.fr: Je suis désolée, je ne trouve plus ma convocation.
items.en: I am sorry, I cannot find my summons anymore.
items.ipa: ʒə sɥi de.zɔ.le ʒə nə tʁuv ply ma kɔ̃.vɔ.ka.sjɔ̃
items.notes: "convocation" ends in tion but sounds like sion, a frequent spelling trap.

items.fr: Excusez-moi de vous déranger si tôt.
items.en: Excuse me for bothering you so early.
items.ipa: ɛk.sky.ze mwa də vu de.ʁɑ̃.ʒe si to
items.notes: "tôt" carries a circumflex accent that changes nothing in sound but is easy to forget.

items.fr: Pardon, je n'entends pas bien la question.
items.en: Sorry, I cannot hear the question well.
items.ipa: paʁ.dɔ̃ ʒə nɑ̃.tɑ̃ pa bjɛ̃ la kɛs.tjɔ̃
items.notes: "n'entends" elides ne before a vowel, always written with an apostrophe.

items.fr: Il s'excuse de manquer la réunion.
items.en: He apologizes for missing the meeting.
items.ipa: il sɛk.skyz də mɑ̃.ke la ʁe.y.njɔ̃
items.notes: "s'excuse" starts with an elided se, do not forget the apostrophe.

items.fr: Elle présente ses excuses à sa collègue.
items.ipa: ɛl pʁe.zɑ̃t se.z‿ɛk.skyz a sa kɔ.lɛg
items.notes: "excuses" starts with ex pronounced eks here before a consonant sound.

items.fr: Nous nous excusons pour ce retard.
items.notes: "excusons" softens the x to gz between vowels, unlike "excuses".

items.en: Have a good day, see you tomorrow morning.
items.notes: "journée" ends in ée for the feminine, not é alone.

items.fr: Bonne soirée à toute la famille.
items.en: Have a good evening, whole family.
items.ipa: bɔn swa.ʁe a tut la fa.mij
items.notes: "toute" agrees in the feminine here, do not write "tout".

items.fr: Bon appétit, profitez bien du repas.
items.en: Enjoy your meal, enjoy it well.
items.notes: "appétit" doubles the p and carries an accent on the first e.

items.fr: Bon voyage, et bon retour chez vous.
items.en: Safe travels, and a safe return home.
items.ipa: bɔ̃ vwa.jaʒ e bɔ̃ ʁə.tuʁ ʃe vu
items.notes: "chez" ends in a silent z, easy to write as "ché".
"Félicitations" is always plural in this expression, never singular.

items.fr: Bienvenue au Canada, tout va très bien se passer.
items.en: Welcome to Canada, everything is going to go very well.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃.və.ny o ka.na.da tu va tʁɛ bjɛ̃ sə pa.se
items.notes: "Bienvenue" is one word here, not two, unlike "bien venu".

items.fr: Bonne chance pour votre examen de français.
items.en: Good luck with your French exam.
items.ipa: bɔn ʃɑ̃s puʁ vɔ.tʁɛg.za.mɛ̃ də fʁɑ̃.sɛ
items.notes: "examen" never doubles the m, a frequent spelling error.

items.fr: Je vous souhaite une excellente journée.
items.en: I wish you an excellent day.
items.ipa: ʒə vu swɛt yn ɛk.sɛ.lɑ̃t ʒuʁ.ne
items.notes: "excellente" doubles the l, a common slip with this word.
"chers" agrees in the plural here with an s, silent in speech.

items.fr: Passez un bon dimanche en famille.
items.en: Have a good Sunday with your family.
items.ipa: pa.se œ̃ bɔ̃ di.mɑ̃ʃ ɑ̃ fa.mij
items.notes: "dimanche" is not capitalized in French, unlike in English.
Say jouer au football to talk about playing it. Le foot is the everyday short form.
Short for le basketball. Use jouer au basket. Les baskets, feminine, means sneakers.
Use jouer au tennis. The final s is pronounced.
Use jouer au rugby. Very popular in the southwest of France.
Use faire de la natation, never jouer.
Use faire du ski. Le ski also names the ski itself.
Use faire du cyclisme for the sport of riding a bike.
Use faire de la course à pied. Literally race on foot.
Use faire de la gymnastique. La gym is the short form.
Use faire du judo, like most martial arts.
Use faire de la boxe.
Use faire de l'équitation.
Aller à la pêche means to go fishing. Same word as the fruit peach.
Use faire du patinage.
Short for le volleyball. Use jouer au volley.
Use jouer au handball. The h blocks liaison and the final part sounds like bal.
Use faire de l'athlétisme.
Use jouer au golf.
Use jouer au ping-pong. Le tennis de table is the formal name.
Use faire du karaté.
Use faire de la musculation. La muscu is the casual short form.
Use faire du yoga.
Use faire du surf.
Use faire de la voile. The word also means a sail.
Use faire de l'escalade.
Use faire de la plongée for scuba or snorkel diving.
On va au stade means we are going to the stadium.
Un terrain de foot, un terrain de tennis.
A big ball, as in football or rugby. Also means balloon.
A small ball, as in tennis or golf. A big ball is un ballon.
For tennis, badminton, or ping-pong.
The net in tennis or volleyball. The final t is silent.
Both the goal frame and a scored goal. Most speakers pronounce the final t.
Mon équipe préférée means my favorite team.
Un match de foot. The plural is des matchs.
A male player. The feminine is la joueuse.
Feminine of le joueur.
Same form for a man or a woman, only the article changes.
The person who trains a team or an athlete.
Je vais à l'entraînement means I am going to practice.
The opposite is la défaite.
The opposite is la victoire.
Quel est le score means what is the score.
Une médaille d'or is a gold medal.
The feminine is la championne.
Feminine of le champion. The final syllable loses the nasal sound.
Un tournoi de tennis, like Roland-Garros.
Faire de la compétition means to compete at a serious level.
Le maillot jaune is the yellow jersey of the Tour de France.
Feminine plural. Not the sport, which is le basket.
Where players change before a match.
The referee blows un coup de sifflet.
Marquer des points means to score points.
A running track or a ski slope, depending on the sport.
Worn for cycling, skiing, or riding. Also means headphones.
Je suis dans un club de tennis means I belong to a tennis club.
Invariable noun, same form in the plural.
Often plural, les loisirs, for free time activities.
Use faire du jardinage.
Use faire du bricolage for fixing and building things at home.
Use faire de la photographie. La photo is the short form.
Always plural for the game. Use jouer aux échecs.
Use jouer aux cartes for card games.
The plural is les jeux, with an x.
Use jouer aux jeux vidéo. Vidéo never takes an s.
Faire une collection de timbres means to collect stamps.
Use faire du tricot.
Use faire de la couture.
Faire un puzzle means to do a jigsaw puzzle.
Use jouer à un jeu de société.
Jouer à for games and team sports, faire de for most other activities.
Aux is the plural of au, used before les cartes.
Faire de for activities you practice, jouer à only for games.
Du before masculine nouns, de la before feminine ones.
Marquer also works for points, marquer des points.
Reflexive verb. Je m'entraîne le samedi means I train on Saturdays.
Un match nul is a tied game.
The gn makes the ny sound, as in onion.
The opposite of gagner un match.
The action verb. The sport as an activity is faire de la natation.

items.fr: Il joue au football avec ses amis le week-end.
items.en: He plays soccer with his friends on weekends.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il joue","t":"he plays"},{"w":"au football","t":"soccer"},{"w":"avec ses amis","t":"with his friends"},{"w":"le week-end.","t":"on weekends"}]}

items.fr: Il joue au foot avec ses copains le samedi.
items.en: He plays soccer with his friends on Saturdays.
items.ipa: il ʒu o fut a.vɛk se kɔ.pɛ̃ lə sam.di
items.notes: “Au” is the required contraction of “à le”, never written separately.
{"tiles":[{"w":"Elle aime","t":"she likes"},{"w":"nager","t":"swimming"},{"w":"le week-end.","t":"on weekends"}]}

items.fr: Les enfants adorent le sport collectif.
items.notes: The liaison between les and enfants turns into a clear z sound, so listen for lezenfants as one flowing unit.

items.fr: Je fais du sport chaque matin.
items.ipa: ʒə fɛ dy spɔʁ ʃak ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: The final t in sport is never pronounced, so do not add a sound after the silent letter.
Nous adorons is linked by a liaison z sound that makes the two words sound almost joined.
The verb ending -ent in gagnent is completely silent, so the word sounds just like gagne.

items.fr: Vous êtes doués pour le tennis.
items.notes: Vous êtes liaises with a z sound, linking the two words smoothly in speech.

items.fr: Le sport rend les enfants plus forts.
items.ipa: lə spɔʁ ʁɑ̃ le.zɑ̃.fɑ̃ ply fɔʁ
items.notes: The final d in rend is silent, so nothing is heard after the nasal vowel.

items.fr: Mon ami arrive au club à midi.
items.en: My friend arrives at the club at noon.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.na.mi a.ʁiv o klœb a mi.di
items.notes: Mon ami liaises with an n sound, so it sounds like monami rather than two separate words.

items.fr: Nous marchons longtemps dans les bois.
items.en: We walk for a long time in the woods.
items.ipa: nu maʁ.ʃɔ̃ lɔ̃.tɑ̃ dɑ̃ le bwa
items.notes: The final s in bois is silent, so the word ends on the vowel sound alone.

items.fr: Ils habitent près du grand stade.
items.en: They live near the big stadium.
items.notes: The h in habitent is silent but still allows a liaison, so ils habitent sounds like ilzabitent.

items.fr: Il fait un temps idéal pour jouer.
items.en: The weather is ideal for playing.
items.ipa: il fɛ œ̃ tɑ̃ i.de.al puʁ ʒwe
items.notes: Both the p and the s in temps stay silent, leaving only the nasal vowel sound.

items.fr: Elles arrivent tôt pour le match.
items.en: They arrive early for the match.
items.notes: Elles arrivent liaises with a z sound that glides the two words together.

items.fr: Elle porte des gants chauds pour le ski.
items.en: She wears warm gloves for skiing.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁt de ɡɑ̃ ʃo puʁ lə ski
items.notes: The final t and s in gants are both silent, so only the nasal vowel is heard.

items.fr: Un athlète entraîne les jeunes joueurs.
items.en: An athlete trains the young players.
items.notes: Un athlète liaises with an n sound because the silent h in athlète does not block it.

items.fr: Les enfants courent vite sur le terrain.
items.en: The children run fast on the field.
items.ipa: le.zɑ̃.fɑ̃ kuʁ vit syʁ lə tɛ.ʁɛ̃
items.notes: The ending -ent of courent is silent, so the verb is pronounced exactly like court.

items.en: These children love swimming a lot.
items.notes: Ces enfants is joined by a liaison z sound between the two words.

items.fr: Ils perdent rarement leurs matchs à domicile.
items.en: They rarely lose their home matches.
items.ipa: il pɛʁd ʁaʁ.mɑ̃ lœʁ matʃ a dɔ.mi.sil
items.notes: The -ent ending of perdent is silent, leaving the verb sounding like perd.

items.fr: Nos amis jouent au volley ce soir.
items.en: Our friends are playing volleyball tonight.
items.ipa: no.za.mi ʒu o vɔ.lɛ sə swaʁ
items.notes: Nos amis liaises with a z sound linking the plural possessive to the noun.

items.fr: Le corps a besoin de sport régulier.
items.ipa: lə kɔʁ a bə.zwɛ̃ də spɔʁ ʁe.ɡy.lje
items.notes: Both the p and the s at the end of corps stay silent.

items.fr: Deux athlètes attendent le début du match.
items.en: Two athletes are waiting for the start of the match.
items.ipa: dø.za.tlɛt a.tɑ̃d lə de.by dy matʃ
items.notes: Deux athlètes liaises with a z sound linking the number to the noun.

items.fr: Elle regarde souvent les matchs à la télé.

items.fr: Il a mal au cou après avoir dormi dans le train.
items.en: His neck hurts after sleeping on the train.
items.ipa: il a mal o ku a.pʁɛ a.vwaʁ dɔʁ.mi dɑ̃ lə tʁɛ̃
items.notes: “cou” (neck) is a homophone of “coup” (a blow), only context decides the spelling.

items.fr: Ses yeux et ses oreilles sont très sensibles au bruit.
items.en: His eyes and ears are very sensitive to noise.
items.ipa: sɛ.z‿jø e sɛ.z‿ɔ.ʁɛj sɔ̃ tʁɛ sɑ̃.sibl o bʁɥi
items.notes: The final “s” of “ses” is pronounced as a liaison [z] before the vowel of “yeux”.

items.fr: L'épaule me fait mal depuis hier.
items.en: My shoulder has been hurting since yesterday.
items.ipa: le.pol mə fɛ mal də.pɥi jɛʁ
items.notes: “Le” elides to “L'” before the vowel-initial “épaule”.

items.fr: Elle s'est fait mal au genou en courant.
items.en: She hurt her knee while running.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle s'est fait mal au genou","t":"she hurt her knee"},{"w":"en courant.","t":"while running"}]}

items.fr: Il faut se laver les dents matin et soir.
items.en: You have to brush your teeth morning and night.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faut se laver les dents","t":"you have to brush your teeth"},{"w":"matin et soir.","t":"morning and night"}]}

items.fr: Elle a un bleu sur le bras depuis hier.
items.en: She has had a bruise on her arm since yesterday.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a un bleu","t":"she has had a bruise"},{"w":"sur le bras","t":"on her arm"},{"w":"depuis hier.","t":"since yesterday"}]}

example.en: His teeth were chattering, he was so cold.
example.fr: Il claquait des dents tellement il avait froid.

items.fr: avoir des fourmis dans les jambes
items.en: to have pins and needles in one's legs
items.ipa: avwaʁ de fuʁmi dɑ̃ le ʒɑ̃b

example.en: My legs are tingling after sitting too long.
example.fr: J'ai des fourmis dans les jambes après être resté assis trop longtemps.

example.en: He lost consciousness for a few seconds.
example.fr: Il a perdu connaissance pendant quelques secondes.

example.en: She squinted because of the sun.
example.fr: Elle plissait les yeux à cause du soleil.

example.en: He crossed his arms while waiting his turn.
example.fr: Il a croisé les bras en attendant son tour.

example.en: She fell ill after the trip.
example.fr: Elle est tombée malade après le voyage.

items.fr: Je me suis cassé le poignet en faisant du ski la semaine dernière.
items.en: I broke my wrist while skiing last week.
items.ipa: ʒə mə sɥi ka.se lə pwa.ɲɛ ɑ̃ fə.zɑ̃ dy ski la sə.mɛn dɛʁ.njɛʁ

items.fr: Elle avait très mal à la gorge et elle est allée voir le médecin.
items.en: Her throat hurt a lot and she went to see the doctor.
items.ipa: ɛl a.vɛ tʁɛ mal a la ɡɔʁʒ e ɛl ɛ.t‿a.le vwaʁ lə med.sɛ̃

items.fr: Quand j'étais enfant, j'avais souvent des otites.
items.en: When I was a child, I often had ear infections.

items.fr: Il s'est foulé la cheville pendant le match de football.
items.en: He sprained his ankle during the soccer match.
items.ipa: il sɛ fu.le la ʃə.vij pɑ̃.dɑ̃ lə matʃ də fut.bol
items.notes: "foulé" ne prend qu'un seul l, ne pas doubler comme dans "foule".

items.fr: Elle toussait beaucoup et elle a pris du sirop contre le rhume.
items.en: She was coughing a lot and took some cough syrup for her cold.
items.ipa: ɛl tu.sɛ bo.ku e ɛl a pʁi dy si.ʁo kɔ̃tʁ lə ʁym
items.notes: "toussait" garde les deux s de "tousser" même à l'imparfait.

items.fr: Quand nous étions jeunes, nous allions souvent chez le dentiste.
items.en: When we were young, we often went to the dentist.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ nu.z‿e.tjɔ̃ ʒœn nu.z‿a.ljɔ̃ su.vɑ̃ ʃe lə dɑ̃.tist
items.notes: "allions" prend deux l et un i, facile à mal orthographier à l'imparfait.

items.fr: Elle coupe les oignons avant de les faire cuire.
items.en: She cuts the onions before cooking them.
items.ipa: ɛl kup le.z‿ɔ.ɲɔ̃ a.vɑ̃ də le fɛʁ kɥiʁ
items.notes: “oignons” keeps a silent i: it sounds like “ognons”, not “oi-gnons”.

items.fr: Il a ajouté trop de sel dans la sauce.
items.en: He put too much salt in the sauce.
items.ipa: il a a.ʒu.te tʁo də sɛl dɑ̃ la sos
items.notes: “Sel” sounds exactly like “celle”, but only “sel” fits here.

items.fr: Nous coupons les légumes en petits morceaux.
items.en: We're cutting the vegetables into small pieces.
items.ipa: nu ku.pɔ̃ le le.ɡym ɑ̃ pə.ti mɔʁ.so
items.notes: The final “s” of “légumes” and “morceaux” is silent.

items.fr: Ma mère prépare toujours une soupe le dimanche soir.
items.en: My mother always makes soup on Sunday evenings.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ma mère","t":"my mother"},{"w":"prépare toujours","t":"always makes"},{"w":"une soupe","t":"soup"},{"w":"le dimanche soir.","t":"on Sunday evenings"}]}

items.fr: Il faut laisser mijoter la sauce pendant vingt minutes.
items.en: You need to let the sauce simmer for twenty minutes.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faut","t":"you need to"},{"w":"laisser mijoter","t":"let simmer"},{"w":"la sauce","t":"the sauce"},{"w":"pendant vingt minutes.","t":"for twenty minutes"}]}

items.fr: Elle a acheté des tomates au marché.
items.en: She bought tomatoes at the market.
items.ipa: /ɛl a aʃte de tɔmat o maʁʃe/
items.notes: The auxiliary a and the preposition à sound identical, only the accent marks the difference.

items.fr: Nous avons mangé une pizza délicieuse.
items.notes: Mangé, manger and mangez are all pronounced the same way, so grammar must decide the ending.

items.fr: Il va préparer le dîner ce soir.
items.en: He is going to prepare dinner tonight.
items.ipa: /il va pʁepaʁe lə dine sə swaʁ/
items.notes: The final r of the infinitive préparer is never pronounced.

items.fr: Nous allons faire les courses ce matin.
items.en: We are going to do the grocery shopping this morning.
items.notes: Nous allons links with a z liaison before the vowel of allons.

items.fr: Elle a mis la table avant le repas.
items.en: She set the table before the meal.
items.ipa: /ɛl a mi la tabl avɑ̃ lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The past participle mis ends in a silent s that is often forgotten in dictation.

items.fr: Ils ont mangé toutes les crêpes.
items.notes: Ont and on sound exactly the same, so only context shows which one is meant.

items.fr: On a préparé un gâteau pour son anniversaire.
items.en: We made a cake for his birthday.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ a pʁepaʁe œ̃ gato puʁ sɔ̃n‿anivɛʁsɛʁ/
items.notes: On is easily confused with ont since both are pronounced the same nasal sound.

items.en: Where did you buy this cheese?
items.notes: Où, meaning where, and ou, meaning or, are pronounced identically, only the accent separates them.

items.fr: Tu vas éplucher les pommes de terre.
items.en: You are going to peel the potatoes.
items.ipa: /ty va eplyʃe le pɔm də tɛʁ/
items.notes: The final r of éplucher stays silent, as in every -er infinitive.

items.fr: Elle a fait cuire les pâtes dix minutes.
items.en: She cooked the pasta for ten minutes.
items.ipa: /ɛl a fɛ kɥiʁ le pat di minyt/
items.notes: The irregular past participle fait ends in a silent t.

items.fr: Nous avons goûté la sauce avant de la servir.
items.en: We tasted the sauce before serving it.
items.ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ gute la sos avɑ̃ də la sɛʁviʁ/
items.notes: Goûté still carries the circumflex accent from goûter, even in the past participle.

items.fr: Les enfants ont bu tout le jus d'orange.
items.en: The children drank all the orange juice.
items.ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃ ɔ̃ by tu lə ʒy dɔʁɑ̃ʒ/
items.notes: Enfants liaises into ont with a hidden z sound that must still be written as two words.

items.fr: Elle va couper les carottes en rondelles.
items.en: She is going to cut the carrots into rounds.
items.ipa: /ɛl va kupe le kaʁɔt ɑ̃ ʁɔ̃dɛl/
items.notes: Like all -er infinitives, couper ends in a completely silent r.

items.fr: J'ai lavé la salade avant de la manger.
items.en: I washed the salad before eating it.
items.ipa: /ʒe lave la salad avɑ̃ də la mɑ̃ʒe/
items.notes: Lavé, laver and lavez all sound the same, so the ending must be chosen by grammar, not by ear.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté des pommes et des poires.
items.notes: Avons acheté chains two liaisons in a row that are easy to miss in fast speech.

items.fr: Il a versé l'huile dans la poêle chaude.
items.en: He poured the oil into the hot pan.
items.ipa: /il a vɛʁse lɥil dɑ̃ la pwal ʃod/
items.notes: La huile is unpronounceable, so it becomes l'huile before the vowel sound.

items.fr: Elle a préparé la soupe qu'elle a servie chaude.
items.en: She made the soup she served hot.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pʁepaʁe la sup kɛl a sɛʁvi ʃod/
items.notes: Servie is pronounced exactly like servi, but the silent added e agrees with the feminine soupe.

items.fr: On va manger dans la cuisine ce soir.
items.en: We are going to eat in the kitchen tonight.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ va mɑ̃ʒe dɑ̃ la kɥizin sə swaʁ/
items.notes: On here is easy to confuse with ont since both share the same nasal sound.

items.fr: Les invités sont arrivés avant le dîner.
items.notes: With être, arrivés adds a silent s to agree with the plural invités.

items.fr: Elle a coupé les légumes qu'elle a lavés ce matin.
items.en: She cut the vegetables she washed this morning.
items.ipa: /ɛl a kupe le legym kɛl a lave sə matɛ̃/
items.notes: Lavés sounds identical to lavé, but the silent s agrees with the plural légumes.

items.fr: J'ai coupé les légumes puis je les ai fait cuire.
items.en: I cut the vegetables then I cooked them.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai coupé","t":"i cut"},{"w":"les légumes","t":"the vegetables"},{"w":"puis","t":"then"},{"w":"je les ai fait cuire.","t":"i cooked them"}]}

items.fr: Il faut composter le billet avant de monter.

example.en: I missed the bus so I had to walk.
example.fr: J'ai raté le bus alors j'ai dû marcher.

example.en: We can take a shortcut through the park.
example.fr: On peut prendre un raccourci par le parc.

example.en: She gets carsick in the car.
example.fr: Elle a le mal des transports en voiture.

example.en: You have to change trains in Lyon.
example.fr: Il faut changer de train à Lyon.

items.fr: J'ai raté le bus, donc je suis arrivé en retard au travail.
items.en: I missed the bus, so I arrived late to work.
items.ipa: ʒe ʁa.te lə bys dɔ̃k ʒə sɥi.z‿a.ʁi.ve ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ o tʁa.vaj

items.fr: Il faisait froid et nous avons pris un taxi pour rentrer.
items.en: It was cold and we took a taxi to get home.
items.ipa: il fə.zɛ fʁwa e nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ pʁi œ̃ tak.si puʁ ʁɑ̃.tʁe

items.fr: Nous avons attendu longtemps, mais le train n'est jamais arrivé.
items.en: We waited a long time, but the train never arrived.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ a.tɑ̃.dy lɔ̃.tɑ̃ mɛ lə tʁɛ̃ n‿ɛ ʒa.mɛ a.ʁi.ve
items.notes: Ne pas oublier le "ne" devant "est jamais", facile à perdre à l'oral ; liaison train_n'est.

items.fr: Il pleuvait fort, donc nous sommes restés à la maison.
items.en: It was raining hard, so we stayed home.
items.ipa: il plœ.vɛ fɔʁ dɔ̃k nu sɔm ʁɛs.te a la mɛ.zɔ̃
items.notes: "Restés" s'accorde au pluriel avec "nous", ne pas oublier le s final.

items.fr: Elle a rangé cent feuilles blanches dans le tiroir.
items.en: She put a hundred blank sheets of paper away in the drawer.
items.ipa: ɛl a ʁɑ̃.ʒe sɑ̃ fœj blɑ̃ʃ dɑ̃ lə ti.ʁwaʁ
items.notes: The final t of “cent” stays silent here.

items.fr: Les enfants attendent leur professeur devant l'école.
items.en: The children are waiting for their teacher in front of the school.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ a.tɑ̃d lœʁ pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ də.vɑ̃ le.kɔl
items.notes: The s in “les” links to “enfants” with a z sound because of the liaison.

items.fr: L'institutrice explique l'exercice une deuxième fois.
items.en: The teacher explains the exercise a second time.
items.notes: “La institutrice” becomes “L'institutrice” because “la” elides before a vowel.

example.en: Correct your error with a red pen.
example.fr: Corrige ton erreur avec un stylo rouge.

example.en: Reread your sentence before handing it in.
example.fr: Relis ta phrase avant de la rendre.

example.en: Put your paper in your notebook.
example.fr: Range ta copie dans ton cahier.

example.en: The dictation test is on Friday.
example.fr: Le contrôle de dictée est vendredi.

example.en: The French alphabet has twenty-six letters.
example.fr: L'alphabet français compte vingt-six lettres.

example.en: Don't forget the apostrophe in 'l'école'.
example.fr: N'oublie pas l'apostrophe dans « l'école ».

example.en: The teacher dictates the text slowly.
example.fr: Le professeur dicte le texte doucement.

example.en: Pronounce each word clearly before writing it.
example.fr: Prononce bien chaque mot avant de l'écrire.

example.en: Articulate clearly so I understand the word.
example.fr: Articule bien pour que je comprenne le mot.

example.en: Read the sentence out loud.
example.fr: Lis la phrase à haute voix.

example.en: Don't forget to hand in your paper on time.
example.fr: N'oublie pas de rendre ta copie à temps.

example.en: First write your text as a draft.
example.fr: Écris d'abord ton texte au brouillon.

example.en: Skip a line between each sentence.
example.fr: Saute une ligne entre chaque phrase.

example.en: The dictation takes up a whole page.
example.fr: La dictée occupe une page entière.

example.en: This word comes from the second chapter.
example.fr: Ce mot vient du deuxième chapitre.

example.en: The dictation text is about a trip.
example.fr: Le texte de la dictée parle d'un voyage.

example.en: Write a summary of the text in three sentences.
example.fr: Écris un résumé du texte en trois phrases.

example.en: Give an example with this word.
example.fr: Donne un exemple avec ce mot.

example.en: Write your answer in a complete sentence.
example.fr: Écris ta réponse en une phrase complète.

example.en: There are three questions after the text.
example.fr: Il y a trois questions après le texte.

example.en: You need to memorize the spelling of this word.
example.fr: Il faut mémoriser l'orthographe de ce mot.

example.en: Learn this poem by heart for Friday.
example.fr: Apprends ce poème par cœur pour vendredi.

example.en: Her dictation grades are on the report card.
example.fr: Ses notes de dictée sont sur le bulletin scolaire.

example.en: French is my favourite subject.
example.fr: Le français est ma matière préférée.

items.en: the start of the school year

example.en: Dictations start again right after the school year begins.
example.fr: Les dictées reprennent dès la rentrée scolaire.

example.en: The dictation counts toward the final assessment.
example.fr: La dictée compte pour l'évaluation finale.

example.en: She earned her diploma after the exam.
example.fr: Elle a obtenu son diplôme après l'examen.

example.en: You need to write well to pass an exam.
example.fr: Il faut bien écrire pour réussir un examen.

items.fr: Mon fils commence l'école demain matin.

items.fr: Nous avons inscrit notre fille à l'école du quartier.

items.fr: Le directeur adjoint surveille la cour pendant la récréation.
items.en: The vice principal watches the yard during recess.
items.ipa: lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ ad.ʒwɛ̃ syʁ.vɛj la kuʁ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la ʁe.kʁe.a.sjɔ̃
items.notes: "adjoint" se termine par -oint, garder le t muet à l'écrit.

items.fr: J'ai signé le registre d'absence à l'accueil de l'école.
items.en: I signed the absence register at the school's front desk.
items.ipa: ʒe si.ɲe lə ʁə.ʒistʁ dab.sɑ̃s a l‿a.kœj də l‿e.kɔl
items.notes: "accueil" prend deux c et se prononce comme "a-keuille", pas "ak-seuille".

items.fr: Les enseignants ont préparé un examen commun pour tous les élèves.
items.en: The teachers prepared a common exam for all the students.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.sɛ.ɲɑ̃.z‿ɔ̃ pʁe.pa.ʁe œ̃.n‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ kɔ.mœ̃ puʁ tu le.z‿e.lɛv
items.notes: "commun" prend deux m, à ne pas confondre avec "comment".

items.fr: Ma fille a terminé ses devoirs avant de regarder la télévision.
items.en: My daughter finished her homework before watching television.
items.ipa: ma fij a tɛʁ.mi.ne se də.vwaʁ a.vɑ̃ də ʁə.gaʁ.de la te.le.vi.zjɔ̃
items.notes: "terminé" prend un seul m et un seul n, faute fréquente de doublement.

items.fr: Nous avons reçu le calendrier scolaire par courriel hier.
items.en: We received the school calendar by email yesterday.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʁə.sy lə ka.lɑ̃.dʁi.je sko.lɛʁ paʁ ku.ʁjɛl i.ɛʁ
items.notes: "courriel" prend deux r, contraction de courrier électronique.

items.fr: L'élève a demandé la permission de sortir de la classe.
items.en: The student asked for permission to leave the classroom.
items.ipa: l‿e.lɛv a də.mɑ̃.de la pɛʁ.mi.sjɔ̃ də sɔʁ.tiʁ də la klas
items.notes: "permission" prend deux s pour garder le son s entre voyelles.

items.fr: Les enfants apprennent à lire dès l'âge de six ans.
items.en: Children learn to read from the age of six.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Les enfants","t":"children"},{"w":"apprennent à lire","t":"learn to read"},{"w":"dès l'âge de six ans.","t":"from the age of six"}]}

items.fr: La nouvelle directrice a visité toutes les classes.
items.en: The new principal visited every classroom.
items.ipa: la nu.vɛl di.ʁɛk.tʁis a vi.zi.te tut le klas
items.notes: “nouvelle” takes the feminine form because “directrice” is a woman.

items.fr: Où est-ce que tu ranges tes affaires de sport ?
items.en: Where do you keep your sports gear?
items.ipa: u ɛs kə ty ʁɑ̃ʒ te.z‿a.fɛʁ də spɔʁ
items.notes: “où” with the accent means “where”, unlike “ou” meaning “or”.

items.fr: Chaque élève doit apporter son propre goûter.
items.en: Each student has to bring their own snack.
items.ipa: ʃak e.lɛv dwa a.pɔʁ.te sɔ̃ pʁɔpʁ gu.te
items.notes: “chaque” is always singular, so “élève” stays without a plural s.

items.fr: Le directeur a annoncé une sortie scolaire pour vendredi.
items.en: The principal announced a school outing for Friday.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le directeur","t":"the principal"},{"w":"a annoncé","t":"announced"},{"w":"une sortie scolaire","t":"a school outing"},{"w":"pour vendredi.","t":"for Friday"}]}

items.fr: Range tes affaires tout de suite, s'il te plaît.
items.en: Put your things away right now, please.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Range tes affaires","t":"put your things away"},{"w":"tout de suite,","t":"right now,"},{"w":"s'il te plaît.","t":"please"}]}

items.fr: Les élèves ont un contrôle de grammaire demain matin.
items.en: The students have a grammar test tomorrow morning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Les élèves","t":"the students"},{"w":"ont","t":"have"},{"w":"un contrôle de grammaire","t":"a grammar test"},{"w":"demain matin.","t":"tomorrow morning"}]}

example.en: He failed his chemistry exam.
example.fr: Il a échoué à son examen de chimie.

example.en: She got her diploma last year.
example.fr: Elle a obtenu son diplôme l'année dernière.

example.en: The class council meeting was held yesterday afternoon.
example.fr: Le conseil de classe avait lieu hier après-midi.

example.en: The parent-teacher meeting started at six p.m.
example.fr: La réunion de parents commençait à dix-huit heures.

items.fr: Hier, mon fils a oublié son cahier de mathématiques à la maison.
items.en: Yesterday, my son forgot his math notebook at home.
items.ipa: jɛʁ mɔ̃ fis a u.bli.e sɔ̃ ka.je də ma.te.ma.tik a la mɛ.zɔ̃

items.fr: Quand j'étais petite, j'aimais beaucoup l'école.
items.en: When I was little, I really liked school.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ ʒe.tɛ pə.tit ʒɛ.mɛ bo.ku l‿e.kɔl

items.fr: Le professeur a corrigé nos copies pendant la récréation.
items.en: The teacher corrected our papers during recess.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fe.sœʁ a kɔ.ʁi.ʒe no kɔ.pi pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la ʁe.kʁe.a.sjɔ̃
items.notes: "Corrigé" ends in -é (past participle after avoir), not -er like the infinitive, easy to confuse when writing from dictation.

items.fr: Quand il était petit, il oubliait souvent son cartable.
items.en: When he was little, he often forgot his school bag.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ i.l‿e.tɛ pə.ti i.l‿u.bli.jɛ su.vɑ̃ sɔ̃ kaʁ.tabl
items.notes: Imparfait ending "-ait" sounds identical to "-aient" and "-é", a common spelling trap; also a silent final t in "petit".

items.fr: Mes parents habitent à la campagne depuis dix ans.
items.en: My parents have lived in the countryside for ten years.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mes parents","t":"my parents"},{"w":"habitent","t":"have lived"},{"w":"à la campagne","t":"in the countryside"},{"w":"depuis dix ans.","t":"for ten years"}]}

items.fr: Mes parents sont nés en Belgique.
items.en: My parents were born in Belgium.
items.ipa: me pa.ʁɑ̃ sɔ̃ ne ɑ̃ bɛl.ʒik
items.notes: “nés” takes an “s” because the passé composé with “être” agrees with the plural subject “mes parents”.

items.fr: Ma tante habite à côté de chez nous.
items.en: My aunt lives right next door to us.
items.ipa: ma tɑ̃t a.bit a ko.te də ʃe nu
items.notes: “à” needs a grave accent here since it's the preposition, not the verb “a” from avoir.

items.fr: Elle rend visite à sa grand-mère chaque dimanche.
items.en: She visits her grandmother every Sunday.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle rend visite à","t":"she visits"},{"w":"sa grand-mère","t":"her grandmother"},{"w":"chaque dimanche.","t":"every Sunday"}]}

example.en: We moved close to my grandparents last year.
example.fr: Nous avons déménagé près de mes grands-parents l'année dernière.

items.en: to settle in, to move in

example.en: My sister moved in with us during the summer.
example.fr: Ma sœur s'est installée chez nous pendant l'été.

example.en: Children grow up fast.
example.fr: Les enfants grandissent vite.

example.en: I remember my childhood fondly.
example.fr: Je me souviens de mon enfance avec joie.

items.fr: Mon père a téléphoné et ma mère a répondu tout de suite.
items.en: My father called and my mother answered right away.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pɛʁ a te.le.fɔ.ne e ma mɛʁ a ʁe.pɔ̃.dy tu də sɥit

items.fr: Mes grands-parents étaient fatigués, mais ils ont continué la fête.
items.en: My grandparents were tired, but they continued the party.
items.ipa: me gʁɑ̃ pa.ʁɑ̃ e.tɛ fa.ti.ge mɛ i.l‿ɔ̃ kɔ̃.ti.nɥe la fɛt

items.fr: Mon oncle a acheté une maison et il a invité toute la famille.
items.en: My uncle bought a house and he invited the whole family.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.n‿ɔ̃kl a a.ʃ(ə).te yn mɛ.zɔ̃ e i.l‿a ɛ̃.vi.te tut la fa.mij
items.notes: « a acheté » : deux mots séparés, ne pas oublier l'auxiliaire avoir.

items.fr: Ma tante était malade, mais elle est venue au mariage quand même.
items.en: My aunt was sick, but she came to the wedding anyway.
items.ipa: ma tɑ̃t e.tɛ ma.lad mɛ ɛ.l‿ɛ və.ny o ma.ʁjaʒ kɑ̃ mɛm
items.notes: « venue » s'accorde au féminin avec le sujet elle, ne pas oublier le e final.

items.fr: Il est huit heures moins le quart.
Nous avons repeint les volets en vert cet été.
items.en: We repainted the shutters green this summer.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʁə.pɛ̃ le vɔ.lɛ ɑ̃ vɛʁ sɛ.t‿e.te
items.notes: “Repeint” stays invariable even though “volets” is plural, since the object follows the verb.

items.fr: Le grenier est plein de vieux cartons poussiéreux.
items.en: The attic is full of old, dusty boxes.
items.ipa: lə ɡʁə.nje ɛ plɛ̃ də vjø kaʁ.tɔ̃ pu.sje.ʁø
items.notes: The final “x” of “vieux” is silent.

items.fr: Nous rangeons le salon tous les samedis matin.
items.en: We tidy up the living room every Saturday morning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous rangeons","t":"we tidy up"},{"w":"le salon","t":"the living room"},{"w":"tous les samedis matin.","t":"every Saturday morning"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons déménagé dans un nouvel appartement.
items.en: We moved into a new apartment.
items.notes: The past participle "déménagé" sounds identical to the infinitive "déménager", so the ending must be chosen from grammar, not sound.

items.fr: Elle a peint les murs du salon en bleu.
items.en: She painted the living room walls blue.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pɛ̃ le myʁ dy sa.lɔ̃ ɑ̃ blø/
items.notes: "peint" ends in a nasal sound with a silent final "t", an irregular past participle spelling.

items.fr: Nous allons repeindre la cuisine ce week-end.
items.en: We are going to repaint the kitchen this weekend.
items.notes: Liaison links "nous" and "allons" with a /z/ sound before the verb.

items.fr: Les voisins ont fait beaucoup de bruit hier soir.
items.en: The neighbors made a lot of noise last night.
items.ipa: /le vwa.zɛ̃ ɔ̃ fɛ bo.ku də bʁɥi jɛʁ swaʁ/
items.notes: "ont" (they have) sounds like "on", so check the plural subject "les voisins" to know it takes "ont".

items.fr: J'ai acheté des étagères pour la chambre.
items.en: I bought some shelves for the bedroom.
items.ipa: /ʒe aʃ.te de ze.ta.ʒɛʁ puʁ la ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: "acheté" ends in the same sound as the infinitive "acheter", so only the auxiliary "ai" shows it is a past participle.

items.fr: Où as-tu rangé les clés de la maison?
items.en: Where did you put the house keys?
items.ipa: /u a ty ʁɑ̃.ʒe le kle də la mɛ.zɔ̃/
items.notes: "où" (where, with accent) must not be confused with "ou" (or), even though both sound the same.

items.fr: Ma mère a nettoyé toute la maison ce matin.
items.en: My mother cleaned the whole house this morning.
items.ipa: /ma mɛʁ a nɛ.twa.je tut la mɛ.zɔ̃ sə ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: "nettoyé" stays masculine singular because the direct object "la maison" comes after the verb, not before.

items.fr: Ils vont poser un nouveau parquet dans le couloir.
items.en: They are going to lay new flooring in the hallway.
items.ipa: /il vɔ̃ po.ze œ̃ nu.vo paʁ.kɛ dɑ̃ lə ku.lwaʁ/
items.notes: The final "t" of "vont" is silent, and "parquet" also ends in a silent "t".

items.fr: Nous avons enfin fini les travaux de la salle de bain.
items.en: We have finally finished the bathroom renovations.
items.ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃ fi.ni le tʁa.vo də la sal də bɛ̃/
items.notes: Two liaisons in a row link "nous avons" and "avons enfin" with /z/ sounds.

items.fr: Le propriétaire va augmenter le loyer en janvier.
items.en: The landlord is going to raise the rent in January.
items.ipa: /lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ va oɡ.mɑ̃.te lə lwa.je ɑ̃ ʒɑ̃.vje/
items.notes: "en" before a consonant makes a nasal sound with no separate "n" pronounced.

items.fr: Elle a déjà fini de ranger sa chambre.
items.en: She has already finished tidying her room.
items.ipa: /ɛl a de.ʒa fi.ni də ʁɑ̃.ʒe sa ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: "déjà" always keeps its grave accent on the final "a" even though nothing in the pronunciation signals it.

items.fr: J'ai nettoyé la salle de bains ce matin.
items.en: I cleaned the bathroom this morning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai nettoyé","t":"i cleaned"},{"w":"la salle de bains","t":"the bathroom"},{"w":"ce matin.","t":"this morning"}]}

items.fr: Nous allons repeindre la cuisine la semaine prochaine.
items.en: We are going to repaint the kitchen next week.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous allons repeindre","t":"we are going to repaint"},{"w":"la cuisine","t":"the kitchen"},{"w":"la semaine prochaine.","t":"next week"}]}

items.fr: Mon frère a réparé le robinet qui fuyait.
items.en: My brother fixed the leaking faucet.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon frère","t":"my brother"},{"w":"a réparé","t":"repaired"},{"w":"le robinet qui fuyait.","t":"the leaking faucet"}]}

items.fr: Elle va acheter un nouveau canapé pour le salon.
items.en: She is going to buy a new sofa for the living room.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle va acheter","t":"she is going to buy"},{"w":"un nouveau canapé","t":"a new sofa"},{"w":"pour le salon.","t":"for the living room"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons signé le bail pour l'appartement.
items.en: We signed the lease for the apartment.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons signé","t":"we signed"},{"w":"le bail","t":"the lease"},{"w":"pour l'appartement.","t":"for the apartment"}]}

items.fr: Je vais ranger le garage ce week-end.
items.en: I am going to tidy the garage this weekend.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je vais ranger","t":"i am going to tidy"},{"w":"le garage","t":"the garage"},{"w":"ce week-end.","t":"this weekend"}]}

items.fr: Le propriétaire a augmenté le loyer en janvier.
items.en: The landlord raised the rent in January.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le propriétaire","t":"the landlord"},{"w":"a augmenté","t":"increased"},{"w":"le loyer en janvier.","t":"the rent in january"}]}

items.fr: Elle a accroché des rideaux dans la chambre.
items.en: She hung curtains in the bedroom.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a accroché","t":"she hung"},{"w":"des rideaux","t":"curtains"},{"w":"dans la chambre.","t":"in the bedroom"}]}

items.fr: Nous allons déménager dans un mois.
items.en: We are going to move in a month.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous","t":"we"},{"w":"allons déménager","t":"are going to move"},{"w":"dans un mois.","t":"in a month"}]}

items.fr: J'ai perdu les clés de l'appartement.
items.en: I lost the keys to the apartment.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai perdu","t":"i lost"},{"w":"les clés","t":"the keys"},{"w":"de l'appartement.","t":"to the apartment"}]}

items.fr: Les prix du marché ont un peu baissé cette semaine.
items.en: Market prices have gone down a little this week.
items.ipa: le pʁi dy maʁ.ʃe ɔ̃.t‿œ̃ pø bɛ.se sɛt sə.mɛn
items.notes: “Ont un” requires a liaison, pronounced “ɔ̃.t‿œ̃”.

items.fr: Elle a acheté un panier plein de tomates bien mûres.
items.en: She bought a basket full of nice, ripe tomatoes.
items.ipa: ɛl.z‿a a.ʃə.te œ̃ pa.nje plɛ̃ də tɔ.mat bjɛ̃ myʁ
items.notes: “Mûres” agrees in the feminine plural with “tomates”.

items.fr: Il y a beaucoup de monde au marché le dimanche.
items.en: There are a lot of people at the market on Sundays.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il y a beaucoup de monde","t":"there are a lot of people"},{"w":"au marché","t":"at the market"},{"w":"le dimanche.","t":"on Sundays"}]}

items.fr: Nous choisissons toujours les fruits les plus mûrs.
items.en: We always pick the ripest fruit.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous choisissons toujours","t":"we always pick"},{"w":"les fruits les plus mûrs.","t":"the ripest fruit"}]}

items.en: to do one's shopping at the market
to go to the market in the morning
to ask the price before buying

items.fr: comparer les prix entre les étals
items.respell: kohn-pah-RAY lay pree ahntr lay zay-TAL

items.fr: choisir les fruits les plus mûrs
items.respell: shwah-ZEER lay frwee lay plü MÜR

items.fr: payer en espèces ou par carte
items.en: to pay in cash or by card
items.respell: peh-YAY ahn ness-pess oo par KART

items.fr: faire la queue devant le stand
items.en: to wait in line in front of the stall
items.respell: fehr lah kuh duh-vahn luh STAHND

items.en: to fill one's basket with groceries

items.fr: peser les légumes avant de payer
items.en: to weigh the vegetables before paying
items.respell: puh-ZAY lay lay-güm ah-vahn duh peh-YAY

items.en: to taste a piece of cheese

items.fr: arriver tôt pour éviter la foule
items.en: to arrive early to avoid the crowd
items.respell: ah-ree-VAY toh poor ay-vee-TAY lah FOOL

items.en: to take advantage of low prices
to ask for a paper bag
to give change to the customer

items.fr: flâner entre les étals du marché
items.en: to stroll between the market stalls
items.respell: flah-NAY ahntr lay zay-tal dü mar-SHAY

items.fr: Hier, j'ai acheté des fraises au marché.
items.en: Yesterday, I bought strawberries at the market.
items.ipa: /jɛʁ ʒe aʃ.te de fʁɛz o maʁ.ʃe/
items.notes: Acheté ends in a sound identical to acheter and achetez, so the ending must be chosen by grammar, not sound.

items.fr: Nous avons choisi les meilleurs fromages.
items.notes: Liaison between nous and avons adds a z sound not visible in either word alone.

items.fr: Elle a payé avec sa carte bancaire.
items.en: She paid with her bank card.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pɛ.je a.vɛk sa kaʁt bɑ̃.kɛʁ/
items.notes: Payé sounds the same as payer and payez, so the past participle ending relies on grammar, not sound.

items.fr: Ils sont allés au marché tôt le matin.
items.en: They went to the market early in the morning.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ a.le o maʁ.ʃe to lə ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: Allés takes a silent plural s to agree with ils because it uses the auxiliary être.

items.fr: Le vendeur a pesé les tomates.
items.notes: Pesé ends in the same sound as peser, a frequent past participle confusion.

items.fr: Nous allons acheter du pain demain.
items.en: We are going to buy bread tomorrow.
items.notes: Liaison between nous and allons produces a z sound that signals the plural subject.

items.fr: Elle va goûter le fromage de chèvre.
items.en: She is going to taste the goat cheese.
items.ipa: /ɛl va gu.te lə fʁɔ.maʒ də ʃɛvʁ/
items.notes: The circumflex on goûter is silent but must be written, marking a historical lost s.

items.fr: Vous avez trouvé des fruits mûrs.
items.notes: Trouvé sounds identical to trouver and trouvez, so only grammar tells you which ending to write.

items.fr: Les enfants ont mangé toutes les cerises.
items.en: The children ate all the cherries.
items.notes: Ont (have) is a homophone of on (one), distinguished only by grammatical context.

items.fr: On a acheté beaucoup de légumes.
items.en: We bought a lot of vegetables.
items.notes: On sounds like ont, so writers must rely on meaning to choose the right spelling.

items.fr: Où as-tu trouvé ces belles fleurs ?
items.en: Where did you find these beautiful flowers?
items.ipa: /u a ty tʁu.ve se bɛl flœʁ/
items.notes: Où (where) carries an accent to distinguish it from ou (or), though both sound identical.

items.fr: Elle a demandé le prix des poires.
items.en: She asked the price of the pears.
items.ipa: /ɛl a də.mɑ̃.de lə pʁi de pwaʁ/
items.notes: Demandé ends the same as demander, a common past participle spelling trap.

items.fr: Nous avons marché longtemps entre les étals.
items.en: We walked for a long time between the stalls.
items.notes: Longtemps contains two nasal vowels and a silent final s, easy to misspell.

items.fr: Ils ont goûté les olives avant d'acheter.
items.en: They tasted the olives before buying.
items.notes: De acheter elides to d'acheter before the vowel-initial verb.

items.fr: Le marchand a donné la monnaie à Paul.
items.en: The merchant gave the change to Paul.
items.ipa: /lə maʁ.ʃɑ̃ a dɔ.ne la mɔ.nɛ a pɔl/
items.notes: The sentence contains both a (has) and à (to), which sound identical but are spelled differently.

items.fr: Elle a pris deux kilos de pommes.
items.en: She took two kilos of apples.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pʁi dø ki.lo də pɔm/
items.notes: The final s of the past participle pris is silent, easy to drop in dictée.

items.fr: On va négocier le prix du poisson.
items.en: We are going to negotiate the price of the fish.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ va ne.gɔ.sje lə pʁi dy pwa.sɔ̃/
items.notes: On and poisson both carry nasal vowels that beginners often under-pronounce when writing.

items.fr: Les clients ont fait la queue longtemps.
items.en: The customers waited in line for a long time.
items.ipa: /le kli.jɑ̃ ɔ̃ fɛ la kø lɔ̃.tɑ̃/
items.notes: Ont (have) must not be confused with its homophone on (one), a frequent dictée error.

items.fr: Il a vendu tous ses légumes ce matin.
items.en: He sold all his vegetables this morning.
items.ipa: /il a vɑ̃.dy tu se le.gym sə ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: The final s of tous is silent before a consonant, unlike when it stands alone as a pronoun.

items.fr: Nous avons mis les fruits dans un sac.
items.en: We put the fruits in a bag.
items.notes: Dans and un both end in nasal vowels that liaison links with a z sound.

items.fr: Elle est arrivée tôt pour choisir les meilleurs produits.
items.en: She arrived early to choose the best products.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve to puʁ ʃwa.ziʁ le mɛ.jœʁ pʁɔ.dɥi/
items.notes: Arrivée takes a silent feminine e to agree with elle since it uses the auxiliary être.

items.fr: Ils vont vendre des fleurs demain matin.
items.en: They are going to sell flowers tomorrow morning.
items.ipa: /il vɔ̃ vɑ̃dʁ de flœʁ də.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃/
