items.fr: Le litige avec l'entrepreneur porte sur des malfaçons dans la toiture.
items.en: The dispute with the contractor concerns defects in the roofing.
items.notes: 'Porter sur' means 'to concern/be about'; 'malfaçon' is a legal-technical term for shoddy workmanship, common in renovation disputes.

items.fr: Si les travaux avaient été mieux supervisés, les fissures n'auraient jamais fait leur apparition.
items.en: If the work had been better supervised, the cracks would never have appeared.
items.notes: Third conditional: si + plus-que-parfait, then conditionnel passé; the auxiliary 'auraient' takes 'être' agreement rules only for être-verbs, here 'avoir' stays invariable.

items.fr: Le notaire nous a expliqué les frais de mutation liés à l'achat du bien.
items.en: The notary explained to us the transfer fees related to the purchase of the property.
items.notes: 'Frais de mutation' are the transfer taxes paid when buying property in France; 'bien' here means a piece of real estate, not 'good' in the moral sense.

items.fr: Bien que le diagnostic énergétique soit obligatoire, certains vendeurs le négligent.
items.en: Although the energy assessment is mandatory, some sellers neglect it.
items.notes: 'Bien que' requires the subjunctive; 'soit' is the subjunctive of 'être', not the indicative 'est'.

items.fr: Les copropriétaires se sont opposés à la surélévation de l'immeuble proposée par le promoteur.
items.en: The co-owners opposed the developer's proposed addition of extra floors to the building.
items.notes: 'S'opposer à' takes 'à', not a direct object; the reflexive past participle 'opposés' agrees with the plural masculine subject.

items.fr: Il aurait fallu obtenir un permis de construire avant d'entamer les travaux d'extension.
items.en: A building permit should have been obtained before starting the extension work.
items.notes: 'Il aurait fallu' expresses regret about a missed obligation in the past; impersonal 'falloir' never agrees with any subject.

items.fr: Le syndic a fait appel à un huissier pour constater les dégâts causés par la fuite.
items.en: The building manager called in a bailiff to record the damage caused by the leak.
items.notes: 'Faire appel à quelqu'un' means to call on someone's services; 'huissier' is a legal officer who documents facts formally.

items.fr: La rénovation énergétique du logement a permis de réduire la facture de chauffage de moitié.
items.en: The energy renovation of the home cut the heating bill in half.
items.notes: 'Permettre de' + infinitive means 'to allow/make possible'; do not add a preposition after 'réduire'.

items.fr: Nous contestons la répartition des charges de copropriété telle qu'elle figure sur l'avis annuel.
items.en: We are disputing the allocation of co-ownership fees as it appears on the annual statement.
items.notes: 'Telle qu'elle' agrees in gender with 'répartition' (feminine); it means 'as it' and elides 'que' before the vowel.

items.fr: Le tribunal a tranché en faveur des propriétaires lésés par le retard du chantier.
items.en: The court ruled in favor of the owners harmed by the delay in the construction project.
items.notes: 'Trancher en faveur de' is a formal expression meaning 'to rule in favor of'; 'lésés' means 'harmed/wronged', a past participle used adjectivally.

items.fr: L'assurance habitation ne couvre pas les dégâts dus à un défaut d'entretien.
items.en: Home insurance does not cover damage due to lack of maintenance.
items.notes: 'Dû à' agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies; here 'dus' agrees with plural masculine 'dégâts'.

items.fr: Quoi qu'en pense l'agent immobilier, ce bien est surestimé par rapport au marché local.
items.en: Whatever the real estate agent thinks, this property is overpriced relative to the local market.
items.notes: 'Quoi que' + subjunctive means 'whatever'; distinguish from 'quoique' (although), which is written as one word.

items.fr: Le compromis de vente prévoit une clause suspensive liée à l'obtention du prêt.
items.en: The preliminary sale agreement includes a contingency clause tied to obtaining the loan.
items.notes: 'Compromis de vente' is the preliminary sale contract; 'clause suspensive' is a legal term for a contingency clause.

items.fr: Malgré les mises en demeure envoyées au bailleur, les travaux n'ont toujours pas commencé.
items.en: Despite the formal notices sent to the landlord, the work still has not started.
items.notes: 'Mise en demeure' is a formal legal notice; 'malgré' takes a noun directly, never followed by 'que'.

items.fr: L'expert a estimé que les dégâts des eaux dataient de plusieurs mois.
items.en: The expert estimated that the water damage dated back several months.
items.notes: 'Dater de' means 'to date from'; the imperfect 'dataient' expresses a state that existed over an unspecified duration in the past.

items.fr: Nous avons dû renégocier le prêt immobilier après la hausse des taux d'intérêt.
items.en: We had to renegotiate the mortgage after the rise in interest rates.
items.notes: 'Prêt immobilier' specifically means a mortgage; 'hausse' and 'baisse' are common nouns for rises and falls in rates or prices.

items.fr: Le voisinage s'est plaint que les travaux de rénovation empiètent sur l'espace commun.
items.en: The neighborhood complained that the renovation work encroaches on the shared space.
items.notes: 'Se plaindre que' can take the indicative or subjunctive; 'empiéter sur' means 'to encroach on'.

items.fr: En cas de sinistre, il convient de prévenir l'assurance dans les cinq jours ouvrés.
items.en: In the event of a claim, the insurer must be notified within five business days.
items.notes: 'Il convient de' is a formal, impersonal way of saying 'it is advisable/required to'; 'ouvré' means 'working' as in business days.

items.fr: Le prix au mètre carré a fortement grimpé dans ce quartier au cours des cinq dernières années.
items.en: The price per square meter has risen sharply in this neighborhood over the past five years.
items.notes: 'Au cours de' means 'over/during'; 'grimper' informally means 'to climb/rise' and is common in describing price trends.

items.fr: Certains propriétaires hésitent à louer de peur que les locataires ne paient pas à temps.
items.en: Some owners hesitate to rent out for fear that tenants might not pay on time.
items.notes: 'De peur que' triggers the subjunctive and often the expletive 'ne', which carries no negative meaning here.

items.fr: L'agence immobilière a été mise en cause pour avoir dissimulé des vices cachés.
items.en: The real estate agency was implicated for having concealed hidden defects.
items.notes: 'Vice caché' is a legal term for a hidden defect in a property sale; 'mettre en cause' means to implicate or hold responsible.

items.fr: Une fois la toiture refaite, la maison a repris de la valeur sur le marché.
items.en: Once the roof was redone, the house regained value on the market.
items.notes: 'Une fois' + past participle is a concise way to express 'once something has been done', without needing a full clause.

items.fr: Le propriétaire bailleur doit respecter un préavis avant de donner congé au locataire.
items.en: The landlord must respect a notice period before terminating the tenant's lease.
items.notes: 'Donner congé' is the formal legal phrase for terminating a lease; 'préavis' means notice period.

items.fr: Ils regrettent de ne pas avoir fait inspecter la charpente avant de signer l'acte de vente.
items.en: They regret not having had the roof frame inspected before signing the deed of sale.
items.notes: 'Regretter de ne pas avoir fait' expresses regret about a past omission; 'faire inspecter' is a causative construction meaning 'to have inspected'.

items.fr: La médiation entre voisins a permis d'éviter un procès coûteux concernant la mitoyenneté.
items.en: Mediation between neighbors made it possible to avoid a costly lawsuit over the shared boundary wall.
items.notes: 'Mitoyenneté' refers to a shared wall or boundary between two properties, a common legal term in French property disputes.

example.en: The buyers discovered a hidden defect after the purchase.

example.en: The dispute was settled in court.
example.fr: Le litige a été réglé devant le tribunal.

example.en: The ten-year warranty covers major construction defects.
example.fr: La garantie décennale couvre les gros défauts de construction.

example.en: They redid the attic's thermal insulation.
example.fr: Ils ont refait l'isolation thermique du grenier.

example.en: They plan to renovate the kitchen this year.

example.en: They want to extend the house with an addition.

example.en: The renovation created a nice capital gain.

example.en: The property inspection report flags wiring that needs redoing.
example.fr: Le diagnostic immobilier signale une installation électrique à refaire.

example.en: The landlord sent the tenant a formal notice.
example.fr: Le propriétaire a envoyé une mise en demeure au locataire.

example.en: The insurance covered the water damage.
example.fr: L'assurance a couvert le dégât des eaux.

example.en: The building expert confirmed the cracks in the wall.
example.fr: L'expert en bâtiment a confirmé les fissures dans le mur.

example.en: A right-of-way easement crosses the neighboring garden.
example.fr: Une servitude de passage traverse le jardin voisin.

items.en: the party wall, the shared boundary wall

example.en: The party wall belongs to both properties.
example.fr: Le mur mitoyen appartient aux deux propriétés.

example.en: They're going to start renovation work in the spring.
example.fr: Ils vont engager des travaux dès le printemps.

example.en: Bringing the wiring up to code is mandatory before the sale.
example.fr: La mise en conformité électrique est obligatoire avant la vente.

items.en: to sign a preliminary sale agreement

items.fr: Les meubles que nous avons vendus étaient très anciens.
items.en: The furniture that we sold was very old.
items.ipa: /le mœbl kə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ vɑ̃.dy e.tɛ tʁɛ.z‿ɑ̃.sjɛ̃/
items.notes: "vendus" takes a plural "s" to agree with "les meubles", the direct object placed before "avons vendu".

items.fr: La maison qu'ils ont achetée avait besoin de travaux.
items.en: The house they bought needed renovation work.
items.ipa: /la mɛ.zɔ̃ kil.z‿ɔ̃ aʃ.te.te a.vɛ bə.zwɛ̃ də tʁa.vo/
items.notes: "achetée" adds a silent feminine "e" to agree with "la maison", the preceding direct object of "ont acheté".

items.fr: S'il avait plu, nous n'aurions pas repeint la façade.
items.en: If it had rained, we would not have repainted the facade.
items.ipa: /sil a.vɛ ply nu no.ʁjɔ̃ pa ʁə.pɛ̃ la fa.sad/
items.notes: "si" elides to "s'" only before "il" or "ils", never before other pronouns like "elle".

items.fr: Bien qu'elle soit propriétaire, elle loue quand même une chambre.
items.en: Even though she is an owner, she still rents out a room.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kɛl swa pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ ɛl lu kɑ̃ mɛm yn ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: "que" elides before "elle" to become "qu'elle", pronounced as one syllable.

items.fr: Les clés que le locataire nous a rendues étaient rouillées.
items.en: The keys that the tenant gave back to us were rusty.
items.ipa: /le kle kə lə lɔ.ka.tɛʁ nu.z‿a ʁɑ̃.dy e.tɛ ʁu.je/
items.notes: "rendues" agrees with the feminine plural "les clés", the direct object placed before the auxiliary "a rendu".

items.fr: Si j'avais su, je n'aurais jamais signé ce bail.
items.en: If I had known, I would never have signed this lease.
items.ipa: /si ʒa.vɛ sy ʒə no.ʁɛ ʒa.mɛ si.ɲe sə baj/
items.notes: "je" elides before the vowel of "avais" to form "j'avais", one of several elisions in this sentence.

items.fr: Il faudrait que le propriétaire fasse changer la chaudière.
items.en: The landlord would need to have the boiler changed.
items.ipa: /il fo.dʁɛ kə lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ fas ʃɑ̃.ʒe la ʃo.djɛʁ/
items.notes: "fasse" is the subjunctive form required after "il faudrait que", distinct from the indicative "fait" though both come from "faire".

items.fr: C'est le bruit des voisins du dessus qui l'empêche de dormir.
items.en: It is the noise from the upstairs neighbors that keeps him from sleeping.
items.ipa: /sɛ lə bʁɥi de vwa.zɛ̃ dy də.sy ki lɑ̃.pɛʃ də dɔʁ.miʁ/
items.notes: "le" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "empêche", merging into a single sound.

items.fr: Quoiqu'elle ait repeint tout le couloir, l'odeur de peinture persiste.
items.en: Although she repainted the whole hallway, the smell of paint lingers.
items.ipa: /kwa.kɛl ɛ ʁə.pɛ̃ tu lə ku.lwaʁ lo.dœʁ də pɛ̃.tyʁ pɛʁ.sist/
items.notes: "ait", the subjunctive of "avoir", sounds identical to "es", "est", and "ai" but is spelled differently.

items.fr: Les travaux que l'entreprise a entrepris coûtent plus cher que prévu.
items.en: The work that the company undertook costs more than expected.
items.ipa: /le tʁa.vo kə lɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz a ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁi kut ply ʃɛʁ kə pʁe.vy/
items.notes: "entrepris" stays unchanged for masculine plural agreement because the base form already ends in "s".

items.fr: Il aurait fallu qu'on repeigne la chambre avant l'arrivée du bébé.
items.en: The bedroom should have been repainted before the baby's arrival.
items.ipa: /il o.ʁɛ fa.ly kɔ̃ ʁə.pɛɲ la ʃɑ̃bʁ a.vɑ̃ la.ʁi.ve dy be.be/
items.notes: "que" elides before "on" to form "qu'on", and "repeigne" is the irregular subjunctive of "repeindre".

items.fr: La décoration qu'elle a choisie correspond parfaitement au salon.
items.en: The decor she chose matches the living room perfectly.
items.ipa: /la de.kɔ.ʁa.sjɔ̃ kɛl a ʃwa.zi kɔ.ʁɛs.pɔ̃ paʁ.fɛt.mɑ̃ o sa.lɔ̃/
items.notes: "choisie" adds a feminine "e" because the preceding direct object "que" refers to "la décoration".

items.fr: Quels que soient les travaux, le propriétaire doit être prévenu.
items.en: Whatever the work involved, the landlord must be informed.
items.ipa: /kɛl kə swa.t‿le tʁa.vo lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ dwa.t‿ɛtʁ pʁe.və.ny/
items.notes: "Quels que soient" requires the plural subjunctive "soient", agreeing with the plural "les travaux".

items.fr: Si nous avions loué un logement plus calme, nous aurions mieux dormi.
items.en: If we had rented a quieter place, we would have slept better.
items.ipa: /si nu.z‿a.vjɔ̃ lwe œ̃ lɔʒ.mɑ̃ ply kalm nu.z‿o.ʁjɔ̃ mjø dɔʁ.mi/
items.notes: Liaison links "nous avions" and "nous aurions" with /z/ sounds not shown by any letter of "nous".

The é is the reason the final vowel is said at all. A bare final e would be silent.
Two marks, two identical sounds. Nothing else in the word.
What you say when glasses touch.
Two different marks in four letters. Only the é changes a sound.
The é sounds, the final e after it does not.
Three é, three identical sounds. The mark is completely regular.
The è sounds and the s does not. One of the most common words you will say.
Both marks on an e, in one short word, making two different vowels.
Compare métro. One mark apart, and the vowel changes.
No mark. Say OO. Compare où, which sounds identical and means where.
The grave on a u changes no sound at all. It exists only to tell this word from ou.
The verb: il a, he has.
Identical sound to a. The mark is doing grammar, not sound.
A circumflex that changes nothing you can hear. It separates two words on the page.
No mark, and still /e/: the -es ending does the same job an é would.
Here the grave DOES change the sound: DAY becomes DEH.
Once feste. The s left and the mark took its place. English kept it: feast.
forest without its s. The English word still carries it.
hospital, minus the s. The trick works on most circumflexes.
The most common verb in French, and it opens on a marked vowel.
On an a the circumflex changes almost nothing a beginner needs to hear.
isle, without the s. The mark changes nothing you say.
Without the tréma, oe would fuse into one sound. The two dots force two syllables.
Compare mais, which is one syllable and means but. The dots are the whole difference.
One syllable. ai is a single sound here, which is exactly what maïs refuses.
English borrowed the word and kept the dots, then mostly stopped printing them.
Two marks doing two different jobs in one word: é makes a sound, ï splits one.
Without the tail, the c before a would be a K. The word would be frankay.
Two letters, and one of them is doing the work. Without the tail it would be KA.
Two marks side by side, each doing a different job.
c before a is a K. That is the default the cedilla exists to override.
c before e or i is already soft, so no cedilla is ever needed there.
Two words, two marks, two different jobs. This is the whole lesson in one phrase.
Feminine: grande. Opposite: petit. Un grand arbre, une grande maison.
Feminine: petite. Opposite: grand. Goes before the noun: un petit chat.
Feminine: bonne. Opposite: mauvais. Un bon film, une bonne idée.
Feminine: mauvaise. Opposite: bon. Un mauvais jour.
Feminine: belle. Becomes bel before a vowel: un bel homme.
Feminine: jolie. Softer than beau: une jolie robe.
Feminine: nouvelle. Becomes nouvel before a vowel: un nouvel ami. Opposite: vieux.
Feminine: vieille. Becomes vieil before a vowel: un vieil homme. Opposites: nouveau, jeune.
Same form for both genders. Opposite: vieux. Une jeune femme.
Feminine: courte. Opposite: long. The final t is silent in the masculine.
Feminine: grosse. Opposite: mince. Un gros chien.
Feminine: chaude. Opposite: froid. Un café chaud.
Feminine: froide. Opposite: chaud. De l'eau froide.
Same form for both genders. Opposite: difficile. C'est facile!
Same form for both genders. Opposite: facile. Un exercice difficile.
Feminine: ouverte. Opposite: fermé. Le magasin est ouvert.
Same form for both genders. Opposite: sale. Before the noun it means own: ma propre voiture.
Feminine: ancienne. Opposite: moderne. Before the noun it means former: mon ancien travail.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Before a noun it can mean unfortunate, le pauvre chat.
The feminine of vieux, and it is a different word rather than an added ending: vieille, never vieuxe. Ma grand-mère est vieille. Before a vowel the masculine is vieil.
The feminine of mauvais: add the e and the sleeping s wakes up as a z. Cette idée est mauvaise. The masculine plural is still mauvais, because the s is already there.
Beau becomes bel in front of a word starting with a vowel sound: un bel homme, un bel arbre. It sounds exactly like the feminine belle and it is used with the un kind of thing.
Vieux becomes vieil in front of a word starting with a vowel sound: un vieil ami, un vieil immeuble. It sounds exactly like the feminine vieille and it is used with the un kind of thing.

Feminine: verte, and you hear the final t: /vɛʁt/. The t is silent in the masculine.

Feminine: noire (same sound). Sounds like 'nwahr'.
Feminine: blanche /blɑ̃ʃ/. Masculine ends in a nasal vowel, the c is silent: 'blahn'.
Feminine: grise /ɡʁiz/. The s is silent in the masculine: 'gree'.
Same form for masculine and feminine. Also the noun for the flower: une rose.
Invariable as a color: des sacs orange, no extra ending. Named after the fruit, une orange.

Same form for masculine and feminine. Sounds like 'behzh', close to the English word.
The feminine of bleu, and it sounds exactly the same. Ma veste est bleue. The e is written and never heard, which is why learners refuse to believe the spelling.
The feminine of noir, and it sounds exactly the same. Ma veste est noire. Nothing in the sound tells you the e is there.
The feminine of gris. The silent s at the end of gris wakes up as a z: GREE becomes GREEZ. This one you can hear.
The feminine of violet. The silent t wakes up and the spelling doubles it: violet becomes violette, not violete.

The final l is pronounced: 'ah-vreel'. En avril = in April.

One syllable: 'yair'. The h is silent, as always in French.

items.notes: The S of les is silent alone. Before a vowel it comes back, and it comes back as a Z.
Every vous before a vowel does this. It is the most common liaison in French.
H muet is not there as far as the ear is concerned, so the N links straight across it.
The nasal vowel stays nasal AND an N appears. You do not lose the ohⁿ.
The T of est is silent in est alone. Here it links, and it stays a T.
The X of deux returns as a Z, exactly like an S would. This is the deux‿euros you were promised.
Same shape as vous avez. Pronoun, then a vowel, then a Z.
Without the Z this is ils on, which is not French. The link carries the meaning.
petit alone ends on the vowel. Put a noun starting with a vowel after it and the T wakes up.
Written with a D. Said with a T. A final D always links as T, never as D.
en always links. You will meet it in en avance, en été, en hiver.
A one-syllable preposition. These always link.
et NEVER links. Not once, not in any sentence, not in any register. It is the one rule here with no exception.
The T of et is silent forever. Compare est elle, which does link.
Every instinct you built in the last twenty minutes says link this. Do not.
H aspiré blocks the link. Compare les‿amis, where nothing blocks it. You cannot hear which H a word has: you learn it with the word.
Same block. The S of les stays silent and the two words stay apart.
en links everywhere else. Here the H aspiré of haut stops it, which is why this pair is worth banking.
Another h aspiré. The list is short and it is worth memorising as a list.
The blocked link is at the start. héros arrivent does not link either: a plural noun does not link to its verb.
Two gaps, two different answers. un links to enfant. enfant does NOT link to intelligent: a singular noun never links to the adjective after it.
Singular noun, then adjective. No link, even though the T is sitting right there.
Two links then a hard stop. This one sentence is the whole lesson: link, link, do not link.
onze behaves like an h aspiré word. So does un when it means the number one.
A proper noun does not link to what follows. Paris est stays apart, then est‿une links normally.
selon never links, unlike the short prepositions en, dans and chez, which always do.

turns.ai: Bonjour ! Vous désirez ?
turns.en: Hello! What would you like?
turns.user: Trois pommes, s'il vous plaît.

turns.ai: Voilà. Autre chose ?
turns.en: Here you go. Anything else?
turns.user: Non, merci. C'est combien ?

turns.ai: Deux euros cinquante.
turns.en: Two euros fifty.
turns.user: Voilà. Merci, au revoir !

turns.ai: Bonjour ! Les fraises sont en promotion aujourd'hui.
turns.en: The strawberries are on sale today.
turns.user: Elles viennent d'où, vos fraises ?

turns.ai: De Bretagne — cueillies ce matin. Une barquette ?
turns.en: From Brittany — picked this morning.
turns.user: J'en prends deux, et un kilo de tomates.

turns.ai: Et avec ceci ? Ça vous fait neuf euros vingt.
turns.en: Anything else? That's €9.20.
turns.user: C'est tout. Tenez, dix euros.

turns.ai: Bonjour, bienvenue. Voici l'appartement.
turns.en: Hello, welcome. Here's the apartment.
turns.user: Bonjour, merci de me recevoir.

turns.ai: Il y a deux chambres et une salle de bain.
turns.en: There are two bedrooms and one bathroom.
turns.user: Est-ce qu'il y a un balcon ?

turns.ai: Oui, il y a un petit balcon avec vue sur le jardin.
turns.en: Yes, there's a small balcony with a garden view.
turns.user: Le chauffage fonctionne bien ?

turns.ai: Oui, le chauffage est neuf et le loyer inclut l'eau chaude.
turns.en: Yes, the heating is new and the rent includes hot water.
turns.user: Parfait, je prends l'appartement.

turns.ai: Bonjour, comment puis-je vous aider aujourd'hui ?
turns.en: Hello, how can I help you today?
turns.user: Mon chien a mal à la patte.

turns.ai: Depuis quand a-t-il mal ?
turns.en: Since when has he been in pain?
turns.user: Depuis ce matin, il boite un peu.

turns.ai: Je vais examiner sa patte maintenant.
turns.en: I'm going to examine his paw now.
turns.user: D'accord, merci docteur.

turns.ai: Ce n'est pas grave, donnez-lui du repos pendant deux jours.
turns.en: It's nothing serious, give him rest for two days.
turns.user: Très bien, je vais faire ça.

turns.ai: Je dois me doucher tôt, je pars à huit heures.
turns.en: I need to shower early, I leave at eight.
turns.user: D'accord, mais je me réveille à sept heures aussi.

turns.ai: Tu peux utiliser la salle de bain après moi.
turns.en: You can use the bathroom after me.
turns.user: Parfait, je prends mon petit déjeuner en attendant.

turns.ai: Alors je me douche à sept heures et toi à sept heures vingt.
turns.en: So I shower at seven and you at seven twenty.
turns.user: Ça marche, je suis prête à huit heures.

turns.ai: Super, on se voit dans la cuisine à huit heures.
turns.en: Great, see you in the kitchen at eight.
turns.user: D'accord, à tout à l'heure !

turns.ai: Tu peux me passer le sel, s'il te plaît ?
turns.en: Can you pass me the salt, please?
turns.user: Voici le sel, tiens.

turns.ai: Merci, le riz est prêt, à ton avis ?
turns.en: Thanks, do you think the rice is ready?
turns.user: Pas encore, il faut deux minutes.

turns.ai: D'accord. Combien de poivre je mets dans la sauce ?
turns.en: Okay, how much pepper should I put in the sauce?
turns.user: Mets une petite cuillère de poivre.

turns.ai: Parfait, merci beaucoup pour ton aide !
turns.en: Perfect, thank you so much for your help!
turns.user: De rien, le repas va être délicieux.

turns.ai: Bonjour ! Tu as une question sur les devoirs ?
turns.en: Hello! Do you have a question about the homework?
turns.user: Oui, madame. Quels devoirs sont pour demain ?

turns.ai: Pour demain, tu dois lire le chapitre trois et faire l'exercice deux.
turns.en: For tomorrow, you need to read chapter three and do exercise two.
turns.user: D'accord, je note ça dans mon agenda.

turns.ai: Parfait. Et sais-tu quand est le prochain cours de français ?
turns.en: Great. And do you know when the next French class is?
turns.user: Non, je ne sais pas. Vous pouvez me le dire ?

turns.ai: Le prochain cours est mardi, juste après la récréation.
turns.en: The next class is Tuesday, right after recess.
turns.user: Merci, madame. Je fais mes devoirs ce soir.

turns.ai: Bonjour, je peux vous aider ?
turns.en: Hello, can I help you?
turns.user: Pardon, je cherche la station de métro.

turns.ai: Vous prenez la rue à droite, puis c'est tout droit.
turns.en: You take the street on the right, then it's straight ahead.
turns.user: Merci, c'est loin d'ici ?

turns.ai: Non, ce n'est pas loin.
turns.en: No, it's not far.
turns.user: Parfait, merci beaucoup !

turns.ai: Je vous en prie, bonne journée !
turns.en: You're welcome, have a good day!
turns.user: Au revoir !

turns.ai: Bonjour ! Quel est votre métier ?
turns.en: Hello! What's your job?
turns.user: Je suis ingénieur, je travaille dans une entreprise.

turns.ai: Ah, intéressant ! Vous aimez votre travail ?
turns.en: Oh, interesting! Do you like your job?
turns.user: Oui, beaucoup. Et vous, vous faites quoi ?

turns.ai: Je suis professeur. J'enseigne dans un collège.
turns.en: I'm a teacher. I teach at a middle school.
turns.user: C'est un beau métier ! Vous enseignez quelle matière ?

turns.ai: Le français. Je dois partir maintenant, ravi de vous avoir parlé !
turns.en: French. I have to go now, nice talking with you!
turns.user: Moi aussi, bonne soirée !

turns.ai: Bonjour, qu'est-ce qui ne va pas ?
turns.en: Hello, what seems to be wrong?
turns.user: J'ai mal à la gorge et au ventre.

turns.ai: Vous avez de la fièvre ?
turns.en: Do you have a fever?
turns.user: Non, mais j'ai mal à la tête aussi.

turns.ai: Vous devez boire beaucoup d'eau et vous reposer.
turns.en: You should drink plenty of water and rest.
turns.user: D'accord, merci docteur.

turns.ai: Revenez si ça ne va pas mieux dans deux jours.
turns.en: Come back if you are not feeling better in two days.
turns.user: Entendu, à bientôt.

turns.ai: Viens, je te présente ma famille !
turns.en: Come, let me introduce you to my family!
turns.user: D'accord, avec plaisir !

turns.ai: Voici mon père et ma mère.
turns.en: This is my father and my mother.
turns.user: Enchanté, madame et monsieur.

turns.ai: Et là, c'est ma sœur avec son mari.
turns.en: And over there, that's my sister with her husband.
turns.user: Elle a l'air très sympa.

turns.ai: Maintenant tu connais toute ma famille !
turns.en: Now you know my whole family!
turns.user: Merci de m'avoir tout présenté.

turns.ai: On fait du sport ce week-end ?
turns.en: Should we do a sport this weekend?
turns.user: Oui, j'aimerais bien jouer au tennis.

turns.ai: Super, tu es libre samedi matin ?
turns.en: Great, are you free Saturday morning?
turns.user: Oui, samedi matin, ça marche.

turns.ai: On se retrouve au stade à neuf heures ?
turns.en: Should we meet at the stadium at nine?
turns.user: D'accord, à neuf heures au stade.

turns.ai: Parfait, apporte ta raquette !
turns.en: Perfect, bring your racket!
turns.user: D'accord, à samedi !

turns.ai: Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Claire. Et vous, comment vous appelez-vous ?
turns.en: Hello! My name's Claire. And you, what's your name?
turns.user: Je m'appelle Marc.

turns.ai: Enchantée, Marc. Vous êtes d’où ?
turns.en: Nice to meet you, Marc. Where are you from?
turns.user: Je suis de Lyon.

turns.ai: Ah, j’adore Lyon ! Vous habitez ici maintenant ?
turns.en: Oh, I love Lyon! Do you live here now?
turns.user: Oui, depuis un an.

turns.ai: Quel âge avez-vous, si je peux demander ?
turns.en: How old are you, if I may ask?
turns.user: J’ai vingt-huit ans.

turns.ai: Et c’est quand, votre anniversaire ?
